And uh the nice thing I think about, you know, Ryan is not only is he an excellent punter, but he's probably the best holder in the draft, which is really important, uh as you guys all know. So excited to get him. Rashan Benny, um you know, we we've actually we've coached him, right? Lu Espazito and Jesse. Uh we like his his frame, his skill set. He's a guy that can play five-tech, three-tech, physical guy, long arms, really has a good five-tech body, which is tough to find. He's a strong run defender. Uh, and he fits us. He fits our mentality, and he knows our defense, and he's a he's a plug-and-play guy coming in right out of the gates. Now, last pick is Evan Bernstein. Uh, again, a guy that plays guard. He has played some center, not a lot. Uh, he's he's been playing college football for a long time. And uh he was at I think uh South Dakota and then Northwestern. Uh he's a guard primarily physical, tough, gritty type of Midwest, Big 10 type of offensive lineman. And at that point in the draft, he was by far the highest rated player for us and we think he's got a good chance to help us at some point. Questions? So Eric, when you're when Steve's making that, why did you select that that fifth round as the the one that you know, was there any kind of any backstory to why that was the the the point in the draft that he was going to take one? >> I think he just he probably uh coerced me with a nice bottle of wine down there in Florida and we had all those picks. We knew we were going to have all those picks and so we just decided on that that last pick in the fifth round. Um, obviously maybe your best offseason departure is Kevin Linder Balm. Um, no obvious center in this draft, although I guess, you know, Evan might convert. Um, what was your overall take on this center class available in this draft and ultimately, you know, you even traded back into the fourth round uh when there were some available. Why did do you think it wasn't in your best interest to take one? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's a good question. Um, so there were a couple centers that we really liked. Um, the guys that went in the second round. And I think after that, you know, could we have traded up, you know, potentially maybe traded up into the second round and maybe take one of those guys? And we we really assessed it like where we were picking at 80 for us to do that would have cost our second round pick, our third round pick and our fourth round pick points wise to do that. Um, but know third round, fourth round, fifth round, whatever you're going to say pointswise to do it. probably prohibitive for us to get up that high in the draft. And so, you know, um would I rather have Jacobe, uh Serat, and uh and and and Hibner? I probably would than one player at that point. So, it was impossible for us to really get back up into the second round unless we gave up a first round pick next year, maybe potentially. Um, you know, there were some other centers, but there was nobody that we looked at that we thought necessarily like this guy's going to come in here and, you know, I'm not good players, but there's nobody that's going to necessarily be an impact player for us this year. Um, I do think we'll have a plan um at the position. Feel confident in saying that. And I think we have a couple guys here that will compete for that position. But um as the uh a hall of fame general manager once said um you don't play games till September and I think we'll have a great offensive line at that point. We have a plan. Uh it didn't necessarily fall our way this weekend, but it's still early and I'm thrilled with what we'll be able to accomplish. Derek, were you surprised that the two guys win as early as they did? Those first two centers. >> I was uh I was a little surprised. Um I would probably attribute that to the run on offensive linemen in the first and second round and that trickle down effect. Um because uh you know, you saw those tackles and guards go um you know that's what happens. I I think you see it you saw it in a different way this year with receiver and tight ends. And so again, you saw these receivers get picked and then you saw a huge run on tight ends. Um these teams have to adjust quickly on the fly. So, um I think actually one of the one of the centers that was drafted got turned in as a guard. Um just because all those guards got picked and so now as a team you're trying to look at it and go, "Oh man, how are we going to fill this guard position? Well, let's take this center. He can probably play guard." So it's hard. It's challenging. Um, a lot of times when you find yourself in a position like that, and we've been in this many years, is it's just the pick that you have, the number that you have, um, and not just being able to maneuver, uh, the right way or not not having the ammunition, um, or maybe the the cost of doing so is probably prohibitive. So, unfortunate, but I'm ecstatic with the players that we're able to get. And um honestly like looking at this list of players, I probably wouldn't do anything differently. >> For for you or for Jesse, what what is your guys plan now with Emry? Is someone Is he someone who you're still looking at at guard or a tackle or is he someone who could even potentially have a shot at center? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, coming out, he was a right tackle and he's a damn good right tackle. Um we think he's going to be a damn good guard, too. um coming off the injury. We think he's a talented guy, great mentality, great makeup. Um and you know, he's going to compete. He'll compete to start and we're going to have great depth and we're going to have a great six-man. I don't know who that sixman's going to be, but whoever it is, if you come out of it in with this group, you're going to be really talented. You're going to be really good. So, I like the depth that we have right now. We still have some moves to make. I think we're in a much better place than we have been. Um, and I'm excited to see what happens. >> Jesse, I know you were kind of non-committal in terms of venue where he would play, but I mean, does he have that? I knew he played a little bit of center. That's something you guys would even look at. >> Yeah, I think we'll start off thinking more of a guard, but I think there's always I I really think coach Leadford does a great job. Um, highly confident that we'll be able to put a great O line together. I do think there will be a there's the thought of how do you get your best five guys on the field, you know, no different than a guy like secondary or, you know, linebackers. It's like how do you how do you get the best players that can help you win onto the field and so I think that's the great part about the offseason getting a chance to work with these guys. It's a it's a good time sometimes to experiment with with people like that and see what see the versatility that guys have. Uh and then again come September, you know, figure out figure out where where everybody fits best, where they can best thrive and succeed and uh help us have the best O line. >> Jesse, um Eric mentioned yesterday three guys. I mean, Z Pinter, Vaughn, and um >> are those the three guys you talked about? >> Yeah, those three guys for sure. I think uh we feel good about those guys competing. Um, and then again, just like all the guys, all the interior, all the offensive linemen, having that ability to potentially, you know, showcase some versatility and play different spots and and us figure out the best five, the best six, the best seven, the best eight, you know, that'll be a major work in progress between now and September. >> Jesse, when you sort of step back and look at the 11 guys you drafted over the last three days, do you see any sort of theme that runs through the entire class? um you know, tough, physical, you know, a lot of those these guys are big physical players. Um when you look at when you look at the O line, obviously you start with Venga and just like him setting the tone for the draft class. Um dominant line of scrimmage and so think we added, you know, the best interior interior offensive lineman in the draft. Um Zion again, big physical, tough, rugged player. Jacobe, big matchup guy. Size, speed, length, catch radius, ability to make tough plays. Um, I mean, Srod as well, like that was a really cool opportunity to double dip at that position. The way the board fell and taking the best guy, a guy that's had a ton of production in major impact games the last two years at Indiana. And then I I think when guys are really productive wherever they're playing, you know, he played a year at a JMU, he played a year at even a smaller school before that. A super productive player. U Hibner, you know, I mean, I've seen this guy in some really bloody physical nine on sevens, you know, two, three, four years ago. Um being a really physical blocker, even maybe more so than showed up in and what they were asking him to do at SMU. Uh again, excited about him. Uh, but all the guys, I mean, you you can go all the way down the list. Even Chandler Rivers, not as big in in stature, but plays with a really cool mindset. Love the way that guy plays football. Attacks the ball, plays really physical. He's a good tackler for his size. Um, so I just think you go all the way down the list. Um, it's a really physical group. Big, big, strong, tough, physical team that we're trying to trying to have here. And all these guys fit that bill. Jesse, um it's been probably a blur these couple months of everything you've had on your plate. What was this experience like in your new role with all the first you're experiencing? And what's kind of a general takeaway for you just being part of your first draft as a head coach? >> Yeah, it was incredible. Uh you know, this is the this is the obviously we talked about this all the way back, but like this is the job I wanted because the people here and how they operate and Eric does an amazing job. Uh you got Azie Newsome sitting in there. You got Steve Bashadotti. Just people that are unbelievable. Uh you know, people first and then they they can just manage situations. They got a great mind for what's happening throughout the draft. They've done a great job of bringing the coaches in. And I feel like everybody on the staff really felt value and felt input into how we ended up with these players, you know, which I think is a cool quality to have to to make to bring people in and make it make it collaborative. Um, but at the end of the day, man, it's just a cool, really cool situation to kind of see the team come together. Um, you know, when you go into it, there's, I think, you know, 50 so players on our team and you add 11 and then obviously we'll add more the rest of the day. It'll be really exciting when we look out there and there's uh 90 guys on the roster. >> What was there a position that Eric kind of tasked you with evaluating specific prospect class? >> You know, it was really cool. I I've always taken really a lot of pride as an evaluator. Um it was it was honestly really neat and fun to to do a lot of different positions um over the time and so first time really evaluating like offensive linemen and wide receivers in a way in a different way than just preparing to play against them. Um, you know, and and and to me, like the things that jump out as a as a defensive history coach, I would say, you know, the play style and how these guys play and just like the down after down mindset that they play with when you're looking at offensive players really jumps off the tape with all these guys. Their ability to make tough, especially like the the playmakers, the skilled players, their ability to make tough plays, contested plays, key plays on the field in the red area. both these guys, both these wide receivers, huge red zone uh targets. So, just fun to evaluate all the different positions and look at different things. Um, and then certainly, you know, the secondary has probably always been a knack of mine to try to get some of those guys. >> Eric, uh, obviously you have very detailed records of of all these guys and their various idiosyncrasies, but, you know, you look at your two receivers in in Jacobe and Elijah and then your two tight ends. Um, you know, very sort of similar on the surface profiles for each of those positions. I mean, high point, you know, tall receivers and tight ends or maybe sort of tweener types who have blocking ability and then some, you know, pass catching. >> Are there ways in which those guys sort of diverge from each other or is the overlap some of the point and why you decided to draft them? Yeah, I think the the biggest thing I think is just that we they're they're versatile players that do some really good things. Um they're not exactly the same. You know, our vision for Jacobe is probably a little bit different than maybe the vision for Sarat. They're going to compete for playing time, right? They both catch the ball really well. They're both big. Um but they're not exactly identical. I think u you know Matt and Josh um they're a little different. They're a little different how they're used and the offense is different, but I love the fact that they're both versatile players who can do different things. And in our offense, not to not to give a lot away, and I don't even understand our offense yet to be honest, but I know that versatility and flexibility and being able to do a lot of different things is really important. Being smart, being adaptable, um is really, really important. The idea of deception and all these things and just flexibility to play multiple roles, I think, is really a plus. And so, um, you know, and then just being able to handle the physical aspect of the game, being tough, being tough minded, being able to handle adversity, um, you know, uh, again, like I talked a little bit yesterday about this, but I had a bunch of other players reach out to me today um about some of these guys and just they know their stories and I think these guys were made, you know, of the right stuff, most of these guys and I want to thank for that. I just think it's opportunity for me to thank the scouts specifically um the area guys and then also um couple unheralded guys um Steve Claget and Derek Yam as well. They do a lot of work on the draft in different ways um George and Mark and all those guys and and Nick. But we get great information on how these guys kind of who they are as people, background, motivations, drivers and all those different things. and the scouts and and those guys upstairs, they're really the guys that are able to kind of put that all together for me to help me make the decisions. And so without that, this process would be much more complicated and probably not as not as accurate. So >> sort of on the topic of versatility, um you know, Declan comes from the Shawn Payeyton school and Shawn's offense. Think of Taesm Hill as sort of a do it all jack knife type guy. I think you use the word jack knife when describing Adam. um you know as a receiver turned running back. I mean is there sort of a Joker jack knife role or that he could kind of be in the running for that's new to this offense? >> Well I think that remains to be seen but I will say he's very smart. He's big. He's athletic. He catches the ball well. He runs good routes. He's physical. He's a physical runner. He's played special teams. He can return kicks. So his value it does get it does get magnified. And I think uh not not to speak for coach, but one of the hardest things to do is is come up with a 48man roster and uh if you have guys who can do multiple things, it really makes your job a lot easier because now you can you can you can create roles for other people because you might have a player who can do more than just one thing. So if you can run routes, run the ball, pass, protect, and return kicks, now your value really skyrockets. Eric, I know you were uh dialed in to the whole draft, but did you get a chuckle out of watching uh Mark Ingram's son or the lady from uh the UK? >> We did. We laughed. We saw that, you know. Um yeah, it was it was great. I mean, Mark, you know, he's I think someone said it, but you know, you'd think that Mark spent his whole career with us. He's only with us two years, but they were memorable years and that 19 season especially, he's got a special place in my heart and I think of him as a as a real original Raven, even though obviously he played more more years in New Orleans. And so guy that I really respect, I love his passion. I thought was really funny. Um, and you know, certainly I think the uh back and forth between, you know, Pittsburgh and Baltimore, we we saw that this weekend, right? And I think that's is kind of actually a special thing, right? It's kind of fun that we have that type of rivalry that's like celebrated across the country. Everybody understands like what it's like Red Sox, Yankees, you know. Um, everybody understands it and kind of celebrates it. I think it's one of the things that makes sports special. >> How's the scouting process compared to find equally this year after you're looking for a kicker last year in the pre-draft? >> Oh man. Well, I don't get involved in that too much, you know. Um, and I'm not I don't want to, you know, I don't want to create a monster, but he's already been created, you know, he's already been created. Uh, but Randy does a phenomenal job. He does. And so, um, it's probably the one the two positions that if Randy comes to me and says, "This is the guy that we need," I'm going to accept it. Normally I'd be like a little skeptical and I want to watch the tape and do my homework and put my eyes on the guy, but when Randy does this and says, "Yeah, this is the best one." Then that resonates and um you know, I think our track record with kickers and pawners is pretty good. Long snappers is pretty good. Um so it's not something I'm going to mess with. So, um, now I might fight with him as to when we have to draft the guy or what round, but as far as like being the best at ranking, I think he's the best at that. >> Do you look at Monday, I guess Monday at 4 after that, um, free agent signings no longer counter the comp formula. You're fond of saying that building a roster is sort of an everyday thing year round. Do you view this almost as another phase of free agency for this team? We do. Um yeah, I mean, you know, we don't have any agreements that would be illegal, of course. Um but there's always there always players out there that you can go after that you'll try to talk to at some point. And as you the draft is really, you know, you kind of you you go through this process and now you know what the roster looks like. So now it's easy next week to go out and say, "Okay, we need this, we might need this, we might need this." Um, so I think with free agency, potentially trades, um, terminated players, you know, we still June 1st still at risk for players to be terminated. There were opportunity for us to sign a few guys. And as you guys know, like even I remember, you know, I think uh I don't know what year that was, but 2021, maybe 22, I was at driving up to Penn State with my daughter and we signed uh I negotiated the contract for Javian Clowney in the car. That was in August. So I think it was in August, right? It was in August. Yeah. So those things can happen, right? And so again, it's like we try to be patient, not be uh too reactive to things, not overreact, just to be patient, and we'll see what happens. Let good players fall to us. There's going to be opportunities coming along, and we'll be ready to pounce. Jesse, >> how have you seen Raan Benny progress both when you were with him in Michigan and since then? >> Yeah, Ray's a u tough, rugged, physical defensive lineman that's got some real athleticism. I think there's some real upside there with him and some pass rush ability. Uh he got thought in 2023 he was our third or fourth type defensive lineman. We had Mason and Kenneth Grant and Chris Jenkins and we had obviously a pretty loaded group. Um but he made some really key plays for us in that season. He got hurt in the Rose Bowl that year. Um and it I know it affected him. I was gone after that. But I thought this year he really bounced back after kind of battling through the injury in 2024. Showed some really good stuff. does a lot of things on tape that that obviously we like to see. Um, and so I think he's just kind of a guy that's gotten better and better. He was really really raw and kind of a young player coming into Michigan. Um, but uh those guys there, you know, I know he's been well trained and and well coached and uh excited to add Ray. >> Jesse, we didn't get a chance to ask you about your voluntary mini camp you were able to have this past week. what stood out about that in terms of you know guys attendance and just what did you learn about your football team getting to have most of them together for the first time? >> Yeah, I mean it was unbelievable turnout. Uh we had a great three days together. I think we learned a lot about each other just kind of how we're operating on the practice field. some of the things that we're doing. We didn't do a ton of full speed team work in that just from a health and safety standpoint of where we're at in the offseason program, but the guys had a real opportunity to kind of see where they're at learning the learning new schemes on both sides of the ball. Um, and so it was it was incredible. It was a lot of fun. Um, it was cool to see the coaches out there coaching these guys up. We kind of knew it kind of gives you a especially going into the draft, it gives you a little bit of sense at different positions and kind of where you're at. Um, and so it's a it's a great rule. I do I do love that for new staffs to be able to have that opportunity. And uh now we go right back into phase two and uh continue to try to get better. >> Eric, um since we're not actually talk to you until September now, uh any anything you can tell us about uh progress with Lamar and contract talks? >> No, not really. Okay. Thank you.

title: Eric DeCosta, Jesse Minter Night 2 Press Conference| Baltimore Ravens
text: Long day, but a solid successful day. Um, a lot of moving parts with uh, Venga coming in late and we think we did a good job getting them here across the country. And as far as the, uh, draft goes, you know, I think it it fell nicely for us. Uh, Zion Young, uh, a big, physical, tough, really good both run and pass defender who we had a chance to see this year at the Senior Bowl in person. Talked to several times. He was here in Baltimore a couple weeks ago. Really fits what we want to be on defense. And uh and Jacobe Lane's another guy uh that came into Baltimore uh recently, I think within the last 10 days. Uh really, really impressive kid to talk with. Um you know, large catch radius, phenomenal hands, big receiver, uh tested really well at the combine. Uh just a a kind of player that we haven't had lately here. I think he offers a different dynamic. Um, I, you know, I think you guys probably know, uh, he was mentored, uh, by Todd Heap, who, uh, we, we've talked to, I think Todd's son was Jacob's quarterback, which is kind of a cool story. And, uh, had the chance to get Todd in my office with Jacobe on a Zoom as he was getting on a plane to come back to Baltimore for the uh, jersey uh, unveiling. So, that was kind of cool. So, anyways, it was a good day. Hey, we addressed some I think some some significant needs that we had and we're excited that we've got eight picks coming up uh tomorrow. Questions? >> Yeah, Eric, you did mention with with Todd. I mean, how much because again you I know you take input everywhere you can get it, but how much does you know getting a guy that's known one of your prospects since he was like 13 years old? How much does that impact kind of your decision-m? Well, you know, so I didn't I wasn't aware of the relationship uh initially and when Jacobe told me and he said, "Let me get him on the phone and I was a little skeptical that Todd, we said, "Let me FaceTime." I was a little skeptical that Todd might pick up. Um I thought it was a good litmus test and he picked up right away and they started talking and he said, "Guess where I am." And he showed uh the the screen to to me and Todd saw me and Todd said, "I'm ironically at the airport coming to Baltimore." And so, um, we talked after that that for a while and it was great. And that does carry weight. These guys kind of know the fabric of this place and the culture that we have here and what's been established. And guys like Todd were a big part of that. And so when uh when players reach out, it means a lot. And I've had a couple other players reach out um tonight about the picks, a couple guys that know some of our guys. And that that does carry weight because those guys have played here. And you know, we know that um all those guys want to see the Ravens, the legends, they want to see us do well. So when they endorse a player that carries a lot of weight, [clears throat] >> it seemed like there was a lot of reporting about how many of the bigger wide receivers that were in this draft um had visited with you guys during the pre-draft process. >> Um was that just a coincidence or did you kind of go into this draft wanting to make a commitment to finding like the ex receiver that I know you talked about kind of wanting >> Mar? Um, I think that's, you know, Jonas by design to a degree. You know, we're trying to find different type of players, right? You don't want to have all big guys, all small guys, right? All guys that play inside, all guys that can play outside. So, the idea would be to really build out a room that's versatile and can do different things. and uh Coach Doyle, I think um and uh and Carrie Colbert, those guys did a phenomenal job of evaluating players this year and really presenting their vision for what these guys could be and and how those guys would fit and how those guys would help us. And uh I know that as the person that has to make the ultimate decision, that's really really helpful to get their input um to kind of get a sense for how they're going to fit and what they think they can become. And uh you know, Jacobe was a player that I think our coaches were excited about. Our scouts really liked and we just think that he's a ball of clay with a lot of upside who has unique catching ability and unique size. Uh then I think that our, you know, I think Lamar's going to like throwing the ball to him and I think he's got a chance to really make an impact on this team at some point. Do you think, you know, just kind of watching Lamar develop over his eight years here, you know, he's typically been a guy who's been able to find the open guy that can get to him pretty quickly. Uh, not a lot of like jump balls that you see, you know, some other quarterbacks throw. Is that kind of a realm of his game that you are excited to maybe open up to him with someone of Jacob's size and speed? >> Yeah, well, I mean, I think listen, uh, this guy's proven. I mean, just watch his catches. He's 6'4, over 205 lbs. He jumps 40 in, right? That's that's not many guys can do that unless they're playing, you know, in the NBA. Um, he's got great ball skills, huge hands, and uh, you know, I think any quarterback would like throwing a ball to a guy like him. I think Lamar is going to be excited when he sees him. And, uh, and I think I think Jacobe is going to earn the trust of Lamar, and he's he's going to be a player that can be counted on to make to make big plays. Jesse, what what excites you most about Zion and the traits that he's bringing in. What kind of separates him from some of the other edge rushers that you have already? >> Yeah, Zion is a rugged, tough, physical player. Uh, I think he's just scratching the surface. What he can be as a player. I think there's a ton of upside there. Love his play style. He plays extremely hard, plays extremely physical. um you know is very powerful in the run game, meaning like when he strikes blocks, they go the other way. When people pull on him and he strikes him, it's a it's a train wreck. Uh he's also proven to be I thought he made major improvements this year as a pass rusher. Something he took a lot of pride in this year improving in that area. I do think he has ability to rush up and down the line. So he's got some versatility there, particularly as you get into third down and you want to put different guys in different spots. Um, you know, you want to have different different types of rushers. And you look at that room now, that's a really versatile room that I'm I couldn't be more excited about. Uh, same thing with the receiver room. When you talk about Jacobe, you want guys that have different traits, different types of matchups. Uh, look at the DB room, the receiver room. You want you just want different different types of guys. You don't want everybody to be the same. Um, and so when you look at look at the guys we picked up, they fit what we're trying to do. Jesse, in the past, some of the better Ravens teams have just been really big, like big guys everywhere. That was something Daniel Jeremiah was saying at the combine that when they're at their best, they're big everywhere. You get Venga first round, big Z Young obviously big, and then you get a big receiver. Has that been not just a receiver, but just overall across the board, has that been a trend getting a little bigger and more physical throughout the roster? >> Yeah, it's a great question. Um, you know, I do think certain positions like size, uh, the traits that you're looking for when you do look at the history of this place and the teams that have been really good and especially on the defensive side of the ball, you know, when you look at the edge guys that have really thrived here, um, guys like that have have been really good. Uh, certainly on the offensive line, you know, you're looking for a combination of size and athleticism, uh, which we which we definitely think Vena has. And then as Eric mentioned, just getting a different type of target, you know, for Lamar, a big a big guy, a big X-T type receiver. When you watch this guy in the red zone make catches, you know, that's a that's a vision that our coaches were like, man, we could really, you know, take advantage of that. So, um, you know, I think you're always looking for the best players. Often times, I do think size, you know, is a requisite to be a really good player. So, uh, we're definitely always looking for the best available. Jesse, when you think just like how how rushers play the NFL, you know, last year obviously you had Tulie who doesn't have great first, but he still was a double digit sack guy and able to condense that pocket. Just what do you think about that particular skill set plays in the modern NFL? >> Yeah, these there's a lot of quarterback there's so many different types of quarterbacks right now, but I would say that one of the things that's just showing up over and over again is these guys' ability to extend plays and get out of the pocket. And so you want to have a combination of guys that can that can win one-on-one that you can give them some freedom and then you want the guys that can really constrict everything and keep them in the pocket. And so I think we have a really good blend now. Uh you got guys that can rush inside and cover for some of the guys outside that can do those different types of things. Uh some of the stuff we had success with the with the three or four edges that we had last year in LA. So again, love the look of that room. Love what we've done to that room, you know, in the last couple months. um and excited to get those guys out there and get ready to work. >> Eric, what is um is not taking a center to this point an indication that you like your internal options or just you feel good about the depth in the center class and you feel like you get one on day three? >> Well, you can't make them up, right? I mean, you can't just create a center, Jeff, out of the sky and say, "Oh, let's take this guy." So, you know, the board has to fall a certain way. Um we do have some guys we like on the third day that we think are interesting players. Um, couple guys got picked, right? A couple good players. Um, but there's more available. Um, we do have centers on the roster. I think we got three centers on the roster right now. So, there is going to be a competition. Hopefully, I think we'll have the chance to get some good players tomorrow. Um, if if the center ends up being the highest rated guy and we're on the clock, then that'll be the pick. If he's not, then that probably won't be the pick. But, um, yeah, I mean, it's something that, uh, you go into the draft with a lot of different needs. Um, we've only had three picks, so it's kind of hard for us to fill every single need with three picks. Uh, I think tomorrow's a new day. We're excited about it. I think, uh, tomorrow's, we always call it the scouts day because, um, we got opportunities to kind of go after some of those guys maybe that are under the radar. Um, I thought last year we did a good job with some of those guys that we took um, in the third day and I'm confident that we'll do the same thing again tomorrow. >> Eric, along the same lines, there was a bit of a run on tight ends today. Um, what do what do you like about maybe what's left there tomorrow? >> Yeah, so they come in all different shapes and sizes. You know, you got your guys that can move a little bit, your Hback types, you got your Y's, you got your Fs. Um, we are fortunate we have two, you know, two tight ends on the roster right now that we feel really good about. Um, definitely would expect us to probably draft a tight end tomorrow at some point with eight picks. You think that we'll have a chance to at least add one or two guys. Uh there certainly was a run today. Um you know, it's like uh it's a it's a it's a blessing and a curse when you're at 45 and uh you don't pick again till 80. Uh you get a guy that you have at 45, you have them as a as a first round type of player and then you see all these tight ends get picked between 45 and 80. So it's challenging, right? Um, but I think we did get a playmaker on offense and Jacobe that we're really really excited about who brings something different to the table and I think our challenge tomorrow will be able to go after other players that we think bring something unique to the table for us. >> You mentioned that you heard from other players about some of your picks. Did you talk to Nate Wiggins before the draft about Zion and and have you heard from him since? >> Uh, so I had didn't really talk to Nate before the draft about Zion. spoke a little bit about Clemson guys. Um I wasn't even aware of the connection between Zion and Nate, but I did hear certainly hear from Nate after um after the pick. I got a a barrage of text messages and he's super excited. So um it's great when you get that excitement from your players um about players that you're bringing in or you know, as I said, legends of the you know, who played here that are excited about our players and our picks. Um, it's just I think speaks to, you know, in some ways the culture that we have here that, you know, players that played here feel comfortable reaching out to us to tell us that they think it's a good pick or a bad pick maybe, but the fact that they that line of communication is open, I think is special. >> Eric, are you guys in as far as is Zion in kind of wait and see mode with that pending DWI charge? Have you gotten any info on on where that stands? Uh yeah, I mean we we think we do a good job uh getting information um and uh I think we're comfortable with it. So that's what I would say about that. Okay, thanks guys. >> Thanks guys.

title: GM Monti Ossenfort And HC Mike LaFleur Address The Media After Day 2 Of NFL Draft | AZ Cardinals
text: Uh, all right. Thanks for uh thanks for sticking with us tonight. Um, you know, exciting night for us. Um, we're excited. We very excited to add Jeremiah. Um, you know, happened happened quick there. We had to wait for two picks and uh we're excited to to call him and and let him know that he'd be joining us. Just um excited about the player, excited about the person, um you know, excited about what he's going to add to our team. So, um with that, I'll shoot it to you guys. He said you guys had a conversation last week and it went really well that you know it was just you guys hit it off right away. What was it about the dynamic that you think worked so well and >> I mean he's he's I mean you guys will get a chance to meet him tomorrow. Um he's just an impressive kid. Uh mature. Um has his head on his shoulders never gets too high, never gets too low. Um you know we had a great interaction with him at the combine. um you know, I followed up with him with a uh with a call over the weekend and um yeah, just had a had a great overall interaction. So, you know, like I said, you guys will get a chance to meet him. Impressive kid. Um you know, just really excited to add the person to our locker room. >> We don't know a ton about your offense yet, but what his how does he fit? How does his skill set fit into what you envision yourself doing? Yeah, I mean like I I've said this with running backs, you know, um they do come in all shapes and sizes. What's what's unique about him in my opinion is in all three phases. And what I mean by all three phases, the run game, the pass game, and protection, you know, he's he has the ability to to, you know, mix it in in all those, you know. So, you guys see all the explosive stuff. I mean, that that's all there, you know, but uh you know, he didn't have that weakness in my opinion in any of those phases. So, you can put him in those situations. You know, he's got to learn this game. He's got to learn the NFL. He's got to learn the speed of it. I mean, there's a lot still that that uh needs to be uh learned in practice and all that, but uh he definitely has the tools to get there. >> Monte, obviously uh when you're picking that high in the draft, there's a lot of conversation about premium positions and running back. How did you measure that or was it just a question of Jeremiah being that much better than everybody else? >> Yeah, I think Darren with that, you know, we're we're evaluating each each player, each position. We're stacking our board. Um, you know, when we're picking that high, the the goal is to add an impact player and um, you know, there were there were certainly other players that we talked about. Um, you know, we did we talked about the position. Uh, understand all that. In the end, we we felt we added the guy that could impact our team the most. Um, and just really excited about the versatility that he brings to the offense. it it's obviously generally easier and and cheaper to find running backs through other means, especially free agency, than it is offensive tackles and rushers. I guess like how much did that play into your thinking and and what made you willing to overlook um kind of that element of of um I guess scarcity at different positions? Um, I mean really tail, I mean I think with every decision that we make, we uh in the draft we take the best player that we think is available when we pick and we did that tonight. That'll always be the case. Um, and that's that will always be the case as as long as I'm here. I know that's what Mike believes in. It's what I believe in and that's what we did. >> How do you see the running back room sorting itself out being a little bit crowded now? >> Yeah, it is. It's a it's a good room. There's no question. and it's a good room and I think with with as with anything else the the competition will take care of itself. Um you know so that'll be for Mike and his staff to to sort out but you know it's a it's a good problem to have. >> The two picks ahead of you kind of went a little bit quick just in terms of the clock getting down. You guys obviously kind of went down to the final minute. Could you just talk through maybe the the trade conversations that you had? Did you guys come close to moving out of the pick? Like how did those go? >> Yeah, Donnie you want if you want me to tell you the honest god truth. we had the wrong phone number to uh the the the phone number that we were given was the wrong one and so that was a little bit of the delay. So we got that straightened out and we called Jeremiah and we got a hold of him. That's that's what the delay was. Um >> there was no delay. >> There was no delay. Yeah. Um technical difficulties. Um you know there was a very minimal conversations Donnie. There was you know some surface level but but nothing that came anywhere close to to getting us to move off the pick. Did you have any conversations about moving back into the first round 34 there? >> Yeah, we did. We did late in the draft. Um, you know, we kicked it around. Um, you know, I think I told you guys the other day, you start um you start counting the number of players that you would pick. Um, you know, and you look at it and you look at there was a number of teams that were looking, you guys saw there was a lot of movement there at the end of the first round. Um, so yeah, we had we had some conversations. Um, but, you know, it just didn't work out for us to move up. So, you know, tomorrow, uh, I think San Francisco ended up at pick 33, so, you know, they'll pick and then we're there at 34. >> Jeremiah Jeremiah said, um, that you guys were very authentic with him, very kind-hearted. Just did you get that same feel with him just immediately talking to him? >> He's just a real dude. He's a very, uh, easy guy to talk to. He's very mature. Um, like he said, he's got his head on on straight, you know, and he's about the right stuff. um comes from a great family. I think his story is awesome. Uh but but above all, right right like it's just like right when he walked in, you knew you had a man in there, you know, and uh he loves it. He's smart. He's tough. He's got all those those attributes, but uh he's going to be a good teammate for these guys. >> Obviously, when you're picking at three, there's not a ton of scenarios, right? So, at what point in the process did you kind of land on the idea that Jeremiah would would very likely be your guy at three? Yeah, I mean I think I think we came to a pretty solid conclusion of what where we were going, what we were doing at the start of this week. >> What did uh Jeremiah's father tell you about the guy you were considering drafting? I already had some nice things to say to both of you. >> Uh yeah, I don't know that. Yeah, I'm not sure we either of us spoke to his father. So >> absolutely. >> Yeah. Lonnie, with uh obviously you're you're looking at scenarios, but but there was a lot of time between after your pick and kind of watching how everything plays out. As you're going through that, are you guys just honed in on the round itself? Are you guys already starting to kind of look ahead and see what might be there in second round, etc., etc.? >> Yeah, I mean, I think I think, you know, there was a long time to wait there, Darren. And I think um you know there was 15 16 picks and and you know you just kind of sit there and wait. Um you know I think we had a uh we had a pretty good idea of what might make it till the end of the first round and who what guys we might be considering and then you know we tried to in our mock draft exercises we tried to uh go all the way out to 34 and and see what might be left. Um but really until it until it got to a point I mean call it 23 24 25 um you know really didn't have any discussions about you know you're just you're forced to wait and see what's left there. So that happened around I'd say pick 24 25 and then but nothing came of it and so we'll be we'll we sat where we're at. We'll see what happens tomorrow night. You guys talked last week about taking players based off not only where they are, but maybe where they can be in terms of becoming like an NFL player. A lot of times like top five picks are expected to be these franchise defining guys and game changers and stuff like that. And he's still a rookie obviously, but like where do you guys think Jeremiah can be as an NFL player? >> I think he can be I think he can help us in multiple ways. Mike mentioned um as a runner, as a receiver, in pass protection. Um, but you know, really like at this point his his job is to come in here, uh, meet his teammates, learn the system, um, you know, meet his coaches, uh, figure out just how we run things here and and really that's our expectation for for him right now. >> How many mocks do you guys run through and how accurate are they done with the first? >> Um, yeah, it's a great question. Um, we do we do an exercise on every year on I think we've done it on Monday or Tuesday. um where we we utilize our pro scouts. Um those pro scouts during the season, they have uh seven or eight teams that they're they're involved with. Um and then we just go through the draft and they they pick players according to um you know, media reports. They pick players based on what they know of the draft. Um, and we just we go through and then there's there's scenarios where we'll we'll do one, hey, do this one, you know, straight straight down the fairway and then we do another one. Hey, get a little wild with this one cuz I mean, as we saw tonight, there's things that maybe we didn't anticipate happening. So, that's the truth with every draft. And, you know, we we never get it 100% right, but it's it's a fun exercise to do and and to just see what might be there. with this decision-making process. Was ownership involved in this process in this decision at all? >> Uh in the decision? No. No, not at all. Um you know, Michael um Michael is involved to the point of uh he likes to know what's going on. He loves to hear about our process. He loves to hear about um how we have arrived at um at the board where it's at. Um you know, he's he's great at throwing us scenario. Well, what if this guy goes, "Okay, well then we would do this." So, uh, Michael's been great. He was awesome with letting Mike and I go through our process. Um, and he was he was engaged as always, but really hands off and let us do our job. >> Uh, with Jacobe reportedly asking for the raise, how might that impact everything moving forward through the draft and where do you guys currently stand with him? >> Yeah, had have had good dialogue. Both Mike and I have have had good dialogue with Jacobe. Um, obviously this is the voluntary portion of everything. Um, you know, we'll continue to have conversations with Jacobe, but you know, things are things are in a good spot. >> Mike, what are your initial thoughts when you add a guy with love's talent level to compliment um Marv, Michael, Trey? >> Yeah, just another piece of the puzzle like you just said. I mean, he's got, you know, there's like I'm not going to sit here and say we don't all see the skill set, obviously, but to add that skill set to what I already believe is a pretty good skill set with our receiver room, with our tight end room, to add to that running back room. Um, it's it's cool, you know, and again, like like Monty said, like the expectation is for him to come in here, learn the system, learn his teammates, and get right to work just like we're asking all these other guys to do, even the guys that have, you know, um, done something in this league. So, uh, I think he's going to fit in really well with these guys. But I know he's going to fit in really well with these guys because again he's he loves this and and all teammates want is guys that are going to come in and help him win and compete and fight hard and play tough and do all the things that it takes to move the needle forward. >> How different is the prep moving from round one to rounds two and three going into the market? >> Uh you know really not different at all, Donnie. There's just fewer names left up on, you know, there's 32 less names on the board. Um you know, so we'll u we'll regroup in the morning. um you know, we already have an idea of the the top two or three guys that that are on the board that that we know one of them is going to be there because there's only one pick in front of us the second. Um and then really it's the same, you know, we'll pick there early in the second or you know, obviously we'll always listen if there's any opportunities to move around. Um and then we got to wait for 32 more names to come off the board before it's our turn again. So, um really not different at all. There's just, you know, fewer and fewer names on the board as we go. >> How many picks surprised you today? >> Say again. >> How many picks surprised you today? Oh man, I don't know. There. I mean, there's always a few. >> Yeah, >> there was a few. There was a few, but I mean, it always happens, you know, like 32 different teams, 32 different boards. Like, you know, everybody um everybody sees them a little bit differently. >> Which one surprised you? >> Okay. >> None of them. His mock hit. >> 32. 32 out of 32. >> He won. He won first round bingo. Yeah. Yeah. >> You guys should do that. It's a good game. First round bingo. You write 32 names on the board. First first person that crossed off all 32 wins for entertainment purposes only. Of course, you know. >> Absolutely. >> Yeah. That's right. That'd be great. That'd be great. >> Friendly wagers. >> Yeah. >> Sorry. >> Yeah. I'll go for for Mike. Like how do you think a running back can elevate? like how can an elite running back elevate an offense and kind of change the dynamic of the stress you guys are putting under? >> Yeah, running back, receiver, tight end. Like there's no secret in this league, explosives are are are massive. When you look at, you know, um outside of obviously points, like what are the the two biggest factors statistically? It's turnovers and explosives. It's actually closer than you'd think. And so anytime any way you can generate explosive um that's a good thing for the offense. Anytime you can, you know, obviously li uh limit explosive from a defense, that's a good thing for the Arizona Cardinals, you know. So when you bring in explosive playmakers at any position, uh you're giving yourself a better chance to have those explosives. I don't got to call the greatest play. Sometimes when you just get the ball to a guy like Trey McBride, he breaks three tackles and he turns into explosive. You know, same thing with our receivers. And so anytime you can get that from the backs, it's just that next position that uh allows you to, like I just said, get those explosives. >> Awesome. See you guys tomorrow night. Yeah. Thank you guys. Thank you.

title: LIVE: GM Monti Ossenfort and Asst. GM Dave Sears Day 3 NFL Draft
text: We made it. We made it. All right, you guys. >> Got Dave tonight. Good to see you guys. >> Uh, all right. So, sorry, we just uh just uh finished up the seventh round. Obviously, you see the guys are upstairs kind of finishing up um the undrafted process, kind of grinding through that. Um you know, we'll add a few guys there. Not going to be a huge class of undrafted guys, but we'll have a few of those guys that we hopefully get locked up here in the next half hour or so. Um you know, day started um took Caleb Proctor out of um defensive tackle out of Southeast Louisiana. Um you know, kind of uh came on through the process. Had a really good season this year. really productive season. Um saw him down at the East West game and then continued his strong spring process. Worked out well um both at the combine and his proday and then we had him in here on a 30 visit. Enjoyed our time with him there. Um and then Reggie Virgil um you know had a good year this year at Texas Tech. Had a good season. Um another guy that we had enjoy big personality on Reggie entertaining guy. had him in here on a 30 visit as well. Um, sixround uh Carson Sherar um linebacker out of University of Iowa. Sorry, I got a little allergy thing going on here. Um, you know, productive player for Iowa this year. Had been a productive special teams player his whole career. Um, you know, excited what he can do for us defensively in the kicking game and then finished up at the top of the seventh round with uh Jaden Williams, um, offensive tackle from from Miss. So, um, no movement, no trades. Um, you know, had a couple opportunities. Nothing quite got us excited to to move out on anything. That's the way it goes sometimes, but, um, you know, excited about the the seven guys we added at the in the undrafted group. We'll see how that all shakes out. But, um, you know, I think we added some some guys that are going to help out our our team and, um, increase the competition throughout all levels of the team. So, let it, uh, we'll let you guys fire him at us. Dave, with uh with with a guy like Caleb, um how do you kind of go about measuring what he can be compared to maybe some of the opposition he might have played at? I mean, you're watching the game tape, but there's there's got to be some projection, right? >> Yeah. I mean, the the good thing is he played against LSU this year. Obviously, that's the tape that everybody's going to go to, but he did play against other schools in the past, you know, um FBS school, stuff like that. and then you have him in an all-star game. So, you get to watch him for multiple practices against the bigger school comp. Uh it's a case where the kid succeeded in each one of those opportunities and he's also been able to stack weight. Uh I think at his proday he was up into the 290s, you know, so still tested very well. So, you're seeing some growth potential as well as being able to compete when you put them on the same level some of those bigger school guys. It seemed like uh as you guys went through the day, you guys ended up with a lot of players in this draft class that uh were high on that athleticism scale. Is that something you guys were looking at or is that just coincidence? >> I'd say more coincidence, but you know, obviously um like more athletic the better. Um yeah, I've seen that I've seen that used, you know. Um you know, uh yeah, our guys tested high. That's that's good. That's good. I wouldn't say it's it's something that we necessarily target. Although, you know, whenever we can add a good athlete, that's always a positive. >> Are there certain positions where you see that as maybe more valuable than others to to have some of that elite level athleticism? >> Uh, sure. I mean, I think in every position whenever, you know, but I I I also think you got to be you be careful. Um, you know, there's guys that that test really well and score well on that and then maybe they put the pads on and they get on the field and that may not always translate. So, you know, that's that's one metric. Um, you know, I would say there there's plenty plenty of examples of guys that that um test pot test highly on that type of stuff and then that doesn't translate to the field and the opposite. There's guys that don't test well, but hey, when you turn on the tape, you're wow, this guy's a pretty good athlete. So, it's it's another piece. >> One of those examples of the last thing you were talking about, Reggie was saying, you were actually happy that he ran the 45740 might slip down the board. What did he show you on tape? because he's talking about how he can take the top off defenses. You don't think that when you see four, five, seven. What did he show you on tape that kind of made you feel like he has that skill set? >> Yeah, I think that's a great example. I mean, you know, when you when you watch the tape of of Reggie, he's played against high level of competition this season at Texas Tech and, you know, they played made it into the playoffs and and played against good teams. I mean, you don't turn on the tape and and say Reggie's slow, you know? So, um, in the end, that's what matters. Like there can be guys that run really fast and test really fast and then they don't show that on tape and you know Reggie when you turn on the tape of Reggie he he does not play slow. So that's that's more important is what's on tape. >> With Kobe I I saw him listed anywhere between just right under 6'2 to 6'3. How will his height translate to the NFL kind of impact what he can do here? >> Well I mean it's really that's where he's going to have to improve his technique take the coaching. Um you know you always hear low man wins and leverage and stuff like that. So, if you have loose hips, if you can sink and bend your knees and your ankles, which Caleb can do, it could be an advantage to you. But, you have to have your hand placement correct. You have to have enough lower body strength, all those kind of things, uh, it's not like shorter is necessarily better. But, um, he's not to the point where he's so height deficient that he can't play a certain position or in a scheme, you know what I mean? And especially rushing the passer, when you have bigger offensive linemen who might be a little stiffer trying to get down on you and you could sink and get around, uh, that can be an asset, you know what I mean? M you uh obviously the draft board didn't necessarily fall to get a an edge type player. Um kind of where do you see the pass rush edge group for you right now as the roster stands? >> Yeah, I mean I think we got we got a lot of guys there that played a lot of ball between uh you know Sweaty um Baron Xavan um you know BJ uh BJ had a you know tough year last year coming off the knee and you know never really looked quite you know all the way back. Um you know Jordan Burch going into his second year you So I I think we have a group and then also Elliot Brown Neku in that in that room as well. So you know I think we have a group that is it's a good mix of guys that have are experienced that played a lot. Um you know and we got to find a way to put them in the best position. So um obviously always going to look to add and and increase and and raise the uh talent level. Um but it just didn't work out that way to add to that group and uh over the last three days. >> A lot of guys are coming from winning programs. How much stock do you put into that when you're doing the evaluation? Um, I mean it's nice, but I, you know, I don't, I don't know that that's necessarily a focal point, you know, but, um, obviously you like guys that have been around winning. You like guys that, you know, they're they're obviously coming from programs that are doing something right. So, that's always good, always good to see guys, and then that's going to help them make that transition um, to a higher level of competition. So, not necessarily a focal point, but it's also a nice benefit. >> Monte, with Jaden, I know he played both sides of the line. Is there a plan to start him out on one side or just kind of use that versatility to start off? >> Yeah, I mean he's he's played played u you know mainly right tackle but also saw quite a few snaps at left tackle as well in his career. I mean I think something 34 or something starts in his career. So um you know another guy that um you know he's played against good competition in the SEC. Um but also he's probably blocked as good of guys in practice like with the defensive line that they had coming out of there last year. Um he's he's saw good competition throughout his whole career. So, um, you know, with the with that with the tackle position, it's it's one that we work all our guys, both sides, and that'll be no different for Jaden. >> Just going off that, you bring back Elijah Wilkinson. Is that someone you see right now as a starting right tackle, just given what you guys did in the draft and other moves? >> Um, yeah, I mean, Elijah, you know, Elijah started 16 games or something last year for Atlanta. So, yeah, I think he'll certainly be in the mix. um you know, not really naming starters anywhere right now, but I think Elijah will definitely have a have a chance there. Um Elijah's another guy who he's played a lot of ball. He's played at different positions. He started, you know, the first go around with us, he was inside at guard. Um he's also played a lot of tackle in his career, so like the versatility that he has, but yeah, he'll definitely be in the mix at right tackle. >> Day always seems to be a little more like volatile in terms of like the the player talent and the dart post and stuff, but you guys have found talent pretty much all three prior drafts on day three. Is there a common denominator you find with all of these like round guys to have them see the success they have in the NFL? >> Um, no. I just think, you know, we have a pretty good process. We put a lot of work into it. Him and I, Rob Kissle, spend a lot of hours up there watching the tape of later round guys. Um, I don't think that's universal through everybody's draft process where um, the top level decision makers pour into the late rounds as much as they do the early rounds. Um, we got a lot of good scouts who who have conviction on some of these guys. We have an analytics department who helps guide us. You know, they got their systems, all their different charts, their Bellstar system, whatever they use. But so we get a lot of input from a lot of people and we take it seriously. You know, um, as a lifetime scout, I hate when people like, ah, it's just a six or seven, who cares? Like, really? I can name you a lot of good players who were found in those rounds who end up mattering for their team. So, I think as long as you emphasize it, you know, you should be able to do it pretty well. >> Sorry. We talked to Monty yesterday about Carson playing in some high pressure games and moments. You have a number of guys who played in the playoff and then even Caleb's game at LSU was high pressure. You know, how do you as a scout kind of evaluate or where do you put playing in big games, big moments on your list of I guess intangibles and whatnot? >> Well, I think it's important, you know, clutch play, you you could label it that, but it's more so, you know, you're looking for matchups, too. Who's the guy playing against? it could be a big game and he's got a weak opponent and he goes off in that game. But, um, you know, it's really the matchups of, you know, Carson Becks going against Texas A&M's defense or, you know, Ohio State's defense, things like that, um, that you're looking at as much as what is the stage, you know what I mean? >> Along those lines, um, I think you guys drafted three or four guys that played in the Shrine Bowl particularly and you had mentioned earlier about Proctor. you get to see them against those guys. Like the ability to see those guys in those all-star games against guys that are going in the draft and maybe are a little bit higher than even if they played in a big conference because those are the best of the best. I mean, how important are those games? And do you guys take a good chunk of what you're getting out when you go to these these all-star games? >> Yeah, I mean, I think any exposure you get is important. The thing about all-star games is you get or your scouts get to go to these games and watch the guys consecutive practices in a row, which you don't really do at schools. You you might hit a school in August, hit it again in October, hit it again maybe late November or something, but they're watching guys practice. Boom, boom, boom. Uh, so they get a feel for like the competition. Some guys will improve over the course of this, you know, hey, this guy's improving. If he can do that, there's more there. And the other thing is like we have our coaches at these games. Chris Cook worked the East West Shrine game. He knows Jaden from that game. So, he can tell us, "Hey, the guy was really good in the meeting room." He learned here, here's this technique that he picked up pretty quickly. I was teaching more, you know, vice versa. If it's negative impact, something like that. Clearly, it wasn't in that case, but uh so that is um very valuable to us. But it's not necessarily any more important than any other one, but you you get a a good experience when you dial in on that stuff. Dave, with Carson Shy, he was talking about how much pride he takes in playing special teams, but in what ways can you see his linebacker instincts when you play special teams, >> run hit, I mean, that's the name of the game. Like, you don't see the guy putting the brakes on before he runs through somebody's face. And that's what special teams is, you know what I mean? So, uh, linebacker obviously is a position where everybody leans on that position for special teams play. And when a guy has that background, like usually know the guy's tough, you usually know he'll work hard, whether he can run or not, like all things that translate to defense eventually. You know, >> you said your undrafted class won't be very big. Why? What goes into that decision? >> Just really roster number. You know, our roster was at a point where um we didn't have a ton of room. So, you know, it's it really comes down to that. I think we'll be six to eight somewhere in there. >> How do you say you approach the draft?
