We had a great weight room, but man, the weight room is just it was crazy. It was very open, man. It just spacious. I wanted I wanted to bench press right then and there. You know what I'm saying? Uh, man, I loved it. Um, those are the areas you I'm going to spend most of my time in, uh, getting better. So, uh, just to see it as beautiful as that, it's been great. Facility has been great, you know, and I can't wait to see the new stadium. Um, that'll be unbelievable. I've seen little Instagram clips of it and how it was built, like the process. So, it's pretty cool. >> Bean said that they had a they somebody here on staff who was with Clemson or I don't know, maybe you know the name. I don't I forget who it was, but is very familiar with the Clemson program. He's here on staff, knows how they operate. What is what was your communication like maybe through the season even with anybody on the Bills knowing kind of you had people there that kind of knew about each other? Did really just start in the pre-draft process? >> Um Keith Jennings is who you're talking about. I call him Jug Head, man. I love Jug Head. Um we've had a great relationship since I got to college, you know, and I'm I'm a big on improvement. So I've always asked like are like what you see that I can improve in when he watching my tape and things like that. We've gone back and forth with that. You know what I'm saying? Um just trying to understand where I can get better. Um, and you know, him just just being a Clemson guy, you know, he's always looking out for me. He always, uh, you know what I'm saying? Make sure I'm on top of my game, make sure I'm a good person and stuff still. Um, and he's always rooting for me regardless of what's going on through my ups and downs. Um, and I appreciate him a lot. And I'm just super excited that, you know, I get to get in the building with him, spend a lot of time with him, him being an alumni as well from Clemson. Um, it's amazing. So, >> have you talked to Shaq Lawson at all? He had uh he had uh tweeted uh uh excitement about your arrival in Buffalo after playing here many years. >> I got to hit the guy up. You know what I'm saying? That's my that's my dog, man. Uh and his his younger brother, J, man. I love him to death. We we played three years together, man. I'll do anything for him. The Lawson family in general, they they're great people. Um they're Clemson people. U man through and through. And if y'all know Shaq, you hear him before you see him in the building. You know what I'm saying? >> And that but that's that's him though. That's him though. That's real authentic. You know what I'm saying? And and that's one thing I appreciate, you know what I'm saying, about about Shaq. He going to keep it real regardless of what's going on. Um, man, so I'm definitely going to hit him up after this one. >> Talk about Davos Sweeney and how, you know, he prepared you for this process, >> man. Coach Sweeney, uh, man, I love him to death. First of all, he kept it real with me. You know what I'm saying? I didn't have uh the greatest year that that people would wanted me to have. Um, but at the same time, I put a lot of good things on tape and he he kept it real. said, "If this is what you feel, this how you feel about leaving and you ready, just know that you got you going to have to prepare and have a great a great spring." Um, and he he he understood I was I was always mentally wired the right way to do whatever I had to do. Um, and he was never really worried about me. Um, you know, he always shared his insight about the process and how it would go. Um, and you know, he was always a lifeline if I had any questions. Um, and he was always there to encourage me, always calling, always making sure I was good when I was in Cali training. Um, you know, he's always somebody I can always revert back to and, you know, call if anything needed. Um, so I I really appreciate Coach Sweeney. Uh, it's one of my favorite people I've ever met. He's really helped me change my life. So, >> you talking about putting pain on people? >> How are you planning to do that? And how would you make that effective with the rest of the defense? >> I'm running out there and hit somebody. You know what I'm saying? Look, since I was four years old, I told my mom I want to hit somebody and she threw me in football. Um, always been physical, always been violent. That's just how I play the game. I mean, it's just I think that's how the game should be played. Um, so for me, I'mma fly around, fly to run to the ball, and we're going to hit people. We're going to put pads on pads. You know what I'm saying? That's how the game needs to be played. >> Did you see that your quarterback teammate was just drafted by your division rival now, the Jets? >> Kade. >> Yeah, just showed me that. And Kade, when you see this, man, look, if I get a chance to play you and you out there throwing that rock, it ain't no ain't no practice now. You ain't got no purple jerseys on. I I don't got to ease up no more. I'm going run full speed through you. You know what I'm saying? Obviously, I'm I'mma land with my hands on the ground so we don't get fined. You know what I'm saying? We going we going to play within the parameters. Uh but man, I'm super excited for him, man. He's a hard worker. Unbelievable guy. Uh he going to come in right away, try to, you know what I'm saying, be a leader as much as possible. I mean, I'm super excited to see how his career pan out. Uh obviously, they got Gino Smith there, so that'd be great for him to learn behind him, um and get things going. So, I'm super excited for him. TJ, I would imagine, you know, when you get drafted, you've got all of these different thoughts and emotions that are going through your head now that you've had a little bit of time. I guess what is the thought about landing in Buffalo and what have you been thinking about since you got the call last night? >> That I'm going to Buffalo and like I I couldn't believe it. You know what I'm saying? Like you guys are are winners. You guys constantly win. You always find a way and a great culture. I always see crazy things about how the fans support and doing whatever it takes. Um, and I love that. That's what I've been around my entire football career. Um, and just to be a part of that now, it's amazing and I really can't wait to, you know, for to be embedded in more and the fans know who I am. So, >> I know you didn't get any sleep last night, but it's like what it going to be like, you know, you be able to get the ball back to Josh Allen. >> It's going to be amazing. I can't wait to meet him. You know what I'm saying? Uh when we found out we was going to the Bills, I had there was a couple Bills fans in the background who uh they probably crying like they won the Super Bowl uh knowing I was going here. But man, I I can't wait. I'm going do whatever it takes to, you know, give him the ball back much as possible so he can go win some games. So >> you lined up against Jude Bowie last season, Clemson versus Boston College. The girls just selected him not too long ago. Have you talked with him at all? >> I ain't talked to him yet, but man, I'm excited. You know what I'm saying? We're going to get more work in. Uh he's a great player. Um, I'm super happy for him and his family. You know what I'm saying? I hope he enjoy this moment. Uh, cuz we'll be up here soon. So, I know he's ready to work. I'm ready to work. Let's get to it. >> IGB today from Ohio State. What was that conversation like? >> That was dope, man. We really just shared experience about, you know, how we was waiting for the call and how we excited to be here. U, we excited to win. Um, I got his phone number. So, we g we locked in now. You know what I'm saying? I'm going to spend as much time. I'll help him however he needs it. Um, and I know he'll help me.

title: Brandon Beane Addresses The Media On Day Two Of The NFL Draft | Buffalo Bills
text: And in your decision to trade back three times, can you maybe put into perspective patience um but at a time when there was a little bit of a sense of urgency with the change and transitioning and want to win and the whole thing, but how do you balance one and the other? Yeah, I mean Tim, we we really I tell you every year we try to read our board and you know I I think I was trying to allude to it in here last week with the pre-draft presser that you know we didn't have a heavy number of first round grades and so once we saw the last player come off our board that we had a first round grade on, you know, we started being more aggressive with the calls And we had some different opportunities to go back further at one time, but we also wanted to kind of see how things fail before we before we did it. And we felt like there was still going to be interest by doing that. And I looked at it. It's it's luck. It's not skill. But um we were considering a move with from 26 all the way into two that I thought was a good move for us in the end. And then when we did the one to 28, I'm like, well, this is this is good, but you're also thinking, man, I really could have done a lot. Where I'm going with that is in the end by the multiple trades we ended up with more than that in a very similar position. So some of that's good fortune those teams still wanted to move back into one. Um and it was just really following our board. We had enough guys uh in a similar value on the board that we felt confident going to 35 we would be able to get a player like TJ. There were a lot of edge rushers in that part of the draft. Brandon, why was TJ the the one that you guys identified as the fit for your defense? >> Yeah, it was uh it was one of the strengths of this draft. Uh was a variety of edge rushers. Some of them are more DPRish. Um I would say TJ is a three down player. Uh his his sack production a year ago was 11 11 and a half, can't remember. uh sacks this year, not as many. Um but you've seen you saw enough from them. You know, we did a long study of a lot of these guys of two years versus just the one year. Some guys were better this year, some guys were better the previous year. We also a guy like him had a really good week at the Senior Bowl. So, we we try and weigh it all. Um but it's it's some close discussions, but you saw a run on those guys today. you know, all those guys were in a similar vein and that gave us the confidence to move back here. When I went home last night, I felt confident we were going to add um some type of rusher, whether it was a three down, whether it was a a DPR type um and TJ was the guy, you know, we had number one if it if it fell that way. >> Do you feel that um >> player just taking? >> Yeah. >> Um is you you talked about Christian Benford. I think that's interesting the other day about where he projects maybe. Um what kind of versatility does he have? Is he strictly an outside corner? What can he do for you? >> Yeah, this guy uh IGB because he's got a tougher name to say. Um obviously play major competition uh at Ohio State. He really, you know, a year ago did have some penalties, but this year really cleaned it up. Uh he's big, he's long. You know, if you look at our two, you know, kind of pencil in starters of Benford and Max right now, those are two different skill sets. I think this is a third skill set, a big long The best thing he does is press. Um, some guys are man match, some guys are best in off. Um, I think he gives us another added um, skill set. He started a lot of games, you know, in major college football. Um, he is wired the right way. We brought him I went to his proday and just I wanted to watch his movement, his off the ball, you know, movement versus just just press because he did so much press at Ohio State. Um and you know, he checked the box and and the multitude of people that I talked to there just raved about his football character, um his competitiveness, his love of ball, great teammate. uh and we found that out here start you know Jordan Hancock you know is close with him raved about him and so those guys hung out when he came in for a 30 visit as well so he kind of passed all the all the test for us and you know corner is a is a premium position you you can't have enough of those guys and and so right now with you know Tradavius being a free agent um with Dorian's uncertainty at this point we're we're hopeful uh but you know, we have to prepare right now, you know, with with what we're working with and and this adds another guy. You saw the depth of our corners tested last year through injury. And so, um, you want to make sure as the season goes along, if injury strikes that you got enough guys, even if they're not starters. So, this is a depth player that'll come in and compete. He'll push, you know, our starters in time and and um, you know, we'll kind of take it one day at a time. How did he take those convers How did he take those conversations of those guys being the pencled in starters just like that he'll be a backup? >> Oh, we don't we we haven't talked about that. No, we haven't. No, I'm just He's a rookie. So, I'm just like Max has been here a year. CB's obviously, you know, been here forever. So, any any rookie is going to have to come in here and earn it. Whether it's TJ, IGB, um whoever else we select. I mean, if he's the best player, he, you know, he'll start at the best the best 11. We'll go out there. But there's not really a discussion. Discussion is come in here with all these guys, learn our system, learn your role, play special teams. I think he has the demeanor, the makeup, the size to also help on fourth down. Those are the things you consider as you move into the move down the draft and and add depth at various positions. That's right. And he had a lot of penalties called against him, whether that's officiating or technique, but is it a worry that he committed so many penalties college? >> Well, I would say S. Uh, good question. One that we looked at. Um, he improved those dramatically this year. And so, we'll we'll work on that. Sometimes that's technique. I'm not going to get into the officiating of whether it was I'm I'm going to assume they were they were the good cause. You probably got away with some that could have been called and maybe were called for some ticky tack. that usually evens out. Um, that's one of the things that I would say he improved the most. If you watch his 24 film to his 25 film, very aware, football smart, um, young man, football savvy, you know, he's probably, you know, off coverage is something he'll have to continue to improve on. I think more of those were in that than than when he's up in press. How how much would Jim Leonard have known him or been aware of him when he was at Wisconsin? And um in in the overall picture in making the switch to an attacking style of defense that Joe Watts and Jim wants, how much was it how how important was it to add pieces to it today? Yeah, you know, we we felt like listen, we want to add good players on either side of the ball and and that'll be the plan, you know, assuming we don't pick any more tonight, tomorrow with with what we have left. Um, but we did feel like going into this draft after free agency, you know, we added a DJ Moore, we filled some of the holes in the O line, we probably had more open spots. Um I mean as you sit here today with with I said who who was going to be our third corner if we lined up and played right now that's a again that's a premium position. Um you know we lost Ryan Vandymark. We got some guys who's going to be our third tackle. Um you know we got some guys here at least that have you know in in Greyel and we drafted Lunt last year. But it's positions like that that you have to make sure you're ready because look at the game in I'm going back to the other side of the ball. The Pittsburgh game last year where two backup guys had to start for us at tackle. So the same thing at corner. We've got some probably more available spots on defense than we do on offense. So that's the other conversation you're having as you move down the board. How does the guy make your roster? And if you feel good, he makes your roster. Now, does he get a jersey on game day? How does he does he have fourth down value if he's not going to be a starter? So, those will continue to be the conversations tomorrow as we work through the fourth and fifth round. >> So, I uh I you'd have to ask Jim directly. I don't remember. Jim was very aware him and Jay Valai um and Terrence Jameson uh along the Dline, Bobby April, a lot on our defensive staff have been around these guys or recruited them. So there was a lot of awareness uh of a number. I don't remember specifically IGB without asking Jim. >> And you mentioned liking the uh depth at edge rusher. So, I guess the flip side to that would be why not wait at that position if you feel like the depth is there uh and address it later. What what about TJ stood out that you felt like you needed to to make that move then? >> Yeah, you don't know how I mean there was a run of them and you still have them, you know, you have guys in the second round, guys. I do think if if if there was a guy standing out above these guys, it would have gave us some comfort that we could get a player maybe, you know, at this pick that we just took IGB there. There's still some guys on the board, but I do feel like, you know, there was you're starting, you know, those are lower on our board, so you you kind of value them. I think with TJ, as I said earlier, some guys are two down players. They're they're run, some guys are DPR. feel like TJ has proven over the last couple years to be a three down uh he brings a three down skill set, you know, to the group and and I just think that adds more value. >> How do you evaluate whether this strategy was worth passing on higher drafted guys? >> What's the question? >> How how would you evaluate this strategy was worth passing up on higher drafted prospects? >> Well, I'm basing on my board, so you know, when you trade down, people are going to go up. But that doesn't mean just because someone's drafted there doesn't mean that you valued them. Every team has their own value and it doesn't make them bad picks. Time will tell on all these picks, right? But that's where you you build your board. You study it and you say, "Listen, in this case, we had a number of players at a similar value to TJ that we felt confident moving back." And listen, time will tell. TJ has to prove his worth of of this pick. Uh just like IGB and whoever else we select. >> Did you come to trading up >> uh in today? >> Yesterday. >> Uh yesterday. Um it didn't get close enough when where I felt because knowing that we didn't have the second round the 91st pick, you know, you you can go up four or five maybe. I can't remember or pair that with a four. You know, we had so many of these, you know, what I think are available spots that we need to fill depth, youth, add some some youth in various spots to this roster. Um, we kind of went in saying even if a guy fell close to us that we were like, man, I can't believe this guy's here. We wouldn't we wouldn't want to lose too much of of that ammo. So, it kind of got answered fairly fast. >> Point. How at what point do you have too many picks? How how many guys how many rookies can make this roster? >> Yeah, it's uh great question and I think we'll see as we go down, you know, the board. And that's that's what we're talking about with, you know, after this pick of what other positions, you know, do we do we know that if we don't fill here in the draft, we probably need to add some veteran players after. But I still think there's I still think we have some some spots that we can fill tomorrow. Uh we did, you know, part with one of the picks to move up and and and make sure we got IGB. So, uh what do we have? the three fours, the two fives, and the seven. So, yeah, I mean, you know, when you get to the seventh round, you know, for the most part, you're you're kind of securing a guy that you don't have to fight for as a priority free agent. Um, so in my mind, we got five picks. I would sit here and say most likely, we'll see how the board falls, Tim, but I would think a number of these guys will have a chance to to make a roster and help us In that plane, how important was it to stockpile picks on day one to give you some flexibility to use as leverage to trade up at some point? I mean, getting five picks in the first 126, I think, was uh more than double what you had going in. >> Yesterday was was huge. How you know how it worked out for us. And we knew when we left here last night looking at the board that we're going to be able to get a rusher as I said and we thought, you know, our board, you know, was stacked and I think you saw it. I mean, you guys can look at the picks in the second round. It was a lot more defense than offense. And we kind of saw that as well and thought, you know, we'll follow it. We're at 66. If we feel like a position of need is is starting to thin out, we'll move up. Not too far though because we worked hard to get get this ammunition and we still feel there's some some pieces that we would like to add tomorrow that that can help this team, you know, this year and going forward. >> Brandon, are you seeing when when you're drafting defensive players and you did the two tonight, um are you looking at them differently for this particular defense scheme versus what you've been doing for the past nine years? and if so, how? >> Yeah, good question. It's probably position specific a little bit, Vic. Um, we're grading the, you know, we're grading the player, the talent. Listen, there were other corners. We weren't just looking for a long press corner. There were other corners that had that were that were good as well that had a little different skill set that we like. So, it wasn't like Jim said, I need this big long press corner. We put our values on what they do well. um what are some of the things they need to work on? S referenced that you know the penalties from a year ago. Uh the good thing was that wasn't this year on that. But uh I would just say position by position obviously you know guys this is a this is a three force are the guys that you know used to be DNS for us. How do they how do they stand up? You know are they a SAM? Are they a rush? you know, so that we probably spent more time on those than we did, I would say, corners and safeties. But I do think, you know, there's been a little change even how we exactly want our safeties before versus, you know, what we can play with, you know, under Jim's defense, how he would utilize him. So, it was kind of position specific more than anything. I know you said that you after the last graded guy, first round graded guy went off the board. That's when you ultimately decided to move down. >> But you see the board thing out also as it's going and you said that you knew this was kind of a lesser year for first round and you have eight minutes. So when do you ultimately say to yourself, is it leading up to the draft or at that moment, hey, we got to start thinking about maybe getting out of 26. Are you really sitting there until that moment? No, you're you have conversations even before the draft starts with people people calling do do you guys plan to pick? Do you think you would move? People in front of us calling, hey, would you guys move up here? And you know, teams that were, you know, five, six, you know, however many up. It was like, yeah, that's going to cost us too much unless you're talking about giving us some some great bargain, which, you know, nobody's really going to probably do in the first round. So, I would say 90% of our conversations were with the teams directly behind us all the way into the second round. Some of those happen. Um I would say a lot of contact is made just kind of setting parameters of roughly what you might be talking about for that pick. But like anything, you know, yesterday a couple times some teams were offering more and so you you know it's like anything if more people want it, you can charge a little more, you know, on a premium of it. So it it worked out on a couple of those deals. We h we had a lot of interest in 26, not as much in 28, but then we had a lot in 30 was 31 the last. Yeah, we had a lot in 31. Uh so doing the move to 28 helps set up, you know, the ammo that we got um there at the end to move to 35. Brandon, why do you feel comfortable using a good asset like a second round pick on someone who's least projected now be a backup rather than addressing positions with clear paths to instantly impact this team? >> Um I would say that will impact our team. I mean, if you if you look at the corners are premium positions. If you just look at, you know, who who makes the, you know, the top dollars in the league. And if you look at our season last year, and it's it's happened before, John, those guys are all going to play. They're going to play. It's a long season. And when you have corners that are not capable, they get bullse eyes on them real fast. And especially when you're playing the prime time quarterbacks, the prime time offenses in this league. I I can tell you this, if there's another good corner tomorrow, we'll take them. Like, think of how many guys we went through last season that played in the playoffs for us or helping us get to the playoffs. So, you're going to need those guys. And again, you you're suiting up guys not only to fill in as a backup, but also to help you on fourth down, too. Those are the kicking game matters as well. >> Your advantage, what is the advantage on having five picks in the top 25? >> Yeah, you just, you know, you're you're giving yourself, you know, a chance at better players that you have on your board, guys that you value the most. So, uh, it's anytime you're adding assets, it just gives you a chance to move up, move down. You know, what we did yesterday allowed us to be more aggressive and take the six round pick we had today to go secure a corner. I know you didn't uh pay an exorbitant price, but did you have an inkling that a team between 62 and 65 might have been looking at him or were you worried that another team might be calling to move up to get him? >> I didn't I did know that some of those teams were interested in moving back not crazy far and you know it's it's one of those we we got enough ammo yesterday in a spot like this where it's close it just it just made too much sense. I was like, would I rather sit here and wait or be upset that the player was taken? It was like, it's close enough. Let's just do it. >> I know you don't have a you don't have a crystal ball. Like, you can't predict. Like, >> you guys don't think I have a crystal ball, >> right? Like, um, what's going to best set up TJ for making an impact in year one, but what have you learned as an evaluator and about that part of the process, figuring out how quickly they can assimilate to your program? And do you note that on your board for guys and do they get kind of ratcheted up if they're going to assimilate quicker? >> Yeah, I mean we give what we've talked about before, Bill's blue, which is guys that have all the they can be a seventh rounder, a first rounder, but they have all the intangibles, great teammate. They're going to work hard. They're going to do everything they can to achieve whatever the good Lord gave them. Um, so that that is part of the process. you know, we spend a lot of time and and that's one of the things that I've learned over my time here is how important and it's it's ever changing now with NIL the the athlete you're getting and onboarding and the pressure some of these guys are walking in here with money that they didn't used to walk in, you know, walk in here with. Um, but they're still young men and they're still working their way through life. Sometimes they went to college near where they went to high school and this is the first time moving away from home and they do hit challenges or they're leaving their their fiance, girlfriend, whatever they do life. They're they're humans. I know a lot of times we put them on pedestals, but that is one of the things that we put a lot of time and effort into our our player engagement. Dr. Dez. Um, you know, we we have a full hands-on deal trying to work with these guys and try and onboard them from college to being a professional. How do you manage your hours? You don't have class anymore. Um, you know, how do you manage your week, nutrition, getting them in our weight program? You know, some of these guys are from smaller schools. The weight program is totally different. some of the guys, you know, Ohio State probably not as big of a different transition from their weight program to ours, but sometimes you get some some smaller school guys that are. So, that is very important. And making sure these guys are mentally and physically right off the field helps you get, you know, a better player on. >> Brandon, how did you evaluate TJ's attributes to rush the pass? >> Yeah, I think he's I think he's got speed, but I think he's got power. He can use his arm. I think he's got a multitude of of moves. I think there's more in there. I think we can continue to work on that. But, um, if you just look at his athletic ability and you you see it on tape, uh, I think again, as I said, his his 24 film was very impressive. It it really was. This year, not as consistent. U, we'll, you know, we'll talk about that. We'll look at that. There were definitely flashes. You and you saw it come up again at the end of the year. uh against their rival South Carolina. You saw it at a senior bowl, so it's in there. We just got to all those are part of maturity and uh being a steady pro every day. You know, we can't, you know, one year be this and the next year be that. Um but the flashes are are really good of a three down player that will stick his face in there and play the run, but you know, is athletically explosive enough to help you, you know, in the pass rush. >> Differentiating in this three four system who's going to be on the outside like on the end on on on the line and who's going to be on the outside as far as linebackers go with the players you have and what you need to add >> and then inside too. >> Yeah. I mean like he's going to he'll be a standup outside backer for us, you know, like a like a chub type. That would probably be his closest comp on our team, you know, which will be a great guy for him to learn from as he moves forward. He he's also already he's 21. He's already married. His dad was a he's in the army and the Zoom call he attributed a lot of his maturity leadership to all of that. Can you kind of take us through meeting with him and those kind of characteristics? >> Yeah, I mean I think that's uh as Matt was talking about earlier like what are you know he's for the most part has shown to be a mature young man. I think he got married during the by-week uh last season. Comes from a military uh family. So, you know, seems like he was raised the right way. We, you know, we have a scout here in Keith Jennings at um played at Clemson, knows the Clemson family pretty well. Pretty good insight into this guy's daily routine, daily work habits, and really felt like we knew this this young man. Um, obviously, you know, until you get him in your building, you don't fully know him, but um, you know, a guy that feels like he is fairly mature for his age and we'll we'll work together to kind of continue to help him mature and welcome him and his wife up here to Western New York. >> 32. title: Instant Reaction: Bills Select Ohio State CB Davison Igbinosun After Trade Up In The 2nd Round
text: With the 62nd pick in the 2026 NFL draft, the Buffalo Bills select David Igmanos, DV Ohio State. >> Trade alert, the Bills move up four spots into the bottom of the second round to draft quarterback Davidson Ignosen out of Ohio State. Welcome into our NFL draft special alongside a voice of the Bills, Chris Brown. I'm Mattie Glab. Iben Osen is 6'2, 191, long frame, long arms, a speedster, ran a 445 40, and knows how to disrupt routes. Physicality is his game. He's going to get in your face and bat balls down. Why does drafting a quarterback in the second round make sense for Buffalo? Well, I think it was a sneaky need for the Bills because if you look at their current roster right now, the only players on their roster who got on the field last season and played cornerback for this team were Max Haristen and Christian Benford. Duro they picked up in free agency obviously played corner somewhere else. Atlanta he's projected as a possible nickel corner. So outside you really have no depth because Dorian Strong is coming back from a neck surgery. His future is uncertain as far as an NFL career is concerned. There is no determination on his future playing career as of right now. So he's a major if with a capital I. You don't have anyone else. You needed to fortify the depth at the cornerback position and the Bills felt it necessary to trade up to get Igbonosen here and you know he's reunited with Jordan Hancock his former Ohio State teammate. So, I I think it was a need that they had to address at some point in the draft. They choose to do it at the bottom of round two. >> They trade their 66th overall pick. That was their third rounder and their 182nd pick. That's the sixth rounder to the Broncos for 62 to get into the bottom of the second round and pick Ignosen. As you watch his highlights, he flies around the field. He's quick. that 44540 and is a physical cornerback press man is his type of game. How will his physicality fit in to the quarterback's room in Buffalo? >> Well, I mean, he's 6'2, 189, so he's a little narrowframed and I think he does have to add strength and a little bit of bulk uh cuz he's kind of long and lean, but that's what the Bills like. They like length and height uh for corners that play outside for them. Benford's 6'1. Harrison, I think, is an even six foot, but he's long limbmed. And so too is Igmanosen. I mean, he's got 33 inch arms. I mean, that's like offensive line arm length. So, they like long, tall corners outside. He fits the bill there. I think he's got to get a little bit bigger and stronger. You know, run support. Setting the edge out there on the outside is something that he's still learning to be more consistent with in terms of his game. But you're right about him being a press man corner. He likes getting in the face of wide receivers. He trusts his hip flip and ability to turn and plaster in man coverage and will jockey for position all the time. And I think the word to use for him in terms of plant and drive, he's twitchy. Okay? >> Like he can stick his foot in the ground and go in the other direction at the drop of a hat. So when that receiver is stemming his route, he can plant his foot or on a comeback, he can plant his foot, jump the route, make the int. um ultra competitive player. He's the youngest of four boys, six kids total in his family. We're talking about the number one high school recruit in the state of New Jersey. Yeah. >> When he came out for college, went to Old Miss for a year. His defensive coordinator moves on. He wants to transfer, goes to Ohio State when Ryan Day gave him a call. So durable player, 43 straight starts. And the thing that I like is there are plays on the ball. 29 career PBUS in four seasons. That's a fat number playing at a high level of football against some of the best receivers in the country. So, those are encouraging numbers where you got to worry a little bit. 18 penalties the last two seasons. He's grabby and he gets flagged. And it's clear he developed a reputation for being grabby because refs threw the flags on him a good deal. Like 18 penalties in 16 were while in coverage. I mean, that's a problem. So, that's got to get corrected. Um, you can be physical in the NFL. That's a good thing. It's good that he has that. You don't have to coach that into him, but he's going to have to learn the finer points of playing physical while also not drawing flags. That's on his to-do list. >> Four interceptions over the last two seasons. You mentioned that Igmanosen fills in a depth need at cornerback. The question being, you draft depth in the second round. For fans who may not understand why it's important to go that direction in the second round, >> how important is depth in the room right now? >> It's huge. And all I'll do is point to last season. You had Tradavius White out there who played well in the postseason. I'm not going to debate that for a second. He had a nice season uh for them in his comeback season after spending a year away with the Rams and the Ravens. But he gets nicked up in the Denver game. You lose Jammarcus Ingram on a wacky waiver situation. He's in Houston and you have to put Dane Jackson on the field for one play, >> touchdown, and you lost that game in overtime by three. You want better depth that you can turn to. And this is no reflection on Dane Jackson. He played his best. Guys played his heart out when he was in a Bills uniform, but you need higher quality talent, especially at quarterback in a throwing league. Igbonosen is an example of that. Does he have learning to do? Yes. But the elite physical traits are there and you can win with those and get by with those better than a seventh round pick. They felt they had to address it. They did it here. Check cornerback off the list. >> I think that's a great point by you. It's not just depth that you're adding to the cornerback room in Davis and Ignosen. It is better depth. It was a need because of what happened last year. you felt like that position group got really slim at times and you have someone while he does have learning to do can plug and play at times and does add a physicality to the defense. We look at who the Bills drafted 35th overall. They go edge rusher TJ Parker out of Clemson. Known for that power, known for that motor, then they go quarterback Ignosen, physicality, a powerful type of player. What are we learning about this 2026 draft class? uh that they want guys that are going to run and hit. I think that's pretty obvious. Um these are two very physically oriented players, players that like to deliver a blow, I guess, is what I'm saying. Not that there aren't other players in this draft who can do that, but the early indications are Jim Leonard wants a hard-nosed strength, powerbased, physical defense. That's what these two picks say to me in terms of what Jim Leonard is looking for. Speed might not be quite as important up front in particular. You obviously need speed at the corner position, but I think players that bring a physical edge to the field is clearly what he's looking for based on these first two selections on the defensive side of the ball. >> It seems like this coaching staff wants players where in their head, their mindset is we're going to be game wreckers and we're going to impose our force on you. We're going to make a difference in this game. And that's kind of what Parker and Igmanosen seem like based on their tape and based on some of the traits that we already talked about. You spoke about how he matches back up with defensive back Jordan Hancock who played at Ohio State. Hancock and Ignosen over overlapped for two seasons 2024 2025. Ohio State wins the natty in 2024. You're also getting a player who plays against really good talent and knows how to win at the highest level. >> Yeah. And I think the thing that encourages me is while he has to get bigger and stronger to help a little bit better against the run, he played in a conference where there is a lot of running of the football. Michigan runs the football, Iowa runs the football, Michigan State runs the football. Like there's a lot of teams in that conference. The reason that it's viewed as something he has to work on is because there's enough tape evidence of him defending the run where in other conferences, you know, out west in particular, they throw it all over the place. you never see a corner make a tackle in the run front. So, he's been exposed to it. He's still learning on how to be better and more consistent at it, you know, and I think with the quarterback and DB coaches you have here like Mike Dana, who's a good developer of talent, Jay Valai, the new quarterback's coach, you know, who who enforces and prioritizes defending the run on the edges, you know, I think he's going to get the right coaching to get better in that area. Buffalo had a talented pass defense last year at the top of the NFL. They add some new players to the mix this year. No more Taran Johnson. D. Alfred walks into the building. CJ Gardner Johnson as well as you look at the defensive backs group as a whole. What are you learning about the type of ball they're going to play and how versatile it could be? >> Yeah, I I think they want to play angry. I mean, CJ Gardner Johnson is one of the best trash talkers in the league, but he brings the physicality to back it up. Um, there are people with their head on the swivel on offense when they're facing CJ Gardenner Johnson cuz they might lose their lunch um if they're not paying attention. I think Ignosen has that same onfield disposition. Um, maybe he's a little quieter as a rookie, but I think he wants to make an impact early and often. So, while they have a lot of good character players on this roster, I think they wanted more players with an edge to their game. And we we heard TJ Parker tonight say, "When I get on the field, I want to bring the pain." We know how Imanosen plays. We know how CJ Gardner Johnson plays. So, I think these are examples of what they're trying to institute on the defensive side of the ball. They want an intimidation factor on that side of the ball. So, opposing offenses are looking over their shoulder wondering if they're going to take an extra lick, you know, or if they have enough space to catch the ball and then run or are they going to get blasted. That goes along with one of Joe Brady's new sayings, which is you have to play us. It also makes sense with put the ball down. It doesn't matter where we play, when we play, we're going to be ready to get after it and we're going to play hard.

title: Dan Morgan and Dave Canales post-draft press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: Good to see every every everybody. Um brain's a little fried right now. Um First off, just kind of want to thank the staff, uh the scouting staff, the coaches, football operations, everybody involved for what we feel is a successful draft. Uh we felt like we definitely got better. We challenged the roster in a lot of spots. Um gained gained a lot of depth in a lot in a lot of areas. Um so yeah, we feel feel good about what we accomplished during the draft and excited about things moving forward and we're obviously headed in the right direction, so um with that, I'll open it up to any questions. We'll kick things off with Joe Person. Hey Dan. Uh um What's up, Joe? Good good to see you, man. You too. Get getting a little dark over here. All right, you're good. Um once you traded back to 227, um what about the the I heard you talk about um challenging the roster and building depth. Did did you draft anyone this weekend you think will start from day one? Um you know, I think everybody that we drafted, you know, I think they'll all have the opportunity to compete um and that's what we're all about here, myself and coach and the rest of the staff. We want to bring guys in to challenge the roster and have them compete and you know, we brought we brought in a bunch of competitors during this draft and they're going to have a chance to compete and show us what they can do and uh it'll be fun to watch. Which of these guys do you think has the best chance to make the biggest, earliest impact? Uh I think it's up to them. You know, I think I'm uh excited about all the guys that we drafted, otherwise, you know, we wouldn't have drafted them, so they're all going to have the opportunity to come in and compete and we're excited to see what they can do. Are you considering bringing in another uh undrafted quarterback? Uh potentially. Potentially, we'll we'll do that and have four quarterbacks, which we really haven't had since I don't think we've been here, but yeah, there's definitely the potential for for that. You think it's likely? Yeah, I do. Okay. Yeah. Alex Zietlow. Hey Dan, congrats on um getting through another NFL draft. Thanks. What's up, Alex? What's up, man? Um uh particularly on day three, there seemed to be a couple guys who um uh who fell to you guys. Um particularly uh Zaquandre Whiteley and um and Sam Hecht. Are those two guys, when you had the opportunity to draft them, were were you surprised that they were still available at um when you got the chance to take them? Uh yeah, a little bit. You know, I think uh I think you saw us kind of maneuver around the board a little bit. Uh just looking at our board, you know, we had a handful players that we had up there, so we're like, "Hey, we like these guys." Like they're all guys that we feel like can help us, so we're like, "Let's trade back. Let's gain more picks, gain more value." And you know, we did that and then and it worked out in our favor at the end. Specifically about Zaquandre, how do you see him fitting into the this defense? Yeah, you know, just a big, long, physical guy. Um he fits the DNA that we want, the type of competitor that we want. Um he can play the post, he can play up in the box, he can do a lot of things for our defense that we're excited about. Any more questions? Cassie. Hey Dan, how's it going? What's up, Cassie? Um you had a couple of guys today that made it through college or at least the last couple of years without a single penalty. Is that just kind of a coincidence or is that something that y'all value and look at? I mean, obviously, we don't want penalties. Um I think it's more a coincidence than than anything. Um but honestly, I didn't even really know that. That's kind of cool, though. Yeah, I think it was uh Whiteley and Hecht made it through without a penalty in college or at least last couple of years. And then on Will Lee specifically, he he comes off the tape like really just kind of tenacious. How important is that in a safety back there? Yeah, you know, corner, safety, um that's what we want, you know, that's our identity. You know, we want to be physical, we want to be tough, we want to be competitive and you know, we we're drafting those type of guys in our culture and um you know, I think every one of those guys that we drafted, you know, from the first round all the way down to the seventh, they they embody that. Daron Gantt followed by Mike Kaye. Dan, specifically to Hecht at center, what did you guys see in him that you like and and how do you see him competing right out of the gate? Yeah, he's going to have a chance to compete. Um I think first and foremost, you see his initial quickness. Uh he's really good with angles. You know, he can reach guys. He's good with his hands, getting his hands inside, controlling blockers and staying staying sticky on blocks. Um I would say is the biggest thing with him, staying on his feet, keeping his balance. Um he's another guy that can work to the second level. He can get out in space as a puller. Um so there's a lot of things that we like about him. Was it a priority for you this weekend to to make that room not only deeper, but younger as you look at the makeup of the offensive line as a whole? Yeah, you know, I I definitely think we need to add some youth in there, you know, on the interior and outside at tackle and feel like we accomplished that and you know, we'll do some things in undrafted free agency as well that'll again add to the competition and the and the depth out there. Hey Dan, thanks for doing this. Yeah. I'm setting myself up to be made fun of because of how I pronounce the kids' name uh by Joe. Uh Jackson, the guy you just added from Miami of Ohio. Um do you see him as kind of a special teams cog or what what's your outlook on him? He doesn't have a lot of playing time prior to last year. Yeah, good player, uh really good instincts. He can run, he plays fast. Uh he sees it really well. Uh a guy that we're obviously excited about. You know, I think he's definitely going to be able to contribute on special teams and again, like like every area, like he's going to have a chance to compete and show us what he can do. And then with Will Lee, um do you see him primarily working outside boundary wise? I know he brought up how much he likes doing press man, but obviously that's not something you guys do a ton. Um do you guys see him as like a long-term outside cornerback? Yeah, um you know, I think obviously, I'll leave that up to the coaches for what they want to do with him. Um at Texas A&M, he played on the outside and he's really good at press and and I think he's a guy that as he continues to grow and mature in the game, he'll be able to, you know, figure out off coverage and some of the things that we do schematically. I think he's just a really good fit for us by the way he plays, the temperament he plays with, the swag he plays with out there. Uh just a guy that we really loved. Joe Person followed by Sheena Quick. Um Dan is Dan or Dave can address this or both of you. Kind of following up on Daron's question. Were was this a draft where you you guys wanted to, you know, kind of look long-term more so maybe than than short-term? Uh I'll answer that. I mean, I won't For for me, it's always about right now. Uh this season and what we're doing and um trying to make sure that we can get the most out of our guys that we currently have. We always start with our roster, but then, you know, trying to find guys that fit the traits and characteristics, personality of who the Panthers are. Um and that's what we were looking for is just get more of that and uh it's going to be the same thing every year. You know, can we how can we make the 2026 Panthers the best possible unit that we can make it and um if we have guys that, you know, bring a certain skill set at any position uh to give them a chance to compete and be out there, you know, we just felt feel like it elevates the whole group. And then back to Dan. Um is there's a lot all every year, I really since you took over, people uh and you have drafted tight ends, but I there's this feeling I think that you guys need to go get a tight end a number one tight end. Is that shared in in the building or I don't know. You you addressed it a little bit last week. >> Yeah, we have a we have a lot of confidence in the guys that are on our roster and I said that before, you know, with Tommy and with Mitch and with Jatavion and James Mitchell and you know, we we have some guys that we're excited about and you know, again, we'll always look for, you know, avenues to make the roster better. If we feel like we need to, you know, figure figure out tight end and bring a different skill set in, then we'll do that, but right now, we feel good about it. And then Dan, any positions where you feel like you're still maybe a little light, whether it's inside linebacker, even corner? Uh you know, I think again, we're we're always going to find ways. We're never going to be content. We're never we're never just going to sit there. We're just going to try to add as much depth and competition to the roster as possible and you know, we'll we'll keep doing that moving forward. Good afternoon, guys. How are you? Good. How you doing? Um just a question about uh Lee and Whiteley. What specifically did you guys see in those two players that made them a fit for the corner and safety rooms that you guys have right now? Lee Lee and Wheatley? Yeah, Will Lee. Oh, yeah. Um, you want to go? >> Yeah, I'll take it. Yeah. Um, you know, we look for play style first and foremost. Um, trying to project, you know, the the athletic ability to contribute is obviously a big part of it. But then, once we kind of know and identify guys that we feel like can can impact us and can play in the NFL from an athletic standpoint, then we go to play style. And you know, Will Lee, Dan kind of talked about it a little bit, the length, the aggressiveness, his ability to play physical at the at the attack point, whether it's on bubble screens or getting involved in the run game. We ask our corners to tackle, you know, and and be a part of the fits in our system with our cracker place rules and different things like that. So, we felt like he really fit that mold. And then, for Z Wheatley, he's just a really instinctive player, physical player, shows up downhill, takes really good angles, runs downhill. He's all over the field and you know, just that kind of activity on the back half is it's really crucial for how we play football and and guys being able to see the formation, anticipate concepts, and then show up physically and play with that type of attitude that we're looking for. We had a great time you know, meeting with Zakhia at the combine and just kind of picking his brain about what he knew, what he was looking for and where he came from and how he's become the player that he's come. And we just loved all the background and everything and it really shows on on film and he was one of my favorite guys just through the process to see him in the play style that he brought. Thanks, guys. We have time for just a few more. We'll go back to Mike Kaye. Hey Dave, this running back class is not particularly deep at least from the outside looking in and in the selections that were made. You've had Jonathan in the program for about a week. Obviously, you're not doing any contacts. You drafted Etienne last year. I know we're talking about the moves you did make, but the fact that you guys didn't push for a running back with how much you publicly talk about wanting to run the ball. What does that say about those two guys and your guys' outlook on them? Well, it goes beyond that, too. You know, AJ Dillon's here. You know, Trey Tyson's guy we're really excited about getting to see coming up here when we get into camp in the preseason games. And and and Montrell's another guy who, you know, played at a really high level in college and and is is finding his way in the pros. But we were able to bring those guys in. We're excited to see what they can do. And when we start with this process, we always, you know, as we're looking at players in the draft, we kind of look at them compared to our roster, compared to the guys we have. Who is this guy competing with in this room? Like where do we see them being able to try to affect it? And we got a bunch of guys that we're really excited about. And you know, of course you talked about Jonathan and and Trevor, you know, um, in in that conversation as well. And and we have high hopes for Jonathan, you know, and and he looks great right now. Can't wait to, you know, in the smartest way possible get him out there and expose him at the right time and and get him accustomed to the things that we're doing. But um, yeah, love that group. I love what Bernie Parmalee's doing with them and and how they attack it. And you know, we kind of tell them you set the tone for the offense. And so, we love the way those guys are built. And we haven't been able to talk to you about it yet, but Trevon and JT do you think both participating in the program as well? Yeah. Um, the Trevon came back he's he's doing really great in terms of getting back out there. JT's been cleared. He's doing more and more. So, but right now as we know, you know, they're it's weight room and and meetings right now. So, until we get onto the field and kind of move them around, we still got to be smart about all that stuff. Yeah. Thank you. All right, guys. That's all the questions we have for you today. Thank you so much for taking the time. Thanks, guys. All right, thank you. >> [music] [music]

text: All right. All right. So, uh, first off, uh, jacked about tonight and, uh, being able to get Lee Hunter and Chris Brazzle. But we have a really good group in there uh versatile guys that uh we can use in different ways. >> Yeah. And I would add too like the way that we play our Dline like >> there's really not like starters like you know we're rotating a bunch so he's just going to be in that rotation. He can play nose, he can play a little DN in the 34. Um, so he brings a lot of versatility. >> Were you concerned that the Jets might take him 50? >> I was a little concerned that, you know, Dline's pretty thin this draft. What does that say about, you know, was that something you really wanted to address coming in? Yeah, I think uh you know, coach and I and and the rest of the staff like we believe in building building it up front and and winning the line of scrimmage and and I think if you can win the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, you have a chance to win every single game. So, yeah, that's definitely a point of emphasis. Dave, uh, you haven't had a guy with this type of speed in this offense, uh, so far, a guy that can, you know, get downfield, like you said, vertically consistently. What is it about a guy that has that type of size and speed that makes him so dynamic outside of the route tree that you >> Well, it's the ability to uh take those traits, but then also to play the ball in the air. Um, one of the things that Chris showed is his ability to play the deep ball, land on his feet, finish the play. Um, that's something that's very rare where a lot of times you'll see a guy high point a ball, lay out for it, they end up on the ground. Um, he's just got a special balance with how he finishes, which translates that speed and that size, you know. Um, so just all those things, you know, and and and we've seen how we've been able to use Xavier, T-Mac, Jaylen, you know, with all the uh intermediate stuff and have gone down the field a little bit, you know, and taken some opportunities, but, you know, I think about the space created when they know this is a real burner um and what that does to safeties, what that does to corners and just creating space um for the whole group. >> You mentioned a few guys in that wide receiver room. Can you have too much talent in in a room? >> Absolutely not. You you just, you know, you continue to add great players and and it elevates everybody's play. Um how that plays out, we'll see. You know, there's a lot of work that's got to be done from now until we start the season. And um it's just great to continue to add those guys so that we have different elements and and increase the level of competition in the room. >> You call Chris one of your favorite players in the draft. And um, you know, in our conversations, you know, as we were going through the process, I was like, "Guys, look at this." Um, because it's a two-way go for you at that point. And then, of course, it was just the uh the acrobatic body balance and ability to stay on his feet to track the ball down the field um that I really just uh fell in love with, you know, and uh and looked, you know, was really excited to get an opportunity to work with those skills. >> You guys had him in on a 30, I think. >> Yeah, we did. What was that visit like with him? >> It was great. It was great. Uh, you know, great personality. Uh, obviously another guy that loves football and, you know, he bleeds it. I haven't looked at my phone yet, but I'm sure I'm sure Bryce will be happy about that. >> Dave, your um your response or assessment of the in-person visit with Chris? >> Yeah, so we had him at the combine first. Um and and then we brought him in for the 30 visit, get to spend a little bit more time. And what impressed me about him is just when he talks about what he was working on, that's something that's really big for me, having receiver coaching background. Um, when I can hear a guy talk about the the different skills that they're working on, the drills they're doing, um, he's got a he's got a brother, you know, and like they're doing one-on- ones and they're he he loves the game. He's a um he's about his craft and you can see that on the field. You can see how um how compact and and efficient he is with his footwork and different things. But that always impresses me when a guy has a plan for what they're trying to improve upon. Dan, there are so many kind of players that fit what you guys want to do that got a lot of hype entering the draft. Is there originally it felt like you were going to come in after the end of the third round? Why did you guys kind of stop and come up now as opposed to maybe tracking the rest of the draft possibilities and today? >> Why did we come up in the >> like the draft is still going on? >> Oh, got you. Yeah, I mean there's still guys out there, but you know, we traded up once and obviously we had to give one of our fives and um we got a six back, but you know, I think um in our situation like we feel good about where we're at and what our board looks like and and we'll be ready for tomorrow. >> I think you're averaging like 6'2, 63 in this receiver road now. What kind of how important was it to establish that identity and what does it do for your offense to have a receiver like that? >> Just great players. Uh we're not really necessarily trying to set a prototype. We just happen to continue have opportunities to bring in these massive men, you know, and um all the way down to Bryson Tumine who's 6'5 and goes about 220. You know, they're they're uh these guys are rugged in the run game. That's really important to us. That's something that that Brad uh harps on that Rob Moore is really serious about. Um because we know we're going to run the ball and um and that length and size does help us with some of the different things uh that we do with the run game. And then of course just like uh creating an advantage, you know, um as a target when you when you have that type of size and length, you know, length is very forgiving in terms of getting body position and finishing on the ball. And that's what we've seen out of our guys. Um being able to make those plays in contested situations and and now we got a guy who's who's tall and he's also really fast, you know, and so uh his length and all those things will continue to help him and the speed. Also >> along those lines, there was a lot of speculation that you guys wanted like a yards after catch guy, somebody you could also involve in the run game from a receiver standpoint. Was that a thing and it just didn't quite fit with with your board? >> Um, I think he does have a little run after catch. Um, you know, obviously he's got the 437 speed. Um, so he is a guy that can, you know, if he gets it and he hits a crease, he has the speed to take it the distance. And, um, you know, where we're at making the playoffs and kind of being a little further back in the order, obviously that's going to limit you and, you know, who's going to be available to you as well. So, um, we're just jacked that we could get Chris there at the end. Maybe not a position of need, but is there a certain position in this draft that's kind of gone differently than maybe you had projected or or maybe a trend that you've noticed in these first three? >> Yeah, I mean, I think you just see, you know, once uh like the tight ends, like the tight ends went on a run there for a little bit. The wide outs started kind of going on a run there towards the end when we picked Chris. Um, so yeah, I mean I think you know once one guys starts getting picked and I think teams start seeing guys fall off the board kind of makes everybody a little antsy and you know they start picking that position. So um I don't know if there's one particular position but I think you know once you see you know a particular guy come off the board I think teams get a little spooked and um and they'll go on runs. Dan, as you look at the as you look at the roster as a whole, and as it's got better and deeper, does it change the way you look at day three of the draft, just in terms of how guys fit, whether they make the roster, that kind of thing? >> Yeah, I think uh the big thing is going to be how can guys contribute on special teams. Um, you know, we we only have a certain amount of guys we can dress on game day. So, you know, these guys, you know, here towards the end of the draft, they're going to have to be good teamers, you know, to be able to make our team and and contribute the way we want them to. >> Does that look like linebackers and safeties, tight ends? >> I mean, yeah, it could be it could be a combination of of guys. That's a good try, though. >> No, team. >> Yeah, definitely. Yeah, it's um yeah, usually linebackers, tight ends, it can be corners, safeties, you know, returners, you know, so we'll explore every option and, you know, we'll pick the right guy for us. >> Does Chris have any He doesn't have any return background, does he? >> No, he's No. >> Yeah. >> All right, everybody. Good. Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. Nat.

Like without him, I wouldn't be in this position, man. All the struggles, all the all the trials and tribulations I done went through in college and my family and stuff. And shoot, he brought me out on the other side. So for me and my family, man, this is this is an ecstatic moment, bro. I can't lie. So I'm feeling good, man. My fans feeling good. I'm just ready to get down to Dallas and play some ball, man. >> Anthony, you and I have actually talked a couple times during my time covering the American Conference, and I've been a big fan of your game for quite some time. I know they're getting somebody who can take the top off the defense, somebody who's fast, and somebody who loves to compete, ready to work every day. So, shoot, just as a receiver, man, I'm ready to just go get it. >> Hey, Anthony, congratulations. Walk me through the emotions of the weekend. Did you expect to be picked coming in? I I mean, I did have that faith, man, that I was going to get picked this weekend. Just just having that hope. Um, and then as the weekend went off, went on and stuff like that, I just seen the rounds go on and on and stuff like that. And, um, I still kept that hope, my family still kept that hope that I was gonna get drafted. Um, and then me and my agent had talked and stuff like that. And, um, we were kind of prepared to go to the UDFA route. And then, um, the Cowboys had called me, man, and, uh, walked downstairs with my family and and told them who I was on the phone with and stuff. And I got a lot of family who's Dallas fans. So, when they heard that I was on the phone with you guys, ready to get drafted, they were they were so excited, man. So, for me and my family, bro, it's just like it's a crazy process. It's a long process, but it it was all worth it, bro. For sure. >> And then you'll be reuniting with Savone Revel Jr., uh, have you talked to Vaughn yet? Has he shot you a text? >> He hasn't. He hasn't just yet, but me and him talked the other day, though, man. Me and him talked the other day just about like um being at the next level, things to expect and stuff like that, and the work that you got to put in. And um I mean he's been there for a year so he's been pouring into me knowing that um this is my goal that I want to get to the NFL and I want to play in the NFL. Um so like him just pouring into me and just letting me know the things that I need to get right and and check off the box um so that I can make those things happen. So that's that's my good man for sure. Um, just just getting older, you know what I'm saying? Learning how to how to really play ball and how to really, you know what I'm saying? the ins and outs of the offense and stuff like that. And then um the intentionality that every day coming in coming in the building, whether it's treatment, lift, um conditioning, practice that I'm just trying to attack it, um shoot, won't get 1% better each day, man. Just attack it head on. Um and just compete at everything I do, man. So, >> you also seem to have an outstanding hair game, Anthony. [laughter] Uh what goes into that? >> Shoot. Not much, honestly. I mean, shoot. I I uh I cut my hair not too long ago. I used to have it super super long, but I I cut it short now, so a little bit more manageable, easy to maintain. So, >> that's just natural talent. That's all it is. >> Yeah, man. Just natural, bro. Just natural. [laughter] >> Hey, Anthony, congratulations. I mean, shoot, for me, bro, my goal is to play in the NFL, not just make it. So, whether I get to play a receiver, scout team, running back, returner, front line on kickoff, for me, it don't really matter, man. I just want to just help the team win and make an impact um wherever I can. So, for me, man, I'm open to any and everything, bro. >> Anthony, talk to me about uh what the Cowboys are getting from you off the field. What do you like to do in your free time outside of football? What kind of person are you? >> Shoot. For me, man, I'm a real chill, relaxed person, man. I got two dogs. So, for me, that's that's where I spend most of my time when I'm not um at the facilities or when I'm not doing football. I'm usually outside the dog park or laid up with my pups, man. So that's uh that's something that shoot that that's they've been ride or die on me, man, since the NC State days. So yeah, man. They get all my time when I'm not doing ball, man. >> What kind of dogs are they? >> I got a lab retriever hound mix and then I got a great pair of knees. >> Oo, that's a lot of food. That's a lot of food, man. Hey, good thing you're getting a contract, man. Congratulations. [laughter] >> Hey, for real, though, bro. I appreciate you, brother. >> We We do have a a dog food sponsor, so go ahead and just get on that. Oh, that may come in handy. >> Yeah, just just keep keep that in mind whenever you get here to Dallas. Pinto Pince and a pirate, Mr. Anthony Smith joining us here. Anthony, thanks so much, man. We're excited to to see you here in Dallas. safe travels and we'll talk to you again next week. >> Yes, sir.
