Um, we've been really pleased with the, you know, early part of the offseason program and we think, you know, Taylor will really fit in nicely just because of how he's wired, his work ethic. Um, you know, so we're we're looking forward to seeing that group progress over the course of the spring and summer. >> And do you feel like Deshawn I know he was a really good mentor to the younger guys last year and everything. Do you think he'll be good for someone like like Talon with his Pro Bowl background and all of that? >> Yeah, I like Deshawn's Deshawn's great with his teammates. Um and and I I'd imagine that would continue to be the case. Um so that that group they they work together really well and they get along really well. >> At this stage of the draft, how much does a guy in sort of in relation to to Justin Jefferson, how much does a guy having that special teams quality and that is a characteristic in their game maybe like boost them on your board or sort of fit into the picture when you're thinking about value at this at this stage? >> It's definitely a factor. Um, it's not a one-sizefits-all approach. You know, I think with with Justin, he's a a DNA match for this defense because, you know, we'll prioritize speed, range, athleticism, and sacrifice a little bit of size because of how we play. Um, but then also like his ability in in the kicking game is is certainly a bonus um because it gives a relatively high floor for a year one role. >> You folks right into the season that the offseason is going to be mostly about the offense, right? The resources. I I'm just wondering when you were interviewing Todd and talking to Todd before he got the job, how much of that was a discussion topic on how you're going to fix it and exactly how he thought you might be able to fix? >> Yeah, we were transparent with all the candidates we talked to about that part of it. You know, we were honest with where we were in our, you know, our roster life cycle and said, "Hey, look here. Here's how we've positioned ourselves, you know, going into this year and how here's how we generally uh anticipate deploying the assets." So, that's something that we were very open at. I think to accept a job, you know, this big as like a, you know, head coach in the NFL, um, you know, when you're walking into a team with transition, like you have to have visibility in terms of, you know, what, you know, what that'll look like moving forward. >> Andrew, um, you had some, uh, not draft related, but, you had some a group of players in for for tryyouts during the baller mini camp. Are you planning on did are you planning on keeping some around continuing those tryyous signing any of them? Have any decisions made? >> Uh we have not signed any today. Um you know that's probably TBD. I would not anticipate that we're signing any veterans in the short term. But you know it's something that we could revisit as we get through draft week and as we get through the um undrafted free agent signing process. >> Does Taylor Green then complete the quarterback room? >> Uh yes. Yeah. Uh you know what? Let me back up. I should have I I should have learned the I' I've learned the hard way not to say anything definitively. The current plan is that we would roll with those four. I can't predict if something else comes up. So yes, that would be the intention. >> Off the bat, he has started so many games in college. He's been around for a long time. He's played a lot of football. How did that maybe sort of factor into your decision? you know, it it's part of the equation, Mary Kay, but I wouldn't say that it was, you know, by any means like the heaviest weight or the driving force, you know, behind the decision. Um, but yeah, it it it does it does play a role in >> you feel like you construct like through the draft, through the offse construct this offensive line to make it conducive to a Joel return if he decides that he wants to come back. >> Uh, I play this way. We'll never run away from good players. Of all your picks, which is the most surprising you you got them right now? >> That's a great question, Jeff. >> Um, honestly, it's it's it's Eman. Like, it it really it's Emanuel. Um, that's the one that I I wouldn't have anticipated that he would have been available where where we selected him. >> We so much about quarterback. So, when you entered this weekend, did you think you were going to take Tailon, but was that part of the plan? I mean, I know I know things changed, but like when you envisioned it, was that >> I'd say this like there was um I don't know that you can predict day three of the draft. Um we knew that quarterback could have be one of the positions as we thought through how day three could play out that we could make a selection. Um and he was certainly in the pool of quarterbacks that obviously he was in the pool of quarterbacks that um could come in consideration depending on how the board felt. But I I wouldn't say it was like, okay, hey, look, you can't be so strict with your planning because you just you don't you don't control how the names come off the come off the board.

title: Adam Al-Khayyal Press Conference: "We really like how he fits with the offensive scheme"
text: All right. So, uh, started the day with, uh, four picks in five. Had to wait a little bit. Um, took some patience, but really happy with how it played out. Um, you know, we took Parker Braillesford, made one trade with Seattle to pick up a future four. Um, took Justin Jefferson out of Alabama, and then made another trade back in five to also pick up a future six. So, the whole net, really pleased with that. um can certainly open up to questions on both Parker and Justin um as you have them. >> So Parker's like under 300 pounds, which is becoming an unusual for a center. Was that the physical set you were looking for there? >> A lighter center. >> Light I wouldn't say that. I think an athletic center. What he does really well is move in the run game. Got uh tremendous range. Um, great finish. To be honest, if you didn't know his measurables on his card, you wouldn't say he plays like a sub 300 pound player. He's strong, firm. Um, so really like the skill set and really like how it fits with uh the offensive scheme. >> Along those lines, I was going to say like what you what you just described, it seems like it maybe the the frame is similar to Tyler Lander and Mon being there. Was that something that you saw parallels to or was it kind of a different type of player? >> Yeah, I you don't want to directly compare him one to one with, you know, Linder Bond, but I would say that you have seen coach Monkin play with an athletic center with range and do a lot of creative stuff in the run game and that certainly is appealing in terms of Parker and how we would deploy him. >> Long saw the fastest 10 yard split of any other line at the combine. How important are those movement skills, especially for what you guys? >> Yeah, really important. I mean, the main thing that they got to do is get on guys and get on guys quickly. And so, the guys with range who can climb to the second level, pull, move out in space, you know, all of that's predicated on having quickness, athleticism, and range. So, guys who can move like that are, you know, are really successful in the scheme. when you're looking on day three, how much that, you know, both these guys come from a program at Alabama. How much do you kind of look at the pedigree of the where where they come from, you know, in terms of hoping to catch guys maybe develop maybe a little further along or in the development for this net to jump to the next level? >> Yeah. You know, I would say the interesting thing with both of them is they didn't start their careers at Alabama, right? So Parker starts off at Washington, transfers to Alabama. Justin started off in JO, transferred to Alabama. Um, both those guys had a like a developmental curve. Uh, and with Parker in particular, you know, I think it's he's playing against the best of the best in the SEC. So, he is matching up against guys with size who he's going to have to face in the NFL. And and that is something that maybe if you have a small school guy who lacks size, you're making more of a projection on how that'll play out. Justin, what did you guys like about him and and what do you kind of envision him adding to that linebacker room? And it looks like maybe on special teams, too. >> Yeah, really nice scheme fit first and foremost. I mean, we have played with um you know, Devin Bush, we signed Quincy Williams. Both of those guys are around the same size, six foot, really fast, really athletic. So, just a real clean and vision for how he fits into the scheme. Um, and then when you have guys who can run 44, um, and like to hit, that translates pretty well on special teams. So, I think, you know, Justin, both on defense and on special teams will have a nice role. >> With the four fifth round picks, was there any effort to move up in the round? >> That's something we discussed. Yeah. And discussed moving up. Obviously, we moved back, you know, with one of the picks and we moved out entirely with one of the picks. So >> state center went a few notches ahead of your center >> there. There was there was a run on the centers, but to be honest, Parker was the guy we had targeted all along. >> Can he get bigger or is this his 289? Is that his size? >> He played in the high 280s, you know, low 290s. I I think he is more than capable at functioning and playing where he's at in terms of his weight. Obviously, you guys have devoted a bunch of resources to the offensive line in the last month and a half. Coming into the draft, how important or how much of a focus was it to add somebody at that center spot? >> I wouldn't say there was a focus at one particular spot. I think the focus was adding good players along the offensive line. Um, I think it's been noted we've added guys with positional versatility. That's important. We know that you're going into the year you're going to have your starting five, but the reality is you're going to play with more than five. I think last year the top if you played more than 50% of your snaps with your top five linemen, you would have been in the top 10 in the league. So, you're going to have to cover, you know, a,000 2,000 snaps somewhere on the line with other guys usually the way injuries go. So, you know, I think we just were focused on getting good players who could play on the line and then, you know, figuring out the configuration from there. Dan, do you think um are some positions uh easier for guys drafted later to succeed than others such as Don Parker here in in this round? >> I think there are certain positions within certain schemes that you might anticipate a quicker transition, you know, going from college to pro. Uh but I do think it's it's across schemes more than maybe necessarily across positions. You saw Andrew trade out of the third round then back in. Is Is that kind of what he's doing with this trade down to the sixth round? >> Is he going back up or I don't see the logic in that? >> No, I think we just got, you know, a really good offer to to draw it back in five and still pick up a an extra pick, you know, nearby. So 170 and 182. Um with you know feel pretty confident that the same kind of set of players that we would consider there will be available you know a few few slots later.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: "It's where we hoped we'd address"
text: You guys have looked [clears throat] at everything all the entire all the activity you guys have done you know with the roster really before this first two days. How much more better do you feel about where this roster is as you you know kind of take the next step forward? Feel great. Addressing the receiver room and the old line room along with the safety position. Um you know, I think we're as we went into the draft and I think Andrew can speak to this more than I can but uh it's where we hoped we would head where we would address. Is Austin Barber a tackle or could he move inside? See him as a tackle to start obviously has some flex we think could move inside. Talk about you know back-to-back receivers in the first and second round that's doesn't happen often so what is your reaction to get those two guys? Well, they compliments if you take Denzel after Casey I think he compliments Casey. He's a different body type than what we have. Uh we were looking at uh someone we thought could be a size match-up and especially in the red zone which we did not have. So loved his competitive spirit uh I just talking about Denzel now spoke with Jed Fisch his head coach at Washington who I've got a ton of respect for been in the NFL and and raved about Denzel. Loves to practice competitive a lot of fight in him has come a long way as a player and uh is only going to continue to get better and we certainly needed to to continue to upgrade that position and we did. Feeling coming out you know I know you guys gained this house feeling Andrew and Matt but like to come out of this draft with four players in the first two nights that a lot of folks had first round grades on. Well I mean ultimately now whether we take him in the first round second round third round wherever their grades are now it's up to us as a coaching staff to develop them and that's why we're hired that's why coaches are hired as to develop the players that show up in your locker room. And uh you know, you're always trying to maximize a player's measurable skill set and that's what we're that's what we're going to fight like hell to do. Still kind of a hole in the middle of your offensive line I know a lot of you think he can go there but how much discussion in the draft room has there been about the center position? There has been and um there's a possibility we'll still address that as we get further into the draft. Everybody's tired I get it I'm tired too. I know you talked about Denzel's red zone ability how important was it to have two receivers that have like a complimentary skill sets to do what you want to do offensively? Probably more important than usual just to the makeup of our receiver room as it sits right now would not have been as big a deal um if you would have had some bigger body types but you when you look at some of the body types we have when we take the field every day we certainly needed to um certainly get bigger we certainly needed to add um some size to that room and uh you know, Denzel provided that for us. You got a question for the Andrew but kind of unusual to trade out of the round and then to come back in with Austin and Matt. It was a lot of fun. I mean it was a heck of a ride. I was just in there for the ride so it was pretty cool. You talking about are you talking about Barber? Yeah. No, I mean we really liked him from the jump. Um you don't know how the board again Andrew can answer this you don't know in my limited experience of of this you don't know how it's going to go there's certain players that are picked higher than you would have thought and there's others that are a little bit lower certainly we knew we had to address uh the offensive line. And so you know, as it as as he was still up on the board I think the opportunity to move back and then as it as it continued then let's not wait any longer let's go up and get him and we're fired up to get him. When you look at the competition now in the receiver room what what do you see in total there? Well, I just think you have to keep adding to the room as best you can you're trying to raise the floor mean ultimately at any position group you start by raising the floor and developing who you have and that started this past week so it just turned out the way the draft unfolded and Andrew again can speak to this that when we got to you know, the spot that we had at seven would be actually 39 but today seven we did have opportunities and Andrew will speak to it to move back but we really thought at that pick take Denzel. How do you feel with the guys that you added with the guys you had with Gerald do you feel pretty good about the potential explosiveness of your offense? I feel better. You mentioned safety being something you guys are obviously looking at on the other side of things just what what strikes you and stands out about Emmanuel Moseley Warren and what do you like with with what he brings to the table? length speed tough. That's it. I mean he's got great length excellent speed and he'll hit that guy to you I mean that's three pretty good characteristics of a safety. Yes yesterday so I asked you guys today were you kind of surprised in how the board fell today in getting Denzel with a first round grade? Uh surprised to I would not say that I I would not say that. Of of the picks I would not say uh that I was surprised especially on the offensive guys. If you asked me where those picks went uh I would have said it was you know pretty close to where we kind of had targeted where we thought they they would be available. Again Andrew can speak to that I'm speaking for me. You know, in terms of where I would have thought cuz I did evaluate all those players and I would have said that was about right and the board actually played out that way. How much more fun is it doing this if fun's the right word doing this as a head coach instead of offensive coordinator? I have one more level of input I guess as opposed to a step down you know, from the head coach end of the OC but um ultimately it's more fun cuz um you know, when you're an offensive coordinator you're really not responsible for winning you're responsible for scoring. And when you're the head coach we're responsible for winning so I certainly want to score but uh more importantly we got to win football games and so when it came down you know, when you're talking about defensive players I'm all for great defensive players going to help us win ultimately that's our job as an organization the head coach is to do everything in our power to put a roster together gives us a chance to compete every week and ultimately turn this organization into a consistent winning one. Mentioned how your messaging about what type of players you want is really direct and you get the idea of what you're looking for. Do you feel like you've been listened to is this is the type of player I want to do I want to run my offense? Not really I mean it it doesn't really work that way. It really there are pieces like that I I take that back. I there are elements of what you may need from a What type of tight end for instance do you want a full back? You're going to be an 11 personnel team so personnel wise much more than maybe the player cuz I don't think the the parts that make a player how they're wired their toughness mental toughness you know, their self-awareness do they love to practice do they love football? I think that's from the jump that's who you want to surround yourself with. So but maybe a little bit in terms of how you see usage of a player it does you no good to take a player without a plan for them. And I think we all saw Casey the same way how we could utilize him. I think we all saw it the same way in terms of Denzel. I think you know, when you talk about the offensive lineman you're just trying to get some guys that you think um can play tackle but also have position flex. I think that's the best way to go about it. Speaking of fullbacks do do you and your staff still consider Adrian Colbert a viable fullback or tight end? Well, it's funny the first time I saw him I'm like you're the fullback here right? You know, and he looked at me like you know, no I'm a defensive tackle. So that didn't go over great the first conversation I had with him. I'm joking he was he was fine but ultimately you know, he's going to want to play defensive tackle first but he's certainly um showed some promise in the backfield and obviously has the toughness and the want to and you can see that on special teams he played on special teams you could see him on kickoff. So I do think that is an option as we move forward but again I think depending on how much you're going to use that position, which will as we go along, we'll find out. It's hard if you're going to be a 21 personnel team to have a part-time fullback. So, you're we're going to have to make that decision. Is it is it situationally is it situation only? You know, or you're only talking about a little piece, maybe goal line short yardage, or is it more than that? Is it a normal rundown piece? And if it is, then we're going to need more than a part-time fullback. Did you get a chance to watch the last two um practice Go. Go ahead. We didn't get to watch the last two practices of mini camp, just the first one, obviously. Um so, can I mean, can you kind of share how how did Deshaun and and Shedeur and and Dylan look in getting Now you got all We just couldn't get past the draft and get right on to to back the quarterback. Everybody got some Miles questions too while we're at it. I mean, hell. Um uh we're just, you know, here at night. Um first off, I'll address the question. First of all, it was awesome. 3 days, the weather was unbelievable to get out on the grass and pump the music and get fired up being together, and the neighbors complained, and we didn't care, and we pumped up the music louder. If they don't like it, they can move. And so, we I didn't care. And it was like, you know, being out there with the guys and just getting a little bit of a feel for who we have uh on our roster and I thought all three quarterbacks at times you could see you know, the positives in their game. And learning the new system, and they've been awesome in the meeting rooms and and on the field, and uh it was just kind of dipping our toe in the water, but I thought you know, Deshaun looked really good at times, and there's other things he's got to work on. Same with Shedeur and uh with Dylan. So, I didn't really didn't do a deep dive into all of them, but it was a heck of a lot of fun being out there, I can tell you that. Upstairs, sitting next to Andrew in the room. Um you know, you know, what's that been like for you as a head coach? And you you and Andrew are, you know, find yourselves thinking alike as as the board comes together as you're sitting next to each other? Well, I think we see players the same way in their value. How they're wired. That part of it is for sure. Other than that, I just have a small like picture of each player. I certainly don't have the picture of every single player that they do, that they've spent years, at least 1 year, and probably more than that on a player. So, what I do know is the players that I did look at, and I listen to the scouts, and we all talk about how they're wired, and do we want them representing the Cleveland Browns? Is that who we want? And we've got a great group. We're just continually trying to raise the floor, I've been thoroughly impressed with the process of Andrew and his staff, I can see how the picks came to fruition last year with the talent that we have, and I I feel really good about what we're adding at this point. When it comes to Emmanuel, did you really want to play a bunch of three safety packages? Not really going to get into what we're going to do um considering we won't have film yet for our first game. So, we're just fired up to have him. To go back to the receivers, I know when we first talked about your offense and this offense's identity, talked about scoring being the most paramount thing. Like, do you feel good about the different ways those guys can score effectively at it so far? I do. Um again, like I said, I think they complement each other. I think it started with we had to address the offensive line. I mean, that's you know, in both areas. That's, you know, the receiver position and and the offensive line, and I really feel good about you know, where we're at at this point. Good. Last one, Andrew, and that is uh you know, in getting your evaluation of how the quarterbacks looked, there are still plenty left on the board on the final day of the draft. Do you Andrew has talked about it's wholly realistic you guys could add another quarterback to the room. Would you be kind of excited to do that? And do you see are there some guys that you like from the quarterback position? We'll see how it plays out. I don't think there's any position that is off the board that we wouldn't take. Even after taking two receivers, I've we might have taken a third. We might take another offensive lineman. Um could be a quarterback. I don't think there's any position when I left the you know, the draft room that that I didn't see anything that wouldn't, you know, that wouldn't interest us at any

title: Andrew Berry Press Conference: "A lot of action, a lot of movement"
text: We're uh we're excited about today. Um you know, not just with the players that we added, the three guys that we added, but um also how we were able to add to our um our resource base uh in 27 um and then how we're positioned for for tomorrow afternoon. Um you know, with several other day three picks. So, uh obviously a lot of action, a lot of movement um you know, throughout the evening tonight, but we're pleased with where we ended up. And so with that, I'll open up with questions. >> And I'm sure you didn't come into thinking you'd make this many trades, but when you get a sense that it could be just that kind of night for you. >> It's usually just based on the action that you get or how the board falls. Um, I'll be honest, Dan, like we're pretty like we try to stay pretty nimble and flexible just because you never know, you know, when the next opportunity is going to come up. I think that's actually one of the benefits of having volume and quality with your picks because there are more opportunities to maneuver up and down the board. That being said, were you surprised with some of the guys that fell in your lap like Denzel Mos to begin with? They were first round projections. >> I was probably most surprised with Eman. Um, you know, we figured that Denzel could go anywhere from late one to to early two just to be truthful. Um, but Eman, he wasn't someone that we anticipated being, you know, being there as late as he was. So, um, when he got within striking distance, you know, we felt the move was appropriate. You know, to be truthful, he was in play for us at 39. um look at what you did with your wide receiver room. Can you sort of talk about what you have globally from your pass catching core right now and how this might impact like a Jerry Judy or or anybody like that? >> Zero impact on Jerry. He's our bellcow. Um we feel like we have a nice uh I think with receiver rooms you can have, you know, maybe a ball dominant player or you can essentially build a basketball team, you know, with different skill sets. Um you know, we prefer the the second approach. Now, don't get me wrong, I'll take Calvin Johnson if he's if he's out there, but um we feel like we have a nice, you know, well-rounded room with speed, rack, um contested catch ability, separation. Um so, we're we're really pleased with um you know, the youth and talent in that group. >> On that on that trade, >> uh for Emanuel, do you get a sense that another team is going to take or when do you know when to pull the trigger on that? So there they're there they're there probably two separate situations, Jeff. Um one is when you and one is when you do have maybe an inkling that you know you're going into a a stretch where um you and a player or a group of players you know will be target for several teams and you're trying to get ahead of it. Another may just be um and I would put like the Emanuel trade and then what we did for J in 2021 in this bucket where you have a player that you just didn't expect to be in a certain range of the draft and there's a certain level of like okay you don't necessarily have a a team identified that's going to take that player off the board but you look at your resources and say hey this is a price that I'm I'm willing to pay for this skill set for this guy um relative to what you think you're getting. I'll go here and then I'll go Ashley. Y >> you talked last week before the draft just about that positionless defense. Um where does where does a player like Emanuel Warren sort of fit into to that that idea as you think about what you got in him as a player? >> Yeah. Well, I Emanuel is incredibly versatile and and you know, we're um realistic that you're not going to put everything on his plate his rookie year. Um, but I think you really started seeing this with the safety positions, certainly with what Baltimore did with Kyle Hamilton a couple years ago. Um, you look across the league and you see uh just the increase of three safety packages. You look at what um you know, Emani, Nick Mory did for for Seattle this past year and it just gives you a lot of flexibility where you have safeties that can play deep, they can play in the box, they can live in the linebacker world, they can live in the the the nickel world and um they just give a lot of flexibility for a creative coordinator. >> Remember last year after you guys drafted Carson, you talked about the importance of taking an off ball linebacker that high because you hadn't made a major investment there since like four years prior. Was was there any similar thinking with Emanuel like you hadn't taken a safety that high since Grant like six years ago. >> No, it it really wasn't because you know Grant and Ronnie we obviously like those guys a lot. Um you know Grant we I mean we took him my first draft. We extended them. Um you know Rocket he's outperformed how we acquired him signing him as an undrafted free agent. um Emanuel, it was I mean it we just viewed it as a fantastic opportunity and someone who could you know not only just from a pure talent standpoint improve the room but could also complement our existing core there. Andrew, >> um uh you spoke back in January about dedicating a lot of resources to remaking this offense >> with one day still left in the draft. Do you where do you how do you how do you feel about the process you've done in terms of that remodeling? >> Uh I think we're excited about the players that we've added. Um we're certainly excited to see them on the grass because we haven't seen them as a collective unit. Um, you know, but we still have we still have work to do on both sides of the ball and and and tomorrow will be a big day for that, but um, you know, so will, you know, really made to the cut down period because there are still some um important roles that we'd like to add competition to. >> You said you don't want to put too much on Emanuel's plate too soon. Do you see him initially as kind of a ballhawk free safety? >> I think that remains to be seen, uh, Tony. Um, and and honestly like that determination will be by, you know, Monk, Rudy, Ephraim. Um, yeah, I I it's it's probably hard for me to answer that till he's like in our building until we get him up in up and running. Um, but, you know, we'll we'll crawl, walk, run. Andrew, I know you have to stay flexible during the draft, but did you anticipate a scenario where you might take two receivers either back to back or whatever early on in this draft? And does it feel like like a departure because you really hadn't done that in your previous drafts there taking receiver high? Scott, we did um we did have scenarios where because of the strength of the receiver class and the depth of it that we thought we could take um you know two receivers relatively high definitely doesn't feel like a departure. It's maybe a little bit you know what I mentioned to Fred earlier where I think if you look at the past couple years you know we had we had Jarvis and Odell um you know we traded for Amari who was a Pro Bowl receiver for us and then you know had him on a big money extension. We then traded Jerry for Jerry who was a Pro Bowl receiver for us. Um and then like I was actually even thinking um and this this one didn't maybe work out quite as cleanly but even the years where we were short first round picks you know one of those trades was for Elijah Moore and then you know trading down from two for Elijah Moore and then uh taking set in three. So there's no philosophical thing there. It's obviously easier to to maybe dictate the room a little bit more when you have your full slate of resources. >> I was just asking thought about how the quarterbacks looked on the last two days of mini camp because we didn't get to see any of that. Um, so just wondering how comfortable are you with the quarterback room right now and what are you still thinking that it's wholly realistic to possibly add somebody to the room on the third day of the draft? >> Yeah, we'll always add talent at the most important position. That's that's that's, you know, I guess full stop. Doesn't matter who's in the room. If there's a quarterback that we'll like that's available to us at the right cost, um, we'll add that player. Um, you know, that being said, the three guys have done a really nice job so far this spring. You know, we're lucky that we got three days on the grass. Um, you know, they all are are learning the offense quickly. Um, you know, working through their mistakes, throwing the ball, throwing the ball well. Um, but, you know, that wouldn't that wouldn't um, you know, prevent us from adding a player that we like tomorrow. >> You were gaming all this stuff out. Was there a scenario where you had your first four picks, all this Cleveland Browns? title: Catherine Hickman Press Conference: "We're adding playmakers at every position"
text: When did this this last trade sort of I mean how far out did could you guys sort of start talking with the 49ers about you know hey this you know this possibility >> um the way Andrew operates in those situation is we we start pretty early at a variety of of possibilities and at some point he's like hey from this pick down let's start making calls let's start checking in um to kind of see what's out there and then as you get closer to the pick things warmed up with San Francisco and he was able to to close the deal and um allow us to pick a really good player in person. >> I think I think this is only the third time that Andrew has traded up to select a player, you know, he's usually going to trade back and collect assets. What is it about Emanuel's um skill set that made it so appealing and I know he even mentioned a week ago about positionless hybrid defenders and those big nickel packages? >> Yeah, I think it in this case like we're trying to build a team here. Um, it's not just always about adding assets or collecting picks. Um, when there's a player that's still on your board that's falling to you that you have, you know, really high grades on both as a person, as a player, um, it becomes a no-brainer when when you have an opportunity. Yeah, we really see him as a versatile player that's going to be able to play at a variety of spots for us. Uh to what you just said, Ball Hawk is definitely in in the description. Um and really just someone that with his size, his athleticism, the way he moves for his size. Um I was down at his pro day and uh it's pretty impressive. So I think really someone that's going to be able to give us options. >> Other than his pro day, what were the interactions with Amino through this? He was here too for uh for a top 30 visit. Uh just a really mature, impressive young man. Talked about uh when we met, he talked about his journey. Um not having a lot of offers coming out of high school going to Jo and then how he felt uh the connection the chemist the chemistry sorry at Toledo when he went there. They offered him he committed on the spot. Um and then he had offers to transfer uh decided to stay which as you guys all know it's almost I think a something pretty rare nowadays. Um just was really loyal to the school that gave him a chance and he wanted to um do the best he could there and he did that. So really we're welcoming someone that's going to really add to our culture um and someone that's extremely extremely um mature and wellrounded. Yeah, I know you guys game g game try and game everything out, you know, going into the draft, but considering the four players that you were able to end up with, uh it almost feels like you couldn't have game that out if you if you tried. Just what how pleasant of a surprise was it for you guys to be able to, you know, get these four players and um you know, economize your your picks while doing it? Yeah, I think uh to your point there's a in the draft there's a mix of skill and luck and I think we're um some of this is coming together this year in terms of how the plays how the picks sorry have played out and we've just been able to acquire some really good players at every spot so far. Um and again that will be additive both on and off the field. Kevin, you now have four picks in the fifth round. I believe first year you guys have had multiple picks in the fifth round. Does Andrew consider that some kind of magic route or something or what? Just coincidence. You guys keep collecting fish? >> Uh definitely no magic, but I'd say like those assets can be valuable whether that's for um coming back up, packing packaging them to come back up. Um those are we really can use them in a variety of ways. Um and and if not, make the picks. Uh there's some good players that come out of the fifth round as well, and that can be great additions for our team. So, at this point, uh we just want to continue to improve our team and and get the best players we can. >> Just from a skill set standpoint, uh can you just kind of run through what is so special about Emanuel? >> I think what's so special about Emanuel is the versatility that he brings. Um you're thinking of a player that can play high, can play low. um a player that have excellent ball skills, um size, strength, physicality. So really a player that the way we want to play defense just gives our defensive coaches so many options. Um and I think they're going to be extremely I I don't think I know they're going to be extremely pleased to work with him. >> Yeah. Which seems like he's so good at that. Peanut punch in particular and forcing fumbles. Like what do you guys see from him on film with with that aspect? just like the physicality to your point like um two things that Andrew harp on us all the time is to bring guys here in this building that are tough and competitive and he he embodies that uh the way he plays is exactly the type of football um that we want to play and he'll continue to do that here at our level. How important is that versatility when you guys play as much three safety packages as you do? >> I think I think it's huge and again like um the defensive coaches will obviously figure out how to best use them in and in in different scenarios but again I cannot emphasize the versatility versatility point more just in terms of option that it gives to to our coaches to deploy him and maximize his strengths. when you mentioned uh you're almost surprised that he decided to stay at Toledo when he could have gone elsewhere. How do you gauge a a person's players personality when it seems like they'll jump at the uh from year to year at the transfer program? >> Yeah, it's a good question. I think like overall everybody makes their own decision, you know, whether that's that's their own reasons, their personal reasons. So, it's not really a matter of judging whether you're transferring or not. It's more a matter of giving him the credit to staying loyal to the school and really wanted to uh give back to the school that gave him a chance uh when he didn't really have any offers now that he was producing and he could have just uh left. And he said something to me that really stuck out. he said something along the lines of, you know, the long-term financials or the big, you know, uh, financial gains will come when I make it to the NFL. And at every level, it is a projection. Now, maybe easier to make in some programs than others, but that's our job and that's that's what we um spend a ton of time doing watching the tape. Um but at the end of the day, who they play against as a tape, we got to watch and that's our job to project. >> Ander had mentioned that, you know, with that more teams playing three safety, that position is sort of gaining in profile. Is that position becoming more and more important as far as like you know obviously we always talk about edge rushers and corners and things like that but is safety starting to kind of reach that level? >> I think at the end of the day regardless of position of course there's premium premium position and those types of things but at the end of the day like any position that's going to make an impact take the ball away from for us like take it away uh give it back to our offense. Those became playmakers and that's what we're trying to add at every position. Um, and Iman brings that. >> The draft is part skill, part luck. How do you improve the the skill part of it? >> I think it goes back to your process. It goes back to um the the the ton of film that we watch. That's where it starts. Um, and that's years of years of work from our area scouts. That's really like the ground the ground level, the starting point. And then you add all the other piece of information that you gather through your process, whether that's the medical information, your character, your testing numbers, um the interactions you've had with them, what the coaches think of them. And as to me, your process gets better as you get better at aggregating all that information and make good decisions, sound decisions. Um again, good player, good person. Uh those are things we can't miss on. >> This was this was a couple more. This is a player that was projected by many amateurs as a first round pick. Um, do you think he fell farther than you expected or is this the range that you guys projected this player? >> Uh, we're just happy with where we took him. I mean, where he was on our board for us, it was a no-brainer to get up and get him based on what we think he's going to bring bring to our program. So, at that point for us is just really excited about where we got him. >> Still point for a second. How much does experience help just being able to go through multiple drafts and and learn from um how you how you've done in the past? >> I think it's experience. I think it's the team that you have around yourself that you surround yourself with. Andrew has done an excellent job of of having a staff that is um diverse uh in terms of skill experience. I mean just at the table right now upstairs we have uh Tom Telesco and Chris Bolan. Uh you have Jimmy Ray who's done that for decades. So just the level of experience that we have in advising um in advising our decision maker is just is just diverse and excellent. So I think that helps that definitely helps our process and in making good decisions when the time comes. Good.

And then, how do you utilize that player in in, let's say, known passing situations or on third down? Maybe there's another option, or maybe there's a situation that you can create a matchup with that player. So, we've talked extensively that there is a place for that type of player, that body body type in in this system, and we don't want to cast a player aside because he maybe quote-unquote doesn't fit the profile. So, um and I think that's the beauty of our like defense and like DeMeco is constantly looking for ways to evolve, and we're just not so beholden to well, this is the way it was three or four years ago. I mean, our defense has evolved, our team has evolved, and we need to continue to evolve as a team and as an organization. And so, with to your question, I think sometimes it's like, well, does a player like this fit in this front? You know, I mean, the answer is absolutely yes. Okay, Marlon Mack's case because his his tran- maturation, he hadn't played a whole lot of football compared to speak to a kid coming from the US. Is that Does that Did that propose any issues with y'all as far as the amount of football he's been played up until this point? Or are you just looking at the upside of him? Yeah, not necessarily. I mean, you have players with varied backgrounds. You have some players that have been really successful in this league who didn't even play college football. And you know, some people they only played high school football. Marlon at least played, even though he grew up maybe not foot- not going to say football is foreign to him, but he wasn't thinking about playing probably in the NFL when he was growing up in Germany. And then he came to the States, and then his career kind of evolved and grew. And he spent three or four years, however many years it was, at Michigan, which has a good program, and they had a pretty good track record of tight ends over the course of however many last years. I mean, between Schoonmaker, Colson last year, I mean, they've had a of I'd say good players at that position. He played behind some pretty good players. Had his opportunity here this year, took advantage of his opportunity. Um, I'd say they were definitely more of a running offense. So, you know, can he improve and grow? I think he definitely has the mentality and the mindset to take coaching. He understands football. He understands concepts. So, what you're looking is the player have the willingness and the drive to actually work to improve. And I'd say in Marlyn's case, it certainly appears that way. Now, what that actually looks like, we'll find out here as we go. Mention having a couple of deals in place. Were you all trying to move down at that at 59 at that point? We were looking at both. I mean, I think this draft is kind of emblematic of who we are. What we looked up, we had opportunities to go up. I mean, I think we walked in the draft room, I think we put like 10 boxes on the board. Like we had a hey, here's the trade down group. Here's the trade up group. All right, what's real, what's not. I mean, we probably talked, I don't want to say half the league, we probably talked to half the league here, you know, over the course of the day. What's your appetite for moving up? All right, got it. All right, if we want to move up, what would that look like? All right, if we, let's say we don't pick at 38 and we end up moving back, what does that look like? So, and that's kind of how we how we approach it. And you can have it then. I'm just curious if your process is like, you know, when you when you guys have a guy high on your board, but maybe you might I don't know how you guys view other I don't know how you find out what other teams are thinking or what other NFL >> call them and ask them what they're doing, but >> yeah, so like but like how do you how do you you see like a lot of people think this person might be lower, but we have this guy higher. How do you determine whether okay, we want to take a chance here even though other people could believe he might be lower. How do you make that >> Yeah, I think the beauty of all this everybody kind of has their own board. So, you have your grades. You're probably not grading all the players the same way. I think when you go through this third round, I mean, the reality is I mean, they were basically coming out of the woodwork in this past but this last round. So, there's a lot of players that got drafted where you're looking up there going, oh okay, we probably wouldn't have taken that that player. And maybe there's a few players oh, we'd consider him. So, we just kind of go through our process, grade the players, and create kind of categories and buckets of players. All right, if this pick, all right, here's three or four names. All right, we're comfortable picking one of them. All right, if you move back and still get one of them, are we good with that or would we rather move and I'd say in Caden's case, hey, let's move up a little bit because there's a player that we sort of identified. Look, what other teams are going to do like honestly like for somebody to sit here and tell you like yeah, they knew what they were going to do, I mean, they're lying. I I'm not going to tell you that. I mean, you're trying to project to some degree. That's why we go through the pro staff does an incredible job of like looking at team. Hey, here's what we think their needs are. What we think their needs are might be different from what that team's needs or what they think they are. So, look, this is a big puzzle. You're trying to piece it together. There's probably a thousand pieces and there's never one particular piece that ultimately is going to be the deciding factor, the driving force. You guys have moved up twice already in this draft and it's because of the aggressiveness that you you've targeted players that you really like. When it comes to day three, do you feel like that because of you mentioned that picks at 91, they may be the same players that you're targeting around 96. Is it easier or a little bit more challenging to get aggressive for guys on day three? It doesn't change. And again, I'm not trying to minimize like moving, but like moving two spots in our mind is basically nothing. Like we don't view it that way. I think when you start moving eight to 10 spots, that's a little bit more of a probably a calculated move where you're probably going to have to give up a little bit more capital. I would say again, this is just how we view it. You know, moving two spots and repositioning picks, you don't really give anything up other than draft slots. So, again, yeah, we moved up a few spots. Is that us being aggressive? No, I think it's more of us just sort of being strategic about like what we feel like makes the most sense and what we need to do. When you're making a big jump, I would put the, you know, look, I would put the Will move into that was an aggressive move because we moved like a significant amount of spots. Moving two to three spots, it's just more about positioning. That's kind of how we talk about it as a staff. Um, it'll be the same thing tomorrow. So, we're 106, you know, like does it make sense to move a couple spots? Then it's like, all right, how do we reconstitute those picks? So, I think it'll be the same thought process tomorrow as it's been the fact the past few days. You think there's some little difference every day pretty transparent on this one. Did anyone call you about Nico Collins and then was that just something kind of random or not not anything to that? And why would you want to trade Nico Collins if someone did want to call and talk about that hypothetically? Yeah, I mean, look, teams call teams all the time and ask about players. I mean, we're not trading Nico Collins. So, I mean, like whoever reported it or whatever information that they had, I mean, I mean, they could take it and shove it. Like we're not trading Nico. A lot of money. I I obviously, you know, past few years teams have defense have kind of countered the explosive passing attack by playing more two high safety shells and obviously offenses have kind of countered that by trying to run more downhill. So, did did that kind of help in I want to say elevate McDonald's value knowing that how teams want to play now, how deep the deep well, teams want to attack you guys specifically, um, knowing to have a guy like that and um that can I guess, you know, in a sense be so good at stopping the run when teams are trying to play more two high safety looks and have those guys in the middle to be able to counter that. Yeah, I think our mentality on defense is to play fast, violent, and physical. So, who are the players that have those qualities? Then forget about scheme, forget about other teams are doing, start with that premise, fill the players in, and then whoever we play each week, it's going to be the same thing. Like we're going to have to be good in the running game, we're going to minimize big plays, and we're going to have to play well in the red area. And defense is about points and red area is about points. So, it's it's more of the hey, here's what we want our defense to be about. Here are the things that we emphasize. All right, who are those players that actually fit? Like we pride ourselves in being Um, and that's not going to change. I mean, as long as DeMeco's the head coach, as long as we're here running the team, we're going to prioritize toughness and physicality. So, let's find the players that have those attributes. And if you you want to be a big, strong, tough, physical team, you better have big, strong, tough, physical players that enable you to play a certain way cuz in the end, that's what wins in this league. All right. Thank you. Yep. Thanks.

title: Jonathan Greenard on Joining the Philadelphia Eagles
text: How y'all doing? >> Good. How are you, man? Good. >> Jonathan, what was this process like for you? Obviously, there were rumors about you potentially moving. Uh, I know there were some cap issues. You seem to be happy there. Um, how has this whole sort of situation developed for you? >> Yeah. This is one of the best u organizations that I can remember since coming up watching um football knowing, understanding their history behind it. Um and to be a part of organization like this is is uh means a lot to me. >> How is your shoulder? Are you still rehabbing? >> Yeah. Um on a sore plan, but ultimately I feel good. Um, and coming here with the best trainers as well and the best docs here and stuff like that. Um, I mean, if you look at it across the board, man, they got some dogs already. You starting interior wise, you know, um, JMO. Um, and obviously, you know, JC and, you know, JD, they going to do their things. Um, and on the edge guys, man, it's just such a young presence and guys are just relentless. And um and I feel like that's where I can add to is just a vet presence. Um you know, you got Nolan already doing his thing already and and elevating his game to that point. Jix as well. Um you know, AK I already know about him training him before and then Joe coming in as well. All these guys are just hungry. Um and I think that you know adding my little expertise and still bringing my relentless um energy and my effort to the game and polishing up my certain techniques as well cuz I'm still learning too just cuz I'm the vet. I feel like I still got a long way to go as far as um polishing up my technique. But just adding to what is already being put here um is is something I want to bring to the table. I'm not going to change anything up, change anything I do by myself. Um I'm just going to play ball and keep doing what I've been doing since I've been in the league. >> You take pride in that being being the veteran voice in in a room like this? Yeah, I was just talking um Matt earlier um and and just talking about like now as I've always been a younger one in the room uh or always hung around vets uh coming up and to be a vet now it's still kind of like weird to say they call you uncle and I'm like I'm only 28 but um but stuff like that man I take pride in that because ultimately um you're you're working towards something that's bigger than you ultimately you know that this league obviously you got your your short time here or whatever the time period may be um as as many people I can affect um whether it's on the football field or off the football field. Um that that's where I find joy at and you know whenever we're on the same page and we're all you know trending towards that the same goal um that's when I feel like we're at our best. So anywhere I can uh help contribute to that I'm here. >> What's been your impression of Vic Panio so far and how do you view yourself as a fit in in his scheme? >> Yeah. Um, but I know when it is uh drawn up, it's going to be something serious and we're going to be a force to be working with. So, um, anyway I can be disruptive, bring that relentless motor still here and continue to do what I've been doing. Um, I'll fit right in. >> Jonathan, 12 and a half sacks here last year in Houston, 12 sacks your first year in Minnesota, and then three last year. What do you make of your season? I think a lot of stuff goes into that. But um I still feel like I rush well. I still feel like I was still getting back there. I feel like my moves didn't drop off at all. Um I always tell myself, listen, the day somebody got to tell me to get to the quarterback, that's why no need to hang it up. But um outside of that, if my issue was wrapping a guy up, I promise you I'm going be in good spot. So um if anybody want to let a quarterback go free this time, be more than free. >> Well, sorry. you mentioned still wanting to improve parts of your game technique-wise. Where what what's next for you in your mind? >> Yeah. Um elevating that. I feel like as you mentioned before, I'm sorry. Um having 12 and 12 and then obviously I had the down year and that was not to my standard by any means. Um I'm coming for more. Um definitely trying to get back to that point of double digits to where I can affect the game. And obviously it's not necessarily all about me getting back to double digits. I feel like I fit right in with that. Um, I respect the hell out of the the guys that have come before me and all I can do is just continue to just carry that light. Um, and make sure that what they think the things they've done in the past doesn't go in vain. So, um, I love everything about it. I love the historic franchise. Um, I'm want to be a part of that. I want to be a part of having some hardware in my finger. Um but I pride myself on stopping that run so I can get to the opportunity to rest the passer and um that's what that's the main thing I'm trying to get everybody else to do as well. Um and bring to the table as far as the D line to be relentless in all all aspects of the game because um we all the sacks and all look good, but you know, if you're getting the ball ran down your throat, I mean you got to you got to tighten up. How important is the the leadership part of it? How important is that to you bring others up? >> Yeah. Um, just because I was one of those young guys that was kind of, you know, not necessarily nervous to say something, but you know, when you don't make enough plays or you don't, you know, um, have the name at certain times, you feel like you don't have a voice in this league. Just break it down to a different way till we're all on the same page. Um first I've never played in you know Lincoln at all. I've never played in the um stadium at all. I came here for preseason game last year but um I've never played in the um in the stadium.
