Can't wait to get you in the building. Congratulations and uh we we'll see you in a little bit, bro. >> Yes, sir. [music]

title: FIRST Interview as a Giant | Giants Draft J.C. Davis
text: Big Blue, let's welcome JC Davis, offensive lineman out of Illinois, with the sixth round, 192nd pick. JC, when you heard that, what's the first thing that popped up in your head when you heard your name called? I knew I knew coach Harbaugh told me he was going to come get me, so when I got that call, I was super excited. I was ready to go. >> All right, John Harbaugh, man of his word. Let's go even deeper into what that original conversation was like. You know, don't give us anything, we're going to leak to TMZ or anything, but what was what was that conversation like with the Giants and coach Harbaugh? I felt like me and coach Harbaugh, we talked a little ball, but we mostly talked about like a little bit of stuff like outside of the field. Like just just she's trying to see who I was as a person, my character. All right. Well, what what how are you? What how how are you as a person? How are you as a character? I mean, I'm I'm quiet unless you know me. Like but I talk to people, but like other than that, like I'm cool, I'm chill. Like I'm not doing too much extra. I'm just I'm just working. All right, so let's talk some football, man. I always ask guys like what's your why? You know, when we talk about the dog days of camp, things getting things getting hard, what's going to keep JC Davis going? My family. My mom and dad sacrificed so much for me to get to where I'm at right now today. Like it'll be it'll be like a dishonor if I don't put my all into it. Like when I'm feeling when I'm feeling down, fatigue, all of that. You got a quite the journey, man. Like you started as a defensive lineman, you played that throughout the course of high school, then you switch over to O-line at Contra Costa College, and then you master it at Illinois, all Big Ten, you got a high PFF grade. What was the biggest thing or the biggest challenge on that switch? And when we come to putting in our 10,000 hours, like talk about the grind, man. I feel like I always played both sides in high school, so I played offense and defense. So like and I always played like tackle and guard or whatever, so like it wasn't too much of a a challenge for me. I'll just say like going into college and just like learning like cuz I I transferred like two two times cuz I had to go from Juco to New Mexico, New Mexico to Illinois. So I just learning like to uh the new schemes and the new coaches. Like just understanding the coaches' languages and how they how they speak and stuff like that. I can say that. 49 consecutive starts, that's Iron Man status right there right there, bro. Like you're durable. Kind of talk about what that was like. Like to be able to play in 49 straight games and be a guy that your teammates can rely on. Just make sure you take care of your body. Like I feel like that was like the biggest part is taking care of my body, make sure my body is right, my mind is right to play the game. Cuz like if your body your mind not right to play the game, then you're not going to be all in it. So I feel like that was like the big part of my 49 starts. >> you're going to get a chance to to block for Jackson Dart going in his second year. You know Jackson, you what you what do you know about him and how excited are you to to come in the to the facility and meet him for the first time and get after it? >> Oh, I'm I'm I'm super excited to meet him. I've seen some stuff on social media. He seems like a great a great person and a great quarterback you want to block for, you want to play for, put your all in for. So so yeah. Lastly, the fifth pick of the draft, Arvell Reese from The Ohio State University. Can you guys no bad blood now that you guys are on the same team, right? No bad blood at all, nah. We had a we had a good game out there. We was going at it. All right. >> Putting in work. All right, man. Well, congratulations and uh we look forward to getting you in the building here pretty soon, bro. And thank you for having me on, man.

title: Coach John Harbaugh & GM Joe Schoen Post-Draft Press Conference | New York Giants
text: What do you think about the three guys you got today? Uh we're fired up. It's a long wait. You know, that was that was the toughest part waiting so long to to pick again, but you know, Bobby and JC are two guys that we had in on in on visits and we're able to spend considerable amount of time with those guys. You know, I know we talked about the D-tackle position a little bit last night and we're happy to get him in here. You know, big body, long, strong, powerful. Um you know, JC a guy that played you know, left tackle there at Illinois. Um you know, some position flex for him, you know, tackle, guard. Um you know, we see some versatility with him. And then Jack Kelly, you know, another guy we spent down time with down at the All-Star game. Um ran really well, super productive player. You know, he's playing off the ball for for BYU at Weber State. You know, he played off the edge. He's got 30-plus career sacks. So, a lot of versatility in in him and you know, also the ability to play special teams. So, um clear vision for all three of them, you know, to compete for roster spots and um you know, excited to get all three of these guys. That was your final scheduled pick of the draft. What do you make of your year class as a whole? You want to do that one? Yeah, I think I think we got a bunch of giants, you know, a bunch of figuratively and literally. We we've got guys that we really like that are going to make a difference and to to to Joe's point, clear vision probably is a really good way to say it cuz we have a a clear understanding of how each of these guys fits in. You even look at Jack at the end and and compare him to Ar'vell in a sense. You know, the two bookends on the on the class, two linebackers and Jack will be more in the Mike mold, but he'll also he's also a guy that can rush the passer off the edge. You know, if you saw him at Weber State before he transferred. So, we can move guys around and put them in different spots. He'll play special teams. So, got a clear vision for him as well. Also create competition in that linebacker room, which is strong. Um offensive line, defensive line, defensive tackle. You know, I I don't be talking about that. That's still something we got to continue to address. Um we're not finished with that at all, but to be able to add in the draft a guy we really liked. We're a little surprised he was probably still there. He's a guy that we we had hoped would still be there. We had a couple guys and he was still standing, but we we love the way he plays. Uh he plays the way we like to play. If he plays square, he locks out, he sheds blocks. He's a very fundamentally sound guy. So, uh so he'll he'll be a part of it and then we get a couple vets going forward. You mentioned giant bunch of giants figured in in literally. Um when you took even just including free agency, there's a clear difference like the roster, the look of the roster, right? You're you've added size. You wanted seems like you want to be bigger more physical. How much is that something that was your priority and you noticed when you came here? Yeah, definitely a priority. You know, it's it's it's important, you know, and there's nothing to you can be a giant in different kind of ways. You know, you can be real fast and that makes you that makes you a fast giant, I guess, but just really want really good players. We want guys that that fit how we want to play and and some of these guys, they really fit how we want to play. The fact that they're bigger players, longer, you know, heavy-handed type guys is important, you know, because especially in this division, you know, you've got to play that way. Your interior offensive line has to be physical. Look at the defensive tackles in this league, you know, right down the road especially. Um and offensive line the same way, you know, we want to want to be able to handle the offensive lines that we've got to play against up front and of course we talked about stopping the run right out of the gates, right? You you got to be big and strong to do that. You've got to be athletic, you got to be able to move. All those things are part of it, too, but it's a big part of it. Davis will start out where? Swing guard and tackle. Swing guard and tackle. He can play both. That was that was we just had this conversation and that that went a long way kind of in determining where he would play, but very talented, athletic, long-armed guy. Can bend, can move his feet. He's big. Uh he's got he's got some growing to do as a player, some maturing to do as a player, but we had him in for a visit, talked to him about that at length. Very determined guy and he's he's determined to to kind of develop into his talent level. He's a very talented offensive lineman. You guys have both alluded to not being done at defensive tackle. Where where do things stand with DJ Reader? He came in 2 weeks ago. Just how did that visit go and where do you go from there? Yeah, we've been in contact with you know, several agents of veteran defensive tackles. So, you know, we'll we'll continue to keep those communications open. Um you know, we'll see what happens next week. Maybe have a couple more visits with some vet guys. So, certainly on our radar. How satisfied are you with how you helped your quarterback Jackson in with this draft? I feel really good about it. I I feel very strongly that we did. You know, it was definitely a priority to do it, right? Protect him first of all. You know, it's hard to complete passes if you don't have time to throw. And then give him another weapon, you know, and try to give him as many weapons as we can, but to to to get Malachi was was a big plus. You saw him here for the pictures and things like that and you saw he's a good-looking athlete, right? And good good person. Another very determined guy. So, I'd say that was a major priority. And where where are you with Odell? Where is that now? We worked him out. He looked good. We've just got to kind of continue conversations with him. I I really like him. Odell and I are going to talk Tuesday night. Uh kind of see where he's at, see where we're at. Um see what he's thinking, you know, see what we're thinking now with the roster and the way it looks and see if it makes sense. I think if we do anything, you know, just just being honest about it. You know, it has to make sense for the Giants. It has to make sense for him. And he's in a different part place in his career for sure. I think I love about Odell is he's he's right now he's in such a good place in terms of you know, his humility. He wants to be part of a team. He wants to contribute. He wants to help the young guys. That's what he's talking about doing. He still thinks he has he has some juice, you know. And he and he looked good in the workout. So, um you still got to be able to play, you know. It's not going to be the old Odell. You know, it's going to be a different version, the 2.0 Odell, I guess you'd say, but uh we're not decided on that yet. He's not quite decided on that yet. I think we have to just kind of see where we're at this next week. John, you came in here 4 months ago. You didn't really know Joe, his staff, anybody in the building super well, I can imagine. Just [clears throat] as you look back, you went through free agency, the draft, trades, everything. Like how do you feel like this operation has gone? Yeah, that's good. Thanks for asking that. I I I feel great about how it's gone, you know, and starting from the maybe from the ground up, you know, looking at the the staff and the scouts and everything. It's a great group. It's a great group that Joe put together. On the scouting side, I feel like uh I feel like they're they're thorough. Uh they're excellent at what they do. I saw I saw them work. I saw the reports. I saw them through the process even the last 3 days. The communication communication one of the best things that this this scouting department does is communicate with the coaches. The coaches and the scouts are just seamless. We ended up on the same page. We didn't always agree, but we understood where we were coming from and then we had probably the most important thing is to have a clear understanding of when you bring a place. My dad always used to say in recruiting, it's not who you don't get, it's who you get that matters. You know, do you have a clear vision for what they're going to do? Do do you like them as a player? And can you find a place for them and get them ready to play? So, I think we did that, you know, and communication's a big part of that. So, happy with that. Joe and I have been working together every single day. I mean, hours on end. Uh whether it's planning or organizing or or just talking about players or watching tape again over and over again on these guys. And I feel like it's going very well. I I think if you look at the draft and you want to talk about results, yeah, we'll talk about results down the road. We got to find out. We'll see, you know, it's like all these draft classes. You don't know until they get out there and start playing, but uh on the surface right now, I I I feel great about it. I don't feel we could have done any better. I think we made the most of the draft, made the most of the resources we had. And I'm really really happy with the way it went. I hope I hope Joe feels the same. John, does bringing does bringing an overall philosophy to team building into a draft help clarify what direction you want to go in when certain picks come up? Like saying we want to be bigger, we want to be this kind of team. When you're looking at the grades, does that help clarify kind of where you go and what tiebreakers happen when picks come up? Uh it's a fair point. Like I I think it happens through the process. To your point, like we didn't sit there and say, you know, no one said, "Hey, put this is the philosophy, so to speak." That happens in the conversations, you know, so as you start talking about players, you start talking about your roster. You know, back and forth conversation. It just you try to paint a picture, you know, and and it's it's in it's back and forth, okay? You know, what do you see? What are we looking for? What do you see in this player? How does he fit? How does he fit? Because all every player brings something different to the table and you want to you want to have the type of guys that fit how you want to play, but you want to play the the way the way your guys play, too. So, I think it's part of the process. I don't think it's like you're dictating anything really. You're just you're just you you're you're dialoguing about it. And you come to an understanding through that communication. Right? Make sense? Yes. How do you guys approach now the the draft after the draft, the idea of young drafted guys? Where are you [snorts] at roster-wise? John, I don't know your philosophy through the years and Joe, you know, how you guys do it. How do you handle what comes next as far as that goes? Yeah, we've been working on it for weeks. So, you know, again, talking about the communication with the coaching staff and our scouts. Um you know, we've been well ahead of this. You know, a lot of it is um you know, relationship based for some of these kids. So, whether we're sending coaches out, working kids out privately, going to pro days, meeting with them at All-Star games. You know, it's all part of the process from first round to seventh round and then priority free agent. So, um you know, the recruiting process has been ongoing. They're up there meeting now. And then as soon as the draft's over, then you know, we'll attack it. We have a really good plan in place. You know, we've got targeted players. Again, the coaches, the analysts, our scouts, uh coach and I, you know, Don, the entire scouting staff has been working on, you know, a plan for free agency over the last couple of weeks. So, you know, we're ready to go. Have you guys set a fixed number as far as how many guys you can bring in or is it is it flexible? Yeah, yeah, that's a yeah, we've got It's a great question. We've had that conversation. That's a lot today, all right. It's It's It's It's It's a fixed flexible number. Fixed flexible number is a good way to put it. >> We got a number, but you know, it depends on who you can get. >> Yeah. Because and I would I maybe if we're talking about philosophy, I just kind of say this. It's like we're all trying to make the roster better. So, there's guys, but then there's always the ability to to to to turn your roster and you're always going to be looking to improve it. So, just it just depends, you know, you're going to have the best 90 that you can possibly get and you're going to have the best 53 that you can possibly get and you're going to have the best 16 on the practice squad that you can possibly get. And that's all you always got to be working at. John, what was your Two more. What was your opinion on Malik Nabers' opinions on your guys' first round pick? >> Oh, yeah, it's a good question. Now, we had a great conversation with that. Malik came in the next morning, you know, and sat up there and we were talking about it. You know, he he made him he made himself clear. It's like he even said, I if you you go back and you watch it, you know, I appreciated kind of where he was coming from. I mean, you know, it's uh it's uh you're you're you're in a podcast and you're talking ball and he's just like, well, how they going to use the guy, you know, how's he going to play, you know, and you know, I like don't get me wrong. He said, don't get me wrong and I think maybe we got him wrong, you know, it's out there a little bit because that's what's what we do in our in our world. We look at one thing and we say, well, he must be mad about it and it's like he said, man, I just I was curious about how you're going to use him. And then I showed him how we're going to use him, you know, and he's he's he's fired up about it, but I I appreciated it, you know, I one thing that you'll kind of probably see as we go here, you know, we don't get too worried about stuff, you know, it's like as long as long as a person's heart's in the right place, as long as a person really cares, a player, a coach, or anybody, and you really you really want what's best for everybody, you're coming from a good he's got a good heart in a good place, you know, say what you think, you know, put it out there. We we talk all the time about confronting everything that has to do with our football. And so, Malik wants to know how we're going to use our first round pick. I want to show him. I want to explain it to him, you know, and the fact he says it publicly, who cares, you know, I know I know the fans are probably thinking the same thing. So, it was the same question that that everybody's going to have and we knew that, yeah, you know, cuz we we knew that, you know, how kind of Arvell was perceived. So, I think we I know we've got a great vision for him and I think we saw him I I it's just a it's he's a player that fits our structure, our defense very uniquely. And maybe that's hard for people to see, but you'll see it soon enough, you know, and uh and Malik was fired up about it and happy. He was the first guy that met him coming in the building when they when they got in here. He couldn't wait to get out there and just make sure they knew, you know, that Arvell knew and his family knew uh where he was at with it. When you say you showed him that you really like that you like put up tape and showed >> No, no, I explained it to him, yeah. It would have been a good idea to put up some tape. That would have been fun. But uh no, he could understand it, you know, he knows ball. Was it important >> Left, left. You know, the guys came through yesterday, the idea of, you know, Cece said, you know, he met Jackson. We saw the video he was with Jackson. Abdul was here and so Reese. How important was that? Was that organic or did you guys kind of put it out there and say, it'd be good for you guys to come through when these guys are are coming >> Yeah, we have a great young nucleus of guys that love ball and you know, they they showed up on their own. A lot of those guys showed up on their own and we're excited to meet the new prospects and welcome to the organization. So, it was really cool to see those guys come through and and and and meet their new teammates and welcome with open arms.

title: Colton Hood: "I love this franchise and I'm glad to be a part of it" | New York Giants
text: Hey, I might have got some inside info to ask this question here. Uh, what was the hardest thing you did training growing up as a kid? [laughter] >> Uh, probably run run heels. That was pretty hard. My dad used to since I was like 9 years old just used to make us get up at 6:00 in the morning and go run heels. Also, like one time he made us run like 20ome 200s on the track. So, that was pretty hard with steel toe boots. So, yeah, that was pretty hard. When coach Harbaugh was describing you, he used the term pitbull. Like is how much is that where you got it from? >> Yeah. Um, shoot. Yeah, I definitely got it from that for sure. Um, I would say pitbull. Like pit bull is a great word. You know what I'm saying? Pit bull. I would say I'm more like a Kane Corso though. Like, you know what I'm saying? Bigger dog. You know what I'm saying? But yeah, I'm I'm ecstatic with that, you know, uh, comparison for sure. >> Can I ask, do you have a green Corsa? you know? >> No, I don't have any, but I'm I'm planning to get one. You know, my parents don't really like pets, so um I never had one growing up, but you know what I'm saying? If I'm living by myself, you know, I might get a I might get me a Kane Corso for sure. >> What's the last uh 12 or so hours been like for you since you've been dropped? >> Um kind of feels unreal still to this day. Like I'm in the New York Giants facility. Like it's kind of crazy, but um you know, I'm just happy to be here. You know, I'm ready to go to work. Honestly, if we could practice tomorrow, I'll throw my cleat on right now. So, >> what are your strengths as a player? >> My strengths, I would say just my competitive nature, you know. Um, and I would say also like just my press man ability. Um, I don't think there's, you know, too many people in the draft. I mean, not not too many people. There's no one in the draft that's as good as me as when it comes to press. And then, you know, I I just want to continue to build on that and, you know, continue to build on my game, you know, so when the seasons comes, I can, you know, be out be dominant. So, >> how much have they told you about that press man appeal to them and what they're going to do with this defense? Um, yeah, they they've told me that, you know, that was one of the biggest things that they they liked about me. Just told me about told me about, you know, just my technique and, you know, how they like my technique and, you know, not to change it. You know what I'm saying? To come in and continue to work on it and continue to master it. So, >> who have you modeled your game after? Who are some of the players you hooked up to? >> Yeah. Um, so my uncle played um 10 years in the league and, you know, he trained Patrick Peterson when he was with the Arizona Cardinals. So, yeah, Pat P is a big one. and someone I've looked up to since I was 13, 14 years old. Somebody who I always watched. Um I would also say um shoot Passer 10, Dell Rivas, JC Horn, all those guys are, you know, great great um manto man lock down corners and they also get go get the ball. So those are I guess some of the main guys. You >> mentioned Uncle Ro, obviously Coach Aral mentioned you coached him and you told us that, [clears throat] you know, he kind of prepared you what to expect, but what what have you learned from Mr. Uncle Rod just from your development? and just learning about how to be a pro, how to be a football player. >> Yeah, I I I learned everything from him like him and my dad just about football and then my uncle to the more technical side of just playing the position, playing corner. Um he taught me almost everything I know about it. So, you know, definitely um somebody I look up to, somebody who I still go to to this day, you know, if I need any advice about the position. So, >> when did you uh come up with the celebration? >> Uh I came up with it actually in the spur. It was actually in the spur of the moment. So like right right before you know uh my first PU the season I was like you know actually the night before me and my roommate Tyman we were talking about like celebrations we were going to do and I was just trying to think of a s and I was like bro I want to do something that nobody else has done or that you know nobody else is doing you know. So um and in the spur of the moment I thought of that cuz my last name's hood. So and it kind of stuck. So, >> we'll take a few more. Harbaugh said he thinks he would likely [clears throat] fire in the corner. >> How do you balance like being a rookie and assimilating with trying to take a job and and be a leader right away? >> Yeah. Um, honestly, I'm just going to be myself, you know. I'm not going to go in there and try to step on anybody's toes, but I am coming in there to compete, you know, and um, if you know, that's just that's just who I am. That's the type of person I am. But I'm going to be myself. I'm be fine, lighthearted. you know what I'm saying? Not somebody who's always, you know, I guess super serious, but you know, I'm about my business and, you know, I'mma come in there and compete. >> saw a couple times they put the video out of your phone call, you got pretty emotional. Sounded like you were still a little emotional when you talked to us last night. How do you manifest the emotions or at least describe what it's all about? Is it all the same or are there different points where you just feel it coming and say, you know what, let it go? >> Yeah. Um I I like I didn't have a choice of whether I could hold it in or not. I've been holding it in this whole process cuz I mean I've been dreaming about this since I was 6 years old. Like looking at my ceiling dream about playing in NFL and then to get to play for such a story franchise as the Giants and this great city of New York is just you know something that you know I even I couldn't have dreamed of. So, just being able to be here in this moment is, you know, amazing and definitely something that, you know, I'm grateful for and I'm going to uh be appreciative of. >> Are there any are there any wide receivers that you have watched, you know, I'm sure you watch a lot of football and now you're thinking, "Oh, I can get to cover him now." >> Um, yeah. Like, I mean, shoot, I I was um I'm a big football fan, you You know, I'm a big fan of Jamar Chase, big fan of Justin Jefferson, big fan of all the top guys, Jason, Puka, Nakua, all the top guys I'm a big fan of. So, you know, being able to go out there and compete with those guys is definitely a blessing and something that, you know, I'm looking forward to. >> You mentioned story history of the Giants. Is there any players like particularly familiar with or era? >> Yeah, I mean, you want me to name them all? Um, >> Michael Strahan, Eli Manning, Odell Beckham, [snorts] um, Lawrence Taylor, just I mean like there's so many players that, you know, I've come here, did the right thing, and, you know, the city loves them for it. So, um, yeah, I mean, I'm a football guy. Like, I'm big on football. It's all I know. It's all I do. So, um, yeah, I mean, I love this franchise and, you know, I'm glad to be a part of it.

title: Coach John Harbaugh, GM Joe Schoen Discuss Trade Into Round 3 | New York Giants
text: You said you wanted more picks, right? >> Uh we went the other way. We started to watch for No. Uh Malachi Fields is a player that um you know we coveted coming into the draft and as things started to fall and he was still there and you know you know some of the receivers that had win already. um you know, an opportunity to go get him. And you know, we thought the value was we we were fine with the value and the ability to secure the player that we wanted at a position that you know, we wanted to upgrade um you know, not only the the size, length, athleticism, another phenomenal kid that um you know will come in and be be a really good uh addition for us. >> How much? >> You said you were fine with the value, but you've always talked about the 27 draft like it's this all world draft class. Was that a consideration at all? >> Yeah. And you know, we'll see. I know the the comp formula, we'll see if we're able to still get one there. So, I you know, there's there's a chance we could maybe get a a comp formula for a pick for Well. So, you know, you may get one for one there. But, um, as we've seen throughout the draft, we've had opportunities to move back and, you know, fours, five, sixes. If if you want to be, you know, intentional about it, you can certainly do that earlier in the draft, move back a couple spots. So, um, you know, just excited to get the player that we're able to get. How much was this the kind of receiver you were looking for to maybe compliment? You have like Mooney and Slay or kind of vertical stretch receivers and he's obviously a great receiver, not biggest guy in the world. He obviously fits a certain build and mold. Is that how much was that what you were looking for specifically? >> Yeah, certainly a different body type than we currently have. So, yeah, adding that was um you know, something that we we had talked about doing. Uh we weren't going to force it unless you know the value was um at at the right spot. And you know, obviously being 6'4 and a half, you know, 218 lbs and the catch radius, um, and athleticism that he displays was was attractive. All those things were, you know, almost like build the basketball team. We talk about, you know, you got to power forward now. >> What was I think you guys didn't go to the senior bowl, right? You guys were here, but he had like some like standout senior bowl. What was the word from the scouts after that? >> Best receiver down there was was the reports back. Yeah. co coach and I uh were here that week, but you know, we obviously got to go go through the film and watch the one-on- ones and the practices and the games and um you know, he he had a phenomenal week down there for sure. >> Jackson, >> yeah, you can put it in the radius, you know, put it in the area, you know, and he's he's going to come down with a lot of times and you saw that Notre Dame um you know, just again down, you know, a down the field target um that can come down with the ball in contested situations. red zone, you know, big body in the red zone. title: Will Kacmarek meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Hey, Will. Chris Perkins from the South Florida Suns Sentinel. Congratulations. >> Thank you. I appreciate that. >> Hey, tell me about um your value. You know, we know that you are a uh a blocking tight end, but you seem like you have some good hands also. This seems like a good place for you because they want to run the ball. Tell me about your value to the NFL and your value to the Dolphins. Uh what what you think it both are. >> I mean, you kind of hit on it a little bit. Um, I think I'm a dominant uh run blocker. I think I'm a, you know, a dominant uh blocker at the point of attack, but um, I don't think people give me enough credit for my passing ability. Um, I was using an offense with tons of weapons. So, um, opportunities were are limited, but um, whenever I got the ball, like you said, I had sure hands. I caught it and I made the most of it. So, >> and and tell me about uh, attitude. uh you know this this Dolphins regime with John Eric Sullivan the GM and Jeff Heftley the coach they want physicality they want aggression they want to run the ball how do you fit into that mold >> yeah I mean um I think mentality the aggression is you know 90% of the game I think you need to have that to impose your will on you know other players and wear them down throughout the game you're not going to win the game after one play so I think it's important to again wear down players and this is something I've you know had my entire life that mentality Um, I play with a switch, you know, on the field. I mean, you see, you check out the film, that's how I play, but off the field, I feel like I'm a pretty, you know, genuine, you know, guy that doesn't have too too many enemies. So, >> right, cool, man. Thanks. Appreciate it. >> Yeah, absolutely. >> David, >> hey, will David Feronus, also from the South Florida Sun. Congratulations. >> Thank you. >> So, uh, Kaden Proctor, the Dolphins first round pick, said, and I quote, "We're going to run the out of the ball." >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, drafting you in the third seems to fall in line with choosing him in the first. What do you think of the identity this new Dolphins regime is trying to establish with players like yourself and Proctor on the offensive side? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's pretty clear. I mean, like you said, I mean, he's a power powerful run blocker and I think of that of myself. So, you know, you pair us two together, I think we're going to move some, you know, defensive line and I think that's going to be our identity. >> Cool. Awesome. I appreciate it. >> Yep. Isaiah >> going on. Well, Isaiah Smalls from Miami Herald. How are you? >> Good. Pretty good. I'm feeling good right now. So, >> that's what's up. That's what's up. I wanted to ask a little bit about the mentality of of run blocking. I think that takes a special type of person to commit to that, especially in day and age where a lot of tight ends want to catch the ball, go up field, etc., etc., etc. So, just kind of walk me through why you've leaned into uh this this uh run blocking identity. Yeah. Uh, I mean, I played a bunch of sports growing up. Um, I've played against a lot of tough competition. I feel like I just kind of figured out um to be successful, you need that mentality and, you know, not a lot of people like to, you know, go to that, you know, that area. But, I think it's important and could really wear down the opponent. And again, that's something I take pride in and it's something I definitely uh, you know, hang my head on is my mentality. and uh again just imposing imposing you know your will on someone else. >> And then obviously you're part of that team that won the national championship um in 2024. Just what was that experience like and what did you learn that you hope to take to Miami? >> Yeah. No, absolutely. I mean I never thought I would be in that position. Um I started at Ohio and then transferring to Ohio State the first season I went there I won at Natty. So it's just cool how things play out. And then again, just being in this situation right now, I think, you know, I've gone through the levels of football and I just think it's something that, you know, it's just the next level and, you know, I have to adapt to it like any other level, but you know, once you get there, you know, just, you know, take off running with it. >> Cool. Appreciate you. Congratulations. >> Thank you, >> Travis. >> Hey, what's up, Will? Congrats and welcome to Miami, man. >> Thank you. I appreciate it. >> You talked about playing multiple sports a little I saw you were a lacrosse player back in your day. How do you think that helped to translate onto the football field? >> Um, I think just overall footwork. Um, I mean, I'm a, you know, a taller guy and then lacrosse there's not, you know, the biggest guys playing. They're usually quicker guys. I was a defender. So, I think just, um, being able to move with those guys and, you know, stay in front of them. And again, just footwork. And then I think lacrosse is a great game just competitively. I mean, they say it's the fastest game on two feet and um again, just it puts you in a lot of situations to where um it's you versus somebody else and and and then again, just working with the team. So, that footwork comment is interesting because you did so many things in terms of roles as a blocker at Ohio State, whether you were Hback attached to the to the line of scrimmage or out in space. I'm curious with all those different assignments that you got, how did you approach the like preparing for different blocking angles, different assignments, you know, digging out defensive tackles, kicking out the end of the man line of scrimmage. What was your process like for getting ready for all that you did at Ohio State? >> Yeah, I mean, I was fortunate to play with a lot of, uh, um, really good OC's. I mean, uh, two years ago I was with Chip Kelly and he's super creative. So, you never knew what you're going to get at practice the next day. You know, he's putting you in the back field. We got 14 personnel. you got so many different jobs and um it's just cool to be able to um be trusted in those positions. Uh like you said, whether it's in the back field, on the ball, in the hip or you know, split out. So um I think it's just a lot of it is just trust and then um I mean every day of practice we rep everything cuz again you never know what you're going to get. So >> that's awesome. Thanks Will and congrats again man. >> Thanks >> Chris. >> Hey Will. Chris Perkins again. Um, tell me about the challenge of going to Ohio State and at the risk of sounding ridiculous, why? Um, because you could have stayed at Ohio. Was was stepping up in competition a factor? Was NIL a factor? Why why'd you go? >> Um, I think just to where I wanted to go and, you know, reach my maximum potential. I think, um, entering the portal was, you know, best in my favor. Nothing against Ohio. I loved Ohio. I mean, I love all those coaches. You know, I left on good terms, but I think just to where I wanted to go and to be against the best competition, I had to, you know, make that uh make that leap. And uh definitely wasn't easy. It was uh you know, um it was definitely a shot in the dark, but you know, it worked out. There was a spot open at Ohio State with um you know, Cade leaving, Kate Stover. So, filling that role and then you know, just proving to the team that I'm meant to be there and then just running with the opportunity. It was kind of my mentality. And you got to have a a good amount of confidence in yourself, right? Ohio State, I mean, they could bring in a fivestar, they could get another guy out of the transfer portal, right? You have to be confident to go to Ohio State. Yeah. Yeah. >> And I feel like my entire life I've always been in these situations to where like I mean I was a twoar DN coming out of high school and then was fortunate to play at Ohio and then again fortunate to play at Ohio State. So, I think just, you know, getting to the level at each level is um something, you know, I do. And I think again, I'm a good fit for the Dolphins. >> All right. Thanks. Congratulations again. >> David. >> Hey, Will. David again. Yeah, you mentioned being a good fit for the Dolphins. Uh the past four seasons under Mike McDaniel, they ran a lot of outside zone. Uh some continuity on the offensive side with Bobby Slowick still being on the staff now as OC. So, uh, how much do you enjoy outside zone, the that blocking scheme, and, um, you just how do you think you you, uh, perform in that setting? >> No, I love it. Uh, we got into that a lot, um, throughout the season last year. Um, I was on front side a lot and I feel like I really figured out, you know, the different combinations and different looks and what to expect. And that's something I'm definitely comfortable with. Um, ran a lot of counter. So again, I mentioned, you know, playing different positions, playing off the ball again, front side. Um, just being to do all that and being trust at the point of attack is, you know, something I feel confident in.

God. >> Cool. Appreciate it. Congratulations, >> Chris. >> Yep. >> Hey, uh Chris Perkins from the South. We got two Chrises here. How you doing? >> I'm doing good. How are you? >> I'm good. I'm good. Those guys all got pretty big muscles. >> H how are you able to leverage your physical strength? How do you think that helps you? >> Uh I feel like, you know, it helped me a lot in my game. So, yeah. >> What's your uh what what's the um workout or exercise that you you think you're most impressive at? Like, what do your teammates go, man, that's pretty good. >> Uh I would say before I got here, I would say my my uh back squatting. I was pretty good at that, you know, and I squatted, you know, a lot. Uh I don't put no number on it, but you know, I was good at uh power cleaning. I would say uh invention too. Um I was just kind of know doing you know Louisville you know staff workout. So yeah. >> All right. Congratulations. >> Hey >> Travis. >> Hey Travis. Congratulations and welcome to Miami. Man, I wanted to first start by asking about the call and the moment you found out you were going to the NFL. Just talk about the emotions that you felt last night when you got the call. >> Man, it was it was so many emotions, man. just just seeing, you know, me uh drop down the board, it it hurt, but uh I know um I play better with a chip on my shoulder. So, you know, uh God did that for a reason. And um you know, uh it would happen, but um when I got that phone call, it was it was it was a crazy moment like you know, it it felt unreal. Um so my phone was ringing and um I had it face down and one of my friends was like, "Somebody calling your phone." And I thought it was a joke. And then I answered the phone and I heard uh the gym talking and you know it was just emotional just to uh see you know me uh get drafted. You know I'm from Yu City. It's a small town and you know uh not a lot of people come out of there. So for me to be one of the guys that you know came out of is it's a special it was special moment for me. >> Yeah that's great to hear. I also you talked about your route running and the the way you felt you you know produced in that area. I was reading about you that your drop number increased every year at Louisville. your route tree increased there. So yeah. >> Isaiah going on, Chris. Uh, I echo everyone's congratulations and welcome to the city, man. Thank you. >> Um, I wanted to ask about something you just mentioned. And, um, those guys just, you know, shape me into who I am. You know, I feel like, you know, they shaped me into a man. >> That's what's up. That's what's up. Uh, the Dolphins have a big need at receiver. I know you're excited just to be drafted um regardless of where it would be, but kind of talk to me a little bit about the opportunity to be able to contribute um almost from day one or whenever you get healthy. >> Man, it's a blessing, man. It's a blessing, bro. Just to just to be in this in this position is a blessing, man. That's all I can say. >> Cool. Appreciate you, man. >> Thank you, >> Kyle. >> Hey, Chris. Congratulations, man. >> Thank you. I wanted to ask you about uh your wide receivers's coach Dion Branch. Obviously a guy had a lot of success in the league and I was curious what some of the things were that maybe you learned from him about chopping it up about playing wide receiver. >> Uh I would say uh what I learned is first off just how to be a pro, you know, and how to carry myself, you know, on and off the field. Um you know, I feel like he played a big part of me, you know, growing into this mature person that I am now. Uh it was just the things he said I had the on the field things. It was just a thing things that you know I could uh you know be better at like building a routine or you know my eating habits and things like that when I was at Louisville and I was I learned so much you know you know I put so much in my game just off having him for one season. It it made my game elevate so much more. So u it was a blessing to have Dion Branch and when I found out he was going to be my coach my senior year that's all I need to know to stay. How how different was that relationship when he was director of player development versus when he came over and coached you for wide receivers? >> Yeah, so Dion always been like a on on the um coaching st on the uh staff, but uh it was just uh more of so you know we could you know connect more and we spent more time and stuff like that together. So he we always had that uncle and um nephew relationship, but uh it's just that when he became my position coach, you know, we we we spent more time together. >> Appreciate it. Hal. >> Hi, Chris. Welcome to South Florida. >> Thank you. >> Um, I wanted to ask you about your big day against Miami here at Hard Rock Stadium. What was clicking for you that day? And how much of a factor do you think it was in the Dolphins drafting you? Did they bring it up uh in their discussions with you? >> Um, yeah. You know, I feel like, you know, this just uh something that I like to, you know, I like to go up against. You know, when we, you know, we we was ranked low and um I just wanted to prove everybody that I am who I say I am. And um I just wanted to shock, you know, shock the world and and that's what we did as a team. Uh, I just felt like, you know, when I had my guys behind me and, uh, things like that, you know, that was clicking. So, yeah. >> Oh, thank you, >> Isaiah. >> Just one more for me, Isaiah Smalls, Miami Herald. Uh, you talked about, you know, being a receiver that kind of feels like he was overlooked in the process because of, you know, obviously the injury, right? Um, I know Almanra, I believe, has like the list of receivers taken before him. I I don't I'm curious, are you gonna go to that extreme, but just like how do you plan to, I guess, stay motivated knowing that like you probably should have been drafted higher? >> Because I know uh I've been having, you know, this uh this ranking on um on front of my home screen since uh this this this pre-draft started. So, I'm I'm I'm going to show everybody and I'm going prove everybody, you know, like I said, I am who I say I am. >> You you said you have what on your home screen? >> Uh, it's it's like a college ranking of all the receivers. You know, I'm kind of at the bottom of the list. I feel like, you know, that's my motivation every day. I wake up in the morning.
