Um, obviously my family too, but that's kind of what's got me through and got me got me here today. >> Anything else? >> I appreciate I appreciate >> Thank you very much. Nice meeting you. >> Thanks. Appreciate

title: Rob McCartney Highlights The Bucs 2026 Draft Class | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: What's up? Are we good? Are we good? You got rid of that seventh round pick. >> Yeah, thank you. Like no other. >> He's very attentive. I was thinking I'd see you guys in about two or three hours, but now I'm ready to go. Um >> Like no other. No doubt. I got a lot of names in my head from players, uh but also first want to thank everybody like we've made a tradition here recently. So, I'll start with all the college scouts. Tony Hardy, Byron Kiefer, Andy Spier, Brian McLaughlin, Cesar Rivera, Zack Smith, Emmett Clifford, Corey Finney, Jeremiah Bogan, and Jordan Merrell. We got some first-timers in there, too. So, these guys did a great job. Tony Hardy's really answered the bell as our college director for these guys. Um always laugh it's not their Super Bowl. Our Super Bowl is the Super Bowl, but this is a big day for all of us, especially those uh group of college scouts that put a lot of work into this. So, definitely want to take the time to mention them all. Uh Sean Connolly, Donovan Cotton, and Shannon Hogue in our pro department do a tremendous job getting us prepped for all the team needs, chipping in on 30 visits, chipping in um with some of the evals, too. So, shoutout to all them as well. Peyton Roth, our scouting coordinator, Sheldon Quarles, um and then Griffin Moore, our new scouting assistant along with Ty Schiffler. First go-round for those two, they were great. And then just all the travel that we have for all the prospects coming in, our travel throughout the fall, combine travel, Senior Bowl, uh Peyton and Sheldon do a tremendous job with that. Uh Spencer Dill, Joey Larow, and our recent hire Justin in our football IT department. Um and then Zach Beasline who came on with us last year has just been an integral asset to all of us everything that we do. And then real quick, player engagement for all the visits and interviews, Duke, Tyler Massey, Tim, Zach, Miranda in ops for all their help, video guys for all the pro days, all the film, Brett, Matt, RJ, Levi, and Justin, our medical crew, all the doctors who do such a great job giving us all the information we need, including Bobby, Dutchy, John, Sam, and Mel. And then our nutrition staff we're going to add in this year, we had a huge spread upstairs, it was insane, way too much food, but we're all very well fed and now very happy after all those picks. So, thank you to Jess, Pat, and staff as well. And lastly, the people I have spent more time with than my family lately, obviously Jackie Greenie, um shoutout to Greenie, we did two trades this year, he executed zero of them. So, we can hold that over his head a little bit. And then Shane, uh Mike Beel, and then obviously Jason for just uh empowering all of us. He's he's really the best. So, with that, open up for questions. We had four picks, and then we're going to add about 15 guys here in a minute. So, um fired up. Awesome day. So, just on the macro, like the the whole draft, um you you obviously weigh in on this trying to find the best players, right? >> Sure. Um and and obviously you had certain needs that lined up great with Yep. with so many of them being and others. But, >> [snorts] >> it seems like all these guys not coincidentally have a bit of an edge. >> Yeah, for sure. You feel like that was a mission accomplished? And and what how much better did you get in that area this year? >> Yeah, I think obviously it was a point of emphasis for us. It's something we've always talked about, but definitely more of a enhanced focus on that this offseason. Um again, something we've always talked about, but just um it's funny after we drafted Trotter, we're sitting up there and we're talking about teams running the ball against us, just the physicality of having A'Shawn, um having Reuben, and then having Trotter. So, just some of the things that that may limit opposing defenses to be able to do. And then throughout the whole draft, just the energy um and the pride that all these guys really show on the field is, you know, that's really what all the eye in the man stuff starts with. It's a football character thing, but really like when you watch them, you should want to feel their energy, feel their passion for the game. And I think that's something that we always try to knock out of the park, but feel pretty good about that with this class. And to that effect, I mean, you look at these picks, you talk about like Scott today. these guys are are guys that it it seems like you're in a much better position to be able to stop the run, to get back to doing that. I mean, was that something that you guys were really intentional about this draft? >> yeah, I mean, always an emphasis for us. I mean, that's, you know, I think we all believe even though this has become a true passing league, but if you can't stop the run, then you're going to have a long day at the office. So, I think being able to do that, setting up uh you know, more third and longs this year, getting us into more advantageous down and distance to be able to get after the quarterback a little bit and and and in some more different ways. So, but I mean, those guys, I mean, K Scott's a pretty good blitzer, he's a pretty good cover player, too. And um [snorts] I think Key Part's going to be probably a better rusher at this level. Not saying that's the reason we drafted him, but I think we can unleash him a little bit more. Um so, and Trotter's a really good blitzer as well, too. So, I think he's got a lot of assets to him in the pass game as far as coming after the quarterback, too. So, like all those guys for all those reasons. But yeah, I mean, I think we're really excited about the physicality that we've added on all sides of the ball. When you look at the the first-round pick and the second-round pick, that's your top edge rusher Yep. that you needed. And you have a new Mike linebacker. >> Yep. Both these guys are 21 years old. And they could be here for a long time. You know, that's that's what the hope is, right? For you guys to have that two guys come in like that, around the same age, that have a a really long runway to to improve and and help this franchise for a long time. How how how key is that? I know you weren't planning on that, but I mean, but that's what happened. Yeah, I think when we realized, um you know, top of the second round that there was a chance to be able to do that, like the synergy of having a young edge rusher and a young Mike to come in and really kind of become the identity of our defense is really, you know, that's two of the more important spots on defense, and I think we're really excited to have that youth be able to picture those guys, hopefully, you know, it's a year-to-year league, and it's hard to look past those two and three years sometimes, but to be able to say like, "Hey, like we may have these guys for, you know, I think Jason said to one of the guys on the phone, "What are you doing for the next 5 to 10 years?" So, hopefully we're able to, you know, see that through with all of them being in being in Tampa. Rob, is it cool you guys were probably hedging on the older side in free agency. So, it's kind of neat to juxtapose that with at least at the top of the draft a younger group there where you have a little bit of both as the newcomers on this team. Yeah, I think in all those situations, I I mean, it's great now like um you know, but it wasn't like something we were trying to do in free agency. It wasn't something that we had to do during the draft, you know, it really is kind of like the best player, but I think the veterans coming in that have played a lot of winning football, that have been in big playoff games, having that come in, and then kind of molding these younger guys with what we've had in this building, and then with some guys that have played in big games is going to be a cool mix for us. Can you kind of sum up the emotions from the three days, just kind of Friday what the emotions were, then after day two and getting the Trotter and Tampa first, and then today adding these players? What was each emotion like throughout both of the Each emotion? That's a deep question. Um Well, uttering what or reiterating what Jason said the other day, like I've never seen the draft room so excited when we got Payne. Um our scouting staff erupted from the back room. We I was like, "Where are they? Are they out there?" And they were all the way down the hall, and and we could hear them all. So, really cool clip of them coming in, and just that was exciting. That was awesome. Um Uh not a lot of sleep for me last few days. So, how I felt after all the picks, I'm not I'm pretty even-keeled for the most part, but today is definitely my favorite day. Um I love all the opportunities for us to add really good players at all these levels, and I get jacked about free agency. Most guys upstairs are like, "I can't wait to get this over." And I'm like, "No, we're going to get, you know, great chance here to to uh get all these guys." So, um and then try to see if Greg can find all the names by the end of the night is uh one of my favorite hobbies. That's right. So, yeah. So, I mean, just I mean, this is so much fun for us just to be able to um see the fruits of our labor kind of bear out throughout all these rounds, and um yeah, no, it's just it's so much fun for us. It's what we love to do. So, with some of your picks, uh Trotter, Hurst, they play a position, but within the position there are special designations. So, linebacker you have Mike and Will, wide receiver you have X and Z and that. At what point does their positional uh where they would normally fit within that position play into the evaluation versus maybe another player who plays the overarching uh position, but maybe not that role? Yeah, I would say it's probably twofold. Like when you're evaluating the player, it may not come into your actual grade, your actual eval. You're grading them for what you think they can be. If you're trying to differentiate as far as like the value of like the X versus the F or the Z for the receivers, it kind of comes into play like, "How are we going to use that guy?" For a guy like Ted, um you know, we see him more as a outside receiver, but it's hard to say like I think with the offense now, I don't know that we're going to have a true X. You look at some of the history of of this type of offense now we got with Zach, like I don't know if if there's a pure X. So, obviously without, you know, Mike being here, like those guys are really hard to find. So, if you have that guy, it's awesome, but if you don't, I think we got a really cool group of guys. We got some big guys, we got some little guys, we got a bunch of guys that can run routes, and guys that can block. So, I think that's going to come into play for him. >> And then the linebacker stuff has kind of evolved over the years. I think you really got to be able to play they're really almost interchangeable now. You know, we've talked a lot about, you know, the Mike versus the Mo, and really they've they've become a lot of one in the same. Um just depends now on like the passing game, like how you're going to use Trotter versus Angelone versus Roseboom and Bossick. How are you going to use those guys? Like you're going to try to protect certain guys? Are you going to, you know, enhance what they do well? Um and let those guys kind of do what they do best. So, that may be more in like the actual calls and stuff, but that's more of a probably a Todd question on how he's going to do that, but we're excited to, you know, be able to work with those guys. Just part of the thought process with Trotter, maybe just a byproduct, but with with the league, you know, the offense is always trying to stay ahead of the defense, etc., and a couple years ago it was more spread out, right? And you had lighter and lighter linebackers >> Yep. cover. And now with more 12 and 13 personnel, and the running backs have had a little bit of a resurgence here, a renaissance, is that is that more of the thinking to get a bigger 240-lb linebacker that can play a little bit more downhill to at least stay ahead of the curve, or maybe at the curve? Um I think if they're I mean, we always joke like every time we you get with the coaching staff, it's always like, "We want the big, athletic, fast, tough guy." So, I think the emphasis is always on that. And you know, we've made it known that like emphasis was to get bigger, um which, you know, we're not opposed to taking smaller guys. We've obviously had great success with uh some more undersized guys on our defense in the past, but if we think they're able to do all that and they are big, but yeah, I mean there's what nine tight ends that went in the first 2 days I think which was a record, so you're seeing a lot of more 12 and more 13 personnel. Um, but really like you got to be able to play on all three downs and we think those guys can do that regardless of size, but it's definitely added bonus when you can be a little bigger. Robert, at the start of the day today, back to Keionte, I just want to ask you about uh the nickel as an attack piece and what he does specifically in this defense that that suits him well. >> Yeah, I think it shows up you know when we talk about teams we're getting ready for throughout the season, um you know you got all the different variations of nickel, all the different styles and we've obviously been through a lot of nickels here. Um but like for him like he is really really good going forward, going downhill, attacking line of scrimmage, so blitzing, fitting the run, um being able to get bigger running backs on the ground. And then his ability to just kind of defend the perimeter screen game is really good, so he's really disruptive out there. But he was an outside corner at Auburn, so I think there is the ability for him to be able to run cover um and do all that stuff, but I think just to accentuate what he does best, the thing that stands out to me is just the energy that he plays with. All the TFLs, all the sacks, all the pressures. Were you guys a little surprised that he was available there for you guys in the fourth round? Uh I don't know. I mean we're excited. Um so I mean very happy he was there. It's it's always tough to know who's like you always kind of have a feel who you think's going to go where and then there's always a few surprises, but it's it's it's hard to deal in all the hypotheticals of who you think's going to be there, so I know it's probably sounds like cliche, but kind of just stack it and you know if he's a top guy and he fits us then you just pull the name off. With Billy Schrauth, we asked him a little bit about that USC game where >> Yeah. he played through that knee injury, got to the end there. I'm assuming that came up in your conversations with him and to hear him talk about I just want to be out there for my guys. If I'm given the option, there's no option, I'm going to play. How does that play into who you're looking for as a locker room presence and specifically for the offensive line? Sure, I think offensive line is probably the biggest thing. That is probably like you know I think Jason's made comments about like that is that is the one room that is the probably the most important room just for those guys to gel, those guys to be the identity of your football team and um I don't know if the call with him got released yet or if it will get released, but that was definitely one of the cooler ones to just hear like, oh yeah, that guy fits our room. Um and those are the kind of things that definitely stand out. The way he plays too even character aside, like the way he plays is is is is is is what we desire to be. Um you know and the character backs it up as a captain at Notre Dame. He's got the versatility. So he's just he's got the versatility at both guard spots. Do you envision him learning that center spot as well for you? Uh we'll see. Um I think first and foremost guard, but you know it's always something that I know Carbs and those guys are going to want him to work on eventually, so you know I don't know if it when it clicks, if it clicks, but definitely something we would consider. You mentioned there was a run on tight ends Yeah. first two days and increase in 12 and 13 personnel Yeah. and you guys got a tight end with Bauer Sharp. What are some of the things that you really liked about him enough to want to trade up and get him? Sure. And then how does he fit in both as an offensive player, maybe with special teams this year and Well, couldn't wait to come talk to you guys and you guys were excited to get this over with, so that was a part of it too. Who else we got with that seventh round pick? Um really excited about Bauer. Um interesting story, he was a quarterback um and then transitioned out of that role to tight end, did some wildcat stuff which is really cool to see him do. And then the postseason stuff with him was really good. Um our scouts were on him all fall. I didn't get to see him until the East-West game, but he was really good there. I just combine workout was one of the best ones and then it kind of makes you go back and look. Um you guys played tight end for 3 years now, he's been productive there. I think there's a lot of athletic ability um for him to develop in the in the pass game. Um and I think his size, his speed and his toughness is going to help us on special teams too, so guy that played in the bowl game, guy that competed his ass off in the bowl game too. So there's a lot of really good traits to him um as a guy that still has some upside as a guy that's newer to to the tight end position, but I think he's polished enough to be able to come in and and uh help us. Take us to that trade call. How what was that like calling John up >> Well, that was just that was just Jason and Spy. I will say there were some trade offers that came through from the Raiders that were a little sketchy during the week, so we have to try to pull one over on us. We're like, ah we're not doing this, so no I'll I'll definitely all in good fun and you know hope those guys nail their draft, so. Rob, typically you guys in free agency really sign a lot of your own players. That's kind of been the past. This year a different departure for that. You wanted to kind of churn the roster a little bit and you did so. So with these rookies, with a lot of new free agents, it's going to it might take some time for this unit to kind of gel and all that. I know you guys have put a lot of time into getting the right people so they can come in and fit in, but just can you talk about that especially on the defensive side because there are so many different pieces now through the draft and free agency about how you see this all coming together. Yeah, I'll just say we're excited about each of those people, players individually of what they're going to bring to this franchise, so I think you know holding that standard to a pretty high level like that think they're just going to continue to make us better and I don't really see any issues with that kind of gel and I think we're really excited about that especially talking about those first two picks of how they play is really going to stand out. That's probably the quickest way to earn the trust and respect your teammates and >> I think guys like Anzalone and A'Shawn on defense as we've as we've talked about a bunch are going to make sure that standard is up there and obviously we got a pretty high one already from from all of our current guys, so excited to see those guys kind of fit in and you know I think they're going to add energy and add juice to that defense too, so I think it can take us to the next level. Rob, there was some talk before the draft that that uh there might be an NIL impact and that guys with less guys compelled to leave early and guys staying in school that there's less talent in the pool if you will. I mean you guys essentially were done with your draft with 70 picks left. Um did you is that something you could appreciate in terms of the overall depth of the draft? Sure, yeah we had some interesting conversations about um how many guys on our board were going to be there and you know around five, six and seven. Um you know kind of that middle round came off pretty clean, maybe cleaner than it ever than it ever has rounds probably two to five. as I think there's you know and then you get the older prospects at the end and trying to figure out all all those guys, but it's been kind of a cool journey to see like some of these NIL guys that go back or even still you you still have all the all the COVID redshirt years and all the extra years, so you still got some of those guys and you see them go from school to school and kind of really like what makes them go, like why did they get that extra year and what they do with it, so it's been interesting too. I don't think it's been watered down. I think it's just kind of pushed guys to to to a different seasons and uh different draft classes, but um you know really I think that it did come off pretty clean those first few rounds and then it's going to open back up like it always does in terms of these last few and and the free agency. You stated a desire to get bigger which we've heard from Todd and and and yourself and How did that manifest itself? In other words, you know where did it hurt you the lack of size that you had last year and and why why was that a priority? Yeah, I don't know that is even that. I think it's just something that like we were excited about being able to do and making it something that we wanted to do. I don't really have like specific, you know I don't think we weren't small like you know it wasn't you know something that it was just like a desire to be you know bigger on defense. With Gabe Carter, his testing really really impressive. Uh production especially as a pass rusher maybe doesn't match that testing. Um however, I know he played nose quite a bit at Clemson and he even told us he enjoys playing nose. Do you feel like there's this untapped ceiling there if you get him out a little bit further from center? Yeah, and even with him working as the nose I think um you know he's a he's an explosive player. You don't you know like you see glimpses of it and you see him work out and he's a guy that also made you go back and watch. Um you see just his ability to uncoil his hips. He's got really long arms, he's explosive. So with straight ahead power I think similar kind of like A'Shawn and Vita, like he's going to be able to walk you back in the pocket. Um I don't know if moving him farther away from the ball is going to accentuate. I think there's stuff we can do with him to help him. Um but I think one-on-ones that his ability to have power and just have pure knockback was you know one of the better ones in the draft, so I think accentuating that and kind of giving him some options to work off of that is going to is going to help. And then in drafting Demonte, the defensive tackle room was really deep in this offseason adding a couple veterans. Just how much emphasis did you put on you know having that nasty edge, but then going about it by loading up at defensive tackle? Yeah, I think that was that was part of the plan and I think we did pretty good job, but we'll find out here in in the in the fall, but definitely excited about all all those guys we've added. When you when you when you hear like when you kind of go through some of the scouting reports like with Scott and stuff, you know it you see the word nickel and and I I understand he has like a he has a different skill set though than what you have with Jacob Harris who's also competing for a starting job on the outside and and I know these things will work themselves out and and a lot of this is up to the coaching staff, but like how how would he kind of fit and and where is he at in terms of coverage? I know you also mentioned he he played on the outside at Auburn. >> has played outside. I think him playing nickel this year was probably the best thing that's probably happened to him because that is where he's really at his best. Um we had some conversations during draft meetings about him maybe being a safety too, so we'll kind of figure this out as we go here with him, but he was a really good nickel that can play other spots too, so I think one of the things we've all talked about is like we need to add another body to that corner room that we can rely on. Um pretty thin back there admittedly, so but adding him now frees us up to you know bring back the versatility that Parish can play nickel, Parish can play outside, Bemo takes another step this year on the outside and then we kind of feel a lot better about the room adding a guy that can play multiple spots and um you know excited to see what Rashad Johnson can kind of work with those guys too if if if he can uh get him up uh on the perimeter as well. And as far as I mean cuz you mentioned safety as well. I mean is he someone that you would also want to cross train on the outside too or >> Focus on nickel right now and kind of see where it goes with him, but I think that's his best spot, so we're probably going to let him do that, but you know, we'll see. For your depth chart purposes, is is J.J. Roberts more of a safety in your views? Playing some >> I think so, but that's another guy that, you know, you just appreciate the position flex and the ability to play teams, but I think more safety. With Vea, obviously the attention at that position is always going to be on sacks, right? He certainly has done but however that happens, it happens. But this guy, his ability to his physicality and to play the run and be just impactful, how much you know, does that help his overall game? I I know you're elated to get him when you did, but I think in the draft, too, there's a lot of the maybe like designated pass rusher types, and I think to be able to get a guy that you know can do that, and then plays the run at a really high level, and he never likes to come off the field. I think that's another asset, too, is like this guy does not like coming off the field. you know, his ability to, you know, beat up tight ends in the run game is going to be really good, too, so just excited to be able to have a guy that you know is a three-down capable player. As some of the other ones, we're going to rotate on early downs, and they make it targeted in the run game, but excited about you know, him in all phases. We've got we've heard about J.J. Roberts and and obviously David Walker coming back, both of them back, but you also had Jason Jones coming back from injury as well. Just can you talk about your excitement with them and what you kind of saw in him that maybe kept you from going with like maybe a true nose tackle in the development of Carl with him Yeah, like Jason Jones a lot was a guy that shout out to the pro scouts again for digging him out last preseason. He was a guy that we were really excited about. I'm going to throw Elijah Simmons into that, too, was a guy that we're very happy with and think he's got a chance to be a pretty good player for us, too, and then glad to have Nacho back, so I think there's a lot of different body types on the D-line. But they all have that that physicality and that edge that we're that we're looking for, so I don't know that we have a glaring body type or weakness that we need to like address, but I think we're just excited about all the options we have at all those spots right now. How do you feel about the depth that you have right now at outside corner? You mentioned this a few minutes ago about, you know, just needing, you know, healthy, reliable bodies there. We talked about nickel, but but on the outside of the boundary, how do you feel that you guys are right now? I know you you signed a couple guys in free agency, as well. We're always looking. Always looking. Yeah, we added Chase Lucas and Keimond Hall a few weeks ago, too, so good. I mean, excited to have Key. So, very excited to have him, and then excited for Beano in your two, and obviously Paris and Zion, so in a good spot. Couple of things you've mentioned here today is versatility and the pass rush element from basically all of the defensive players, even Keanu Neal and Scott and Josiah Trotter. Speaking to that versatility and hopefully being able to blitz less, which is something Todd has previously said he's looking for, do you feel like that gives you the versatility to allow Winfield to move up and play closer to the line of scrimmage, where he's had some of his best years? That'd be a better question for Todd when we get there, but I, you know, the more we can do with those guys and the more guys we have to be able to pressure the quarterback, the better. Obviously, that'll be the fastest way to start winning down, but that'll probably be more of a question for for him. Okay. Thank you. Appreciate it, guys. Thanks, guys. Good to see you. Thank you.

title: Billy Schrauth on Doing Whatever It Takes to Win | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Billy, how are we doing? >> Doing well. How are you guys doing? >> Excellent. Doing well. Uh, we got some of our local media here. So, if you are all good to go, we are going to go ahead and get started. >> Feel free to roll. >> Whoever's got a question, go ahead. >> Billy, that USC game, um, what I've heard, you suffered that knee injury pretty early in the game and just kept working. Can you talk a little bit about what what went into your decision that, you know, I'm going to continue to play through this? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I think whenever you get the chance and the the medical team, you know, gives you the the option to go back out there, it's, you know, it's not really an option. You you love to go play with those guys. Um, yeah. So, no regrets. You know, I love I love playing the game and I don't take any moment out there for granted. And, you know, having the opportunity to get back out there with my guys was was all I wanted. Billy, Notre Dame is one of the most prestigious programs in all of college football. With that being said, how much did it mean for you to be a team captain? >> Yeah, it was awesome. Uh I love those guys in that locker room, you know, like brothers and, you know, to be uh to be uh you know, thought of as as a leader in in that uh not only my room but in the whole locker room is uh it's a huge honor. really had you talked to the Bucks much in the in the draft process. Is this something you thought might be happening or >> Yeah, you know, talked with them, met with them probably two two or three times, but uh yeah, had a had a decent feeling, but uh you know, I think you never really know until until your phone, uh starts ringing, but uh yeah, super fired up for the opportunity. And what was that moment like when when you looked down and you saw the 813 and you with your family like what what was that moment like? Talk about it. a lot of gratitude, you know, kind of kind of uh you know, it's been it's been a different little journey here the last couple months, but trying to stay in the moment with all of it and uh you know, put my put my foot forward, you know, and uh you know, super fired up to be in in Tampa and and in Florida. You know, I think it's a good fit. It's one thing to block the guy straight across from you, but part of your scouting report is that you have a a high level of awareness to be able to pick up blocks from angles that you know maybe not um predictable. Can you talk a little bit about how you're able to find those loopers, those stuners, the blitzers, and make sure that the pocket stays clean? >> Yeah, I think it's number one playing playing with the guys next to you. Um it's five is one. um everything's got to be done together at the offensive line positions. So, I think that's number one. And then, you know, you got to be prepared. Um you got to kind of see things un unraveling as they're uh um you know, as they're lined up. You can't be can't be late with everything or with anything. Um so, I think those two things, but uh you know, taking care of the guys next to you is huge. Billy, how would you kind of describe your play style, your mentality when you go out on the football field? >> Yeah. Um, you know, love get getting after guys. title: Mike Biehl Reflects on Day 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: A few people stayed up. That's good. Good to see y'all. Fire away. >> Mike, talk about Josiah Troder. What uh would you like about him? Only two year worth of experience. Like he he thought he was ready to come out and we spent a lot of time with him through this process and um his play on the field dictated that too, I think. How much are you influenced by the relationship like with Mike Caldwell and and stuff like that? >> Yeah, I mean I think all that stuff helps, right? Just to try to get to know the player. Um yeah, Mike had a relationship with him. Todd has a relationship with his dad, too. Um you know, and again, we spent a lot of time with him, too, and just came away feeling really comfortable. But I think all that matters, you know, just again trying to find out everything we can about these kids and and uh that played a part in it. the perception is that you guys needed to improve um some of your pass defense inside with with the linebacker position. I know you got picked up some free agents obviously, but like for for Troder seem to be more of a of a run player right now at least, right? >> Yeah. I mean, I I would say that's that's fair, but I also think that he he can play in coverage. I think he's that's a little bit of a misnomer and you know, I don't know if it's the the narrative that the media is putting out, but like he's actually pretty good at it. Now, that being said, he's an old school downhill Mike backer that can play the run, which is hard to find nowadays. I mean, with the college game, the way it's went, it's all lateral and everybody's looking for the speed stuff. And to us, he has enough speed to play in our our league. Um, now, if you said, is he a better run defender than than a pass defender? I would say, yeah, that's probably fair, but we think he has the capability to be a three down linebacker. >> Talk about his blitzing ability in in that matter. >> Yep. And I would say that's that's a big part of his game, too. I mean, he he understands how to rush the passer and and he can go through running back's faces if he chooses to or he can make a miss. So, that's going to be a plus for Todd on third downs. And I mean, you guys have seen the way that he uses our inside backers when Devin was here. And I mean, I would I would anticipate Josiah having a lot of production in that phase >> with with the fact that I mean, he's only had like two years of college ball experience. Would you expect him to kind of grow in in his coverage, in his recognition, and his instincts in that department? >> Yeah, 100%. I mean, all these guys are like, like I said, when I started, we drafted three 21 year olds, and we think the upside with all of them are is is huge. So, um, yeah, but I would say that he also has played the game for a long time and again has been kind of groomed from from a young age. So, he's he's pretty far advanced, I would say, in that in that area. >> I don't know if you could also speak to the the because I I understand he's had a few knee injuries between college. I know in 2023 he had a torn I think it was an ACL and then I think he had like it was an MCL as well or like I mean did you guys feel comfortable? title: Josiah Trotter: “A Tone Setter” | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Josiah, how we doing? Can you hear us? Yep, doing good. How are you? Excellent, doing well. Welcome to Tampa. Uh we got our little here. >> Rick, why don't you go ahead and get us started? Hey Josiah, congratulations. Uh just let me know what interaction you might have had with the Bucks and and just your reaction to coming to Tampa. They're certainly a a franchise that your family's familiar with. Yeah, no doubt. I mean, it was it was a great visit being to meet that staff even at the combine having my visits with them. So, you know, just knowing that coaching staff especially a lot of the guys on the coaching staff who I've known either for a long time or you know, they have known my dad and then especially just I lived in Tampa for a little bit when my dad played for them. So, kind of already knowing about the not only just the culture, but you know, Bucks football and being down there when I was younger. So, you know, I'm just excited to be able to down there and get to work with all those guys, my linebackers coach and just the rest of guys on that roster. Josiah, tell us what you think your strengths are as a linebacker. What do you do best at the position? Yeah, I think without a doubt when it comes to my strengths, that's going to be physicality. I think as that that position, that's a big thing just for me and just how I was brought up. But definitely physicality, my instincts to be able to play my brain, try to put myself ahead of plays and then just being a leader, be able to communicate, be a tone setter. You know, I think I'm going to be a player that's not only just going to be able to just do that, but also be productive out there in all phases of the game and be able to just, you know, be someone that guys can look at and be a alpha, be a leader, be a green dot guy and just be able to look at to be a not only great football player, but a great locker room guy, someone who's going to put the team before himself. Josiah, congratulations. What do you know about What do you know about Todd Bowles' defense? Yeah, they like to blitz, man. They like to blitz to get after it, man. They play some good defense, hard-nosed defense. And just talking to him, man, it's a it's a great scheme, great system to be able to fit in and, you know, they're going to allow you to be able to show and just showcase everything you can do as a linebacker from all over. And I I love that, you know, love what he's been doing down there, man. I've been knowing him for, you know, a long time. Josiah, congratulations. You went to a Clemson camp with Troy Bowles a couple years ago. You also know Mike Caldwell back when your dad played in Philadelphia. Just talk about those unique connections that you have to the franchise. Yeah, yeah, just knowing, you know, Coach Bowles from when I did the camp with his son and just knowing him ever since then just the interactions with him. So, that was great just being when I met him then and um when he just when he knew my dad and Coach Caldwell and his family just just being family friends with them since for so long and knowing them when my dad both of our parents had played together. So, it was really cool just to be able to not only just meet with them, but just to be a full circle moment of just all this time that's passed and just knowing each other not only just long, but you know, finally seeing each other. Josiah, you you played basically 2 years of college football as a starter. Just want to ask you, what what gave you the confidence to to know you could go to the next level and be drafted as high as you were in your and play well as a pro. Yeah, I think for me it was like, you know, when you come to the SEC, I feel like it's the best competition. When you go to the SEC, and I feel like you're able to go dominate, you know, I feel like it's the closest thing next to going to the NFL and I felt ready. I felt ready to go and just I feel like God was leading me in that direction and praying about it and just had blessed opportunity just to be able to come out and, you know, just trusting him and how my process went and I knew I felt like I was ready and capable of just being able to go to that next level just not only play physically, but also mentally. You've been lauded for your run disruption and, you know, run stopping skills as a linebacker. What kind of skills go into helping you do that? And how did you develop those skills and kind of get the instinct for that type of thing in the game? Yeah, no doubt. I mean, a lot of it is just God-given instincts and just talent and ability that he's blessed me with to allow me to be able to use and have my dad in my life, you know, to be able to help me from a young age how to use those things, to grow up and just know how to be a not only professional, but to play this position. There's a lot that comes with it. And a lot of behind the scenes that you got to put into it that a lot of people don't see. So, a lot of that he's built just built up in me just guiding me, showing me. So, um you know, there's a lot there's a lot with it. So, I think my strengths and just everything that comes with it is something that's just been molded and bred into me since I was born. Josiah, Bowles asks a lot of his linebackers coming downhill. Blitzing is something you're really comfortable with. Obviously, you're a beast against the run. But as far as coverage, dropping back, what's your comfortability there? It's something that obviously, you know, it's something you can improve at as as you get into the next level, but what's your comfortability there? Yeah, no doubt. I think, you know, being able to showcase everything and I think when I get within that scheme and coaching staff, I'm very comfortable when it comes to that, you know, coverage and those aspects of whatever they're asking me to do. And at this point in my career being able to touch all those aspects of the coverage or play calling or defensive scheme. So, I think when I be able to go there, man, just the not only coaches I have with me, but being able to showcase you to my game and, you know, not only will they see it, but the whole NFL will see it and I'll be able to show them that not only am I a complete player, but the whole NFL. Josiah, there's not many people that can say they're the son of an NFL linebacker and also the brother of an NFL linebacker. For you, how has that shaped just your football journey growing up and college? Yeah, it shaped me so much from a young age, you know, being able to see my dad as dad and then growing up, you know, learning more about, you know, what that last name meant, you know, having him as, you know, not only as a coach, as a father, but someone that played in NFL at a high level and then a brother that was really good and then ultimately is playing right now in NFL. So, you know, it was a lot of pressure maybe when I was younger, but I learned, you know, you never embrace it, you always be running from it. So, I always learned to embrace it, put a chip on my shoulder. And I think it's also made me into the player I am today cuz they also helped me. They, you know, poured into me, you know, to be able to get to me to this point as well and, you know, just blessed and thankful to God that, you know, not only they're in my life, but, you know, they were positive influence and people I look up to and really lean on not only for advice just for football, but just in life. So, Josiah, you mentioned the, you know, leadership traits that you bring in that linebacker room. The Bucks have just lost a big one in Lavonte David. So, you just kind of to get that linebacker room and and try to make an impact maybe as a leader as well. Yeah, yeah, you know, the Bucks lost a great leader, a guy that, you know, I think should be in the Hall of Fame and someone that I grew up just, you know, watching him, but just really respected his game, the way he played, especially as long as he did. And you know, being able to come in as a young guy and be able to show guys that, you know, I'm ready to go, I'm ready to work, you know, and just be able to come in and be, you know, be myself, be my authentic self, not trying to be, you know, something I'm not and just show that I can be a leader, you know, in my own way and be able to come in, step in and be someone that they look at, you know, even if I'm being, you know, just turned 21 that, you know, I'm a leader, I can vocalize and be I'm going to go out there and make productive plays and be able to look at as a alpha and as a leader, you know, someone that they can trust and respect at the same time ultimately. Josiah, when when you look at current NFL linebackers when you're watching tape, are there guys that that you like, you like to emulate, that have similar body types, strengths, skill sets to what you have? Um yeah, I mean, there's always, you know, my favorite Fred whenever I can catch his games. You know, just watching good linebacker play. Me, I just like seeing good linebacker play, you know, um just across the league. So, I think there's a lot of good linebackers across the league that I get some really good tape, you know, from week to week or just got the season, you know. And but for me, I never really had anybody I really just say, "Hey, I just put my game after him." You know, I think my dad is always number one cuz that's my dad and he played and I'm always going to take a big portion from his game. So, um especially my brother, too. But I think, you know, a lot of things I work on as a player and things I do, um you know, you don't see too often uh especially maybe nowadays. Um so, I'm trying to just bring, you know, not only just physicality back, but bring out not only old school, but new school feel back, bring in that dominant, you know, force and just, you know, when when they see the Bucks defense, you know, I want people to feel that defense, you know, to feel that front seven all around cuz, you know, I don't want it to just be one player. I want it to be the whole defense just be a bunch of dogs out there. What do you know about the Bucks' first round draft pick, Ruben Bain? How excited are you to kind of come in and be part of that rookie class with him? Man, excited. I was uh I was able to talk with him a while back when we were on the same visit together in Cincinnati. Great dude, you know, I know he's fired up. He's got a chip on his shoulder like I got a chip on my shoulder. We're just ready to just go show not only just, you know, Bucks nation, but the NFL, you know, the whole world know what we can do. Um and just, you know, just grateful to for the opportunity to be able to go there and be able to show teams. What did Todd Bowles say if anything about your opportunity? I mean, obviously they're watching you a green dot guy. Is that the kind of role you think you can step in and and handle right away as a as a 21-year-old? Yeah, you know, just talking with Coach Bowles and just, you know, basically let you know, let me know like he you know, obviously, you know, you see they lost Lavonte David and losing a great leader, you know, guy that was a green dot that's been there and played a long time. And that's a role to be able to step in and you know, something they always asked me and that's something I've done since a young age of someone that's called being able to make plays, call plays and everything like that. So, you know, I'm very comfortable being able to do that and being able to step into that role and to, you know, do it, you know, to the best of my ability and knowing that, you know, they I feel like they'd be happy with me being stepping into that position. And being 21 years old after playing two seasons of college football, do you feel like you're scratching the surface of your potential and what you could be? Oh, without a shadow of doubt. I'm only scratching my surface, you know. Um you know, I only played two seasons and was able to play one season with Mizzou just, you know, of just getting there with a different scheme and I'm just scratching the surface and once people find out and then they see what God put on the inside of me or what I can truly do as a all around linebacker, um you know, I mean, I can they overlook, but I I can I can only show you better I can tell you. So, that's all I really tell people, man. I can only show you better I can tell you. So, I'm just going to let time do its thing and when I get there, just put my head down, go grind, get to work and just try to be the best me I can possibly that God made me to be. Josiah, what's your message to Bucks fans who are who are watching this and excited to have you in Tampa? Man, one thing you're going to get a player that's not only just committed and selfless, but is going to be a physical player and that's is to come in and just try to you know bring a Super Bowl. That's my ultimate goal to bring a Super Bowl to Bucks Nation and try to be the best version I can be for not only just Bucks Nation but for my team, my coaches, my family, God and you know, I just want to come in just give you everything I got every single day and try to just come in and be myself, you know, you guys lost a great one. I want to come in and try to be even better than that and exceed that and man, he was a he was a great person just to be able to watch and especially as long as he was there. That's fine. All right. Thank you. >> Congratulations to the Appreciate it. Thank you.
